title: Expose exact merge-candidate lineage and CI freshness in Cara status
description:
Operator-requested observability gap found during Cacophony native merger operation. `cara status` reported the caravan graph and aggregate health, but the merger still had to call GitHub directly to learn each active PR's exact current base/head, synthetic merge-candidate SHA and parents, auto-merge owner, check-run generation, and whether visible required checks belonged to the current candidate or a stale head/base generation.

Concrete evidence: Cacophony PR #1991 was head `affacaba74132a4642c6aa06021bb8fa5e381097` on main `251d04e9be9742cbf9a9d2cfa0a194601e5a2561`, while its failed workflow selected stale synthetic merge ref `ff68423484b0be2ffe0a2dd70999c8d518c0887b` whose second parent was prior head `329c42e2a22db8146dada382811927e38ee80e50`. Cara status showed a healthy six-member graph but not this generation mismatch.

Extend stable JSON/MCP status and show output for each active member with: provider-updated timestamp; exact base ref/OID; exact head ref/OID; current synthetic merge-candidate SHA/tree/parents when available; native auto-merge enabled/method/actor; required check names and latest check/run IDs with head/candidate association; and an explicit fresh/stale/unknown classification. Bound output and preserve secret-free receipts. Acceptance: a merger can prove current PR identity, candidate lineage, sole auto-merge ownership, and check freshness from Cara alone without `gh pr view`, `gh api commits/refs/pull/.../merge`, or direct check-runs calls.

## Additional operator gap: default-branch movement provenance

The operator asked who, besides Cara/caco-merger, was advancing `main` and invalidating the caravan. Cara status exposed only current default-branch OID `251d04e9...`; answering required an external git-history inspection. Extend the same bounded provider snapshot with recent default-branch movements: commit/merge SHA, timestamp, author/provider actor when available, source PR or Cara operation receipt, and an explicit Cara-owned versus external classification. Include previous observed default OID so an agent can distinguish actual main motion from a stale GitHub synthetic merge-ref race. Acceptance: Cara alone can report which actors advanced main since the prior sync and which active caravan candidates became stale as a result.

title: Trust the devshell cara and drop binary-path defensive checks
description:
Operator posture change 2026-07-27. Cara is now pinned solely by flake.lock and obtained from devshells; nix flake update is the upgrade path. Cara Sync CI is disabled; sync is driven manually for now, and later by a caco cron running cara sync with hooks that dispatch pi agents to repair caravans as they break.

Under that model the defensive machinery around binary LOCATION is dead weight and actively obstructive. Remove or scope down:
- is_package_manager_binary and the self_update_package_managed refusal, which today blocks self-update outright whenever the running binary lives in a Nix store or Homebrew cellar. That refusal is what has to go: a store-managed binary is a reason to install ELSEWHERE, not a reason to refuse.
- require_first_path_executable and related PATH-precedence checks that exist to stop self-update writing a binary PATH would not resolve.

Operator correction 2026-07-27: forced self-update REMAINS useful in general, for deliberately pulling a GitHub release regardless of how the current binary was installed. So this bead does NOT supersede caravan/bd-bd58cd or updatable-cli/bd-e195f5; those stay open and are the intended replacement for the removed refusal. The relationship is: drop the blanket refusal here, and let bd-bd58cd own the safe forced path (never write into a Nix store or Homebrew cellar, install into a user-owned directory, and report clearly when the result shadows a package-managed binary).

Keep the runtime provenance surface added for bd-0629ce: version, resolved executable, sha256, and nix_store on every status receipt. That is how a version-skewed actor is proven rather than inferred; today it is the only reason we could tell one node was answering from a stale debug build while its nix profile sat six releases back. Provenance is diagnosis, not defence, and becomes more valuable under manual and cron-driven sync where a skewed actor otherwise looks like a quiet queue.

Also record the doc change: release/backfill recipes and self-update docs should state that flake.lock is the pin of record for this deployment, and that forced self-update is a deliberate override rather than the normal upgrade path.

title: Reject current-main no-op candidates instead of replaying trunk advances onto the caravan tail
description:
Operator-reproduced Cara join bug in `harryaskham/cacophony` on 2026-07-21. Harry was on branch `fix-cara-timeouts` and attempted to join what was an empty/no-op candidate relative to current default branch. Instead of refusing the empty candidate, Cara created PR #2080 and inferred the already-landed default-branch advance as candidate work, rebasing that unrelated release commit onto the active caravan tail.

Exact graph/evidence:

- Active predecessor PR #2079: head `fix-slackiq-nodes` at `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, parent/default fork `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`.
- True GitHub `main` had already advanced from `80bf4eacae` to release commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7` (`release: v1.2.1562`). The authoritative annotated tag v1.2.1562 also peels to `d9fad17e`.
- Cara created PR #2080 with base `fix-slackiq-nodes`, head `fix-cara-timeouts`, initially containing `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680`.
- `ac701198` has parent `c059bf15`, author `Cacophony Daemon`, committer `Caravan`, and exactly the same release message/patch as already-main commit `d9fad17e`; it is the default-branch release change replayed onto the caravan tail.
- PR #2080 body identifies the unrelated update-helper source (`agent/ms-dev-2/.../update-helper`, source head `e3026e0461`, mode `direct`) even though the provider head branch is Harry's `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- PR #2080 was created at 23:06:39Z. The timeline later records a head force-push at 23:08:19Z and Harry's actual `fix cara timeoutes` commit `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633` only afterwards; current PR files therefore mix the unintended release bump with the intended `.caravan/config.yaml` edit.

This proves the join/rebase delta was derived against the stale caravan/root fork (`80bf4eacae`) rather than the live provider default tip (`d9fad17e`) / candidate's intended patch. As a result, a branch with no intended delta from current main can silently acquire every trunk commit landed since the caravan fork, and Cara can force-update an operator branch with unrelated duplicated commits.

Expected contract:

1. Under the join lock, re-read the live provider default tip and candidate head.
2. Compute candidate intent relative to that live default/fork-point contract, not relative to the active predecessor's old main base.
3. If candidate has no delta from live default, refuse with a typed `empty_diff`/no-op result and do not create/reuse a PR, mutate/force-push its head branch, append membership, or schedule CI.
4. If candidate has one real change X atop newer default M1 while the caravan tail descends from older M0, rebase only X onto the locked tail; never replay M0..M1 as candidate work.

Required regression test graph: create M0 and a caravan tail T from M0; advance default to M1; (a) join candidate C=M1 and assert a typed no-op with zero provider/membership mutations; (b) join C=M1+X and assert the joined result is T+X only, with M1's already-main patch excluded. Also assert an unrelated existing/current operator branch name cannot be selected or force-pushed as the head of another source generation.

## Live automatic-admission no-op blocker — Cacophony PR #2104

After first caravan #2111 merged, operator-prioritized exact-clean #2104 became canonical. Sync source analysis proved its sole source commit 27815c9a6f13fb2618b6c0cae83ac1ab52183022 already landed in current main79a9d38; effective patch is empty, mutated=false. Cara returned join_empty_source_noop with wake_class=retry_tick and left the PR open/priority-labelled, so unchanged retries block all later candidates forever.

Extend this bead acceptance: sync-owned admission must classify exact already-landed source as terminal/advisory retirement, not retry. Under exact ancestry/tree proof, remove queue control priority/skip intent as appropriate, emit a typed already_landed/noop receipt, and continue to later candidates in the same bounded tick or provide an explicit safe PR-close/Caco-return continuation. Never replay main or report success as a new caravan. Cover root/tail admission, squash-equivalent distinct OID, mixed source where only some commits landed, and concurrent main movement.

title: Add idempotent Cara repository initialization for required labels
description:
## Operator expectation

While integrating Cara into Cacophony, Harry asked whether first use correctly initializes a repository by creating the `caravan`, `caravan-evicted`, and `caravan-force` labels.

Current behavior does not initialize them. `cara status` can inventory an unlabelled repository, but mutation paths call `require_labels` and fail before provider mutation with `required_labels_missing`, instructing the operator to create all three labels manually and rerun. There is no `cara init` command.

The Cacophony repository currently has all three labels, verified through GitHub, but they were provisioned externally rather than by Cara first-use initialization.

## Acceptance

- Add an explicit, idempotent first-party initialization surface such as `cara init` (CLI/MCP), or an equally clear reviewed first-use path.
- Create exactly the required labels with documented names, descriptions, and colors:
  - `caravan`
  - `caravan-evicted`
  - `caravan-force`
- Preserve compatible existing labels without mutation; fail closed on incompatible definitions unless an explicit repair option is chosen.
- Return stable receipts distinguishing created, already-present, incompatible, and provider-failed labels.
- `cara status` should report repository initialization readiness and the exact next command when labels are missing.
- `new`, `join`, `renew`, and `rejoin` continue to fail before graph mutation if initialization has not completed.
- Add provider fixtures for empty repo, partial labels, compatible existing labels, incompatible metadata, retry after partial provider failure, and idempotent replay.
- Document whether automatic initialization is ever allowed; avoid hidden label mutation from a read-only `status` call.

Filed from the first Cacophony Cara cutover. This belongs in the Caravan project, not Cacophony.

title: Ship a portable Linux release artifact and expose runtime provenance
description: Root cause from the ms-dev-2 update-helper crash (Cacophony evidence, Cara-owned deliverables). The published x86_64-linux release asset is a glibc-dynamic build (ELF ET_DYN, glibc 2.40 loader). On NixOS with nix-ld the loader resolves through glibc 2.42 plus /run/current-system/sw/share/nix-ld/lib, and the same byte-identical binary (sha256 95dd721d9dace6a23ccdde29443a6e3935f8d48ac6a951905752514901d0509a, 14613392 bytes) reproducibly exits 139 with empty stdout and stderr for status/next-candidate/log while --help still works. Signal-exit classification in callers and PATH hygiene on production nodes are Cacophony-owned (their items 2 and 3) but must be cross-referenced. Targets a 0.0.11 release once landed.

description:

title: [broken-on-main] CI gate loses the nix devShell PATH: cargo: command not found
description:
Caravan CI build-test fails on main and on every open PR, 12-13s in, before any compilation:

  bash: line 3: cargo: command not found
  ##[error]Process completed with exit code 127

Observed red on main at 57639f4 (11:50 BST), 137a914 v0.0.12 (11:58) and c30540d (12:29), and on PR #10 twice including an explicit rerun. No repository change correlates with the onset, which points at a profile/image change on the self-hosted nix runner fleet.

Cause: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the gate as

  nix develop --command bash -lc '...'

The -l makes it a LOGIN shell, so the runner's profile files are sourced AFTER nix develop has established the devShell environment, and they replace PATH rather than extend it. cargo, rustc, clippy and rustfmt disappear even though flake.nix devShells.default still provides all of them. Line 3 of the inner script is the first command that needs cargo, which matches the error exactly.

Fix: drop the login shell.

  nix develop --command bash -c '...'

No login semantics are required by the gate, and this makes CI immune to runner profile drift instead of depending on the runner's profile files being PATH-preserving.

If the runner-side profile change was deliberate, the repo-side fix is still correct and strictly more robust; the two are not in conflict.

Impact while unfixed: every caravan PR is BLOCKED, including the bd-f8cf99 backward-compatibility follow-up (PR #10).

title: Detect caravan heads with missing required CI runs instead of waiting forever
description:
A Cara rebase-on-join can produce a new caravan head for which GitHub never starts any workflow run. Required contexts then have zero reporting runs, the PR remains MERGEABLE/BLOCKED forever, and Cara reports healthy/problems=[] while the whole caravan cannot advance.

Live Cacophony evidence:

- caravan2208 members `[2208,2210,2213,2215]`;
- root PR2208 current rebased head `79abc31d4efc07a579145cf904c83c1420f8b4ac`, base main `b464e1ae5cb8033a0789997652d97d6b3efd5c7e`;
- branch protection requires `Check & Lint` and `Fast Tests (unit)`;
- the rebased root head initially had zero workflow runs/zero reporting required contexts, so it sat MERGEABLE/BLOCKED without pending or failed checks while canonical Cara reported healthy;
- other rebased members had runs, so this is a dropped/missed trigger, not universal rebase failure;
- close/reopen of the same PR/head queued pull_request run `30222268397` on unchanged head, proving missing run creation was the blocker rather than source incompatibility;
- root auto-merge durability is separate Caravan P0 bd-2015d2.

Required:

1. After create/rebase/renew/head transition, discover required contexts for the exact target and verify each has at least one run/check-suite lineage on the exact resulting head after a bounded grace period.
2. Distinguish `missing_required_runs` from pending, failing, cancelled/superseded and unknown provider state.
3. If safe provider support exists, trigger exactly one auditable workflow/check-suite request for the unchanged head and rediscover once. Otherwise emit a typed operator-action problem with exact PR/head/contexts and reviewed recovery; never wait silently forever.
4. Preserve head/base/branch/membership and never use an empty commit, close/reopen loop, force, or broad rerun as an implicit workaround.
5. Scheduler status must become degraded/blocked with a visible problem while missing required runs persist; hook evidence must be deduplicated and bounded.
6. Add tests for one/all missing contexts, delayed run arrival, stale-head run, cancelled superseded run, provider partial reads, exact retrigger success/failure and multi-member isolation.
7. Validate against Cacophony PR2208 without mutating children.

## Serial repair chain

Sequence after caravan-root auto-merge durability bd-2015d2 because both modify scheduler convergence around a rewritten root. Do not dispatch in parallel.

## Updated serial order

Run after budget forward-progress P0 bd-e99fe6. The active seven-member caravan cannot process another full sync inside the current deadline, so budget resumability/capacity must land before missing-run recovery can be validated end-to-end on that chain.

title: Gate reshape on non-regression, not perfect fleet health
description:
Live operator block 2026-07-27 on Cacophony: `cara evict --pr 2223` and even evicting the TAIL fail with reshape_would_break_fleet, so a broken caravan cannot be dismantled at all. PR2215 was reverted on main and the operator wants to evict everything and rebuild, with no first-party way to do it.

Root cause, confirmed in src/reshape.rs preflight_result: it rebuilds the projected snapshot, runs analyze, and refuses unless analysis.healthy() is true for the ENTIRE fleet. It never asks whether this reshape made anything worse; it asks whether the whole graph is perfect afterwards. So any pre-existing problem anywhere - other mutually incompatible members, an unrelated broken caravan - blocks every eviction, including ones that strictly reduce the graph. That is the chicken-and-egg the operator hit: the only tool for breaking up a broken chain is itself gated on the chain not being broken.

Evicting a TAIL cannot introduce a problem. It has no child, so no edge is re-linked and no new compatibility pair is created; the projected problem set is a subset of the current one. Refusing it is a false negative.

Required: gate reshape on NON-REGRESSION. Compute the exact problem set before and after the projected reshape and refuse only when the reshape INTRODUCES a problem not already present. Report the introduced problems specifically, not the whole post-state, so the receipt names what this operation would break rather than what was already broken. Pre-existing problems must be carried forward as visible evidence without blocking a reshape that reduces or preserves them.

Consequences: tail eviction becomes the trivial no-op it should be; middle eviction is still refused when the gap-closing edge it creates is genuinely incompatible, which is correct; and a dissolve or cascade becomes a bounded sequence of tail removals rather than a graph rewrite.

Add regressions: evict the tail of a caravan whose other members are mutually incompatible must succeed; evict a middle member whose new edge is incompatible must still refuse with the introduced problem named; evict from a fleet containing an unrelated broken caravan must succeed and must not report the unrelated problems as blockers.

title: Unadmitted candidate conflict aborts the whole sync tick
description:
Live operator report on v0.0.26: `cara sync --all` aborted with

    cara head_conflict: leading admission candidate does not merge cleanly
    into the current default branch

before touching any caravan.

This is a regression I introduced. bd-e9fcd7 added detection of leading-candidate conflicts and recorded them via `record_compatibility`, which pushes `GraphProblemKind::Incompatible` with a single PR. `sync.rs::decision_for_problem` maps exactly that shape — `Incompatible` with `prs.len() == 1` — to `DecisionKind::HeadConflict`, the fleet-blocking decision meant for a caravan MEMBER that cannot merge. So a single conflicting UNADMITTED candidate aborted the whole tick.

That is the opposite of the bead's intent, which was to stop a conflicting candidate holding the queue.

Fix: `GraphProblemKind::CandidateIncompatible`, distinct from `Incompatible`. A candidate that has not been admitted blocks nothing: it is recorded as advisory evidence, admission skips it, and the queue advances. Squash-equivalence reconciliation is deliberately not collected for it either, since nothing downstream may act on an unadmitted candidate.

Pinned by `a_candidate_conflict_is_never_a_fleet_blocking_problem`.

SEPARATE, STILL OPEN: the operator also reports the offending PR is one whose branch already merged. Verified that the filter and state mapping are sound — `unqueued` requires `state == Open`, and `ProviderPullRequestState` is non-optional so a missing state fails to deserialize rather than defaulting to Open. The likely reality is a PR that is still OPEN on the provider while its content already landed by another route (squash of the same patch, or merged via a different PR). Such a PR has no effective patch beyond the default branch and should be reported as already-landed and skipped, not proven for conflicts. bd-032049 already implements exactly this reasoning for creation (`require_nonempty_source_branch`); admission needs the same check.

title: Reject Cara join when candidate patch already landed on default branch
description:
## Live reproduction

While joining Cacophony PR #2080 (`fix-cara-timeouts`) to an active caravan, Cara physically rebased an already-landed release patch onto caravan tail `fix-slackiq-nodes` and enrolled the result instead of rejecting it as already present on the default branch.

Exact observed generations:

- default branch `main`: `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7` (`release: v1.2.1562`), parent `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`
- caravan tail/base: `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, also parented by `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`
- rewritten PR head: `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680`, parented by the caravan tail
- `git patch-id --stable` for both the main commit and rewritten PR commit: `c8c875993b7fed870c2082837caea490559260e2`
- PR #2080 was force-updated to the rewritten head at 23:08:19Z and then labelled `caravan` at 23:08:56Z.

The rewritten PR therefore contains a patch already integrated on exact current `main`. Its diff against the caravan tail is the release patch, while its diff against current main consists only of unrelated caravan-tail drift. The operator described the source PR as empty/already landed before join.

## Gap

`physical_rebase.rs` rejects `commit_count == 0` relative to the candidate's old provider base (`rebase_empty_patch_range`), but does not reject a non-empty candidate range whose stable patch identity/content is already present on the exact default-branch generation. Rebasing that range onto a stale caravan tail resurrects an already-landed change as a new PR commit.

## Required contract

Before a physical join rewrite or enrollment, compare the candidate-only patch range with the exact current default branch and fail closed when every candidate patch is already represented there (stable patch-id and tree/content proof, with ambiguity rejected). Return a typed `already_landed`/empty-effective-diff decision and do not rewrite the head, retarget, label, or enroll the PR.

Add a fixture for sibling histories from one merge base where branch A's patch has already landed on default and joining branch A onto branch B's caravan tail would otherwise replay that patch. Preserve ordinary joining when the candidate has genuinely new effective content.


---

## Merged duplicate: bd-915573

Title: Cara empty-diff join replays another reintegration patch onto caller branch

Operator reproduction on 2026-07-21 exposed cross-reintegration patch contamination while joining Cacophony branch `fix-cara-timeouts` into the active Caravan/Cara tail. The intended operator change was `fix cara timeoutes`, but before that commit was added, Cara/Cacophony synthesized daemon-authored commit `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680` on `fix-cara-timeouts` with the complete, unrelated update-helper `release: v1.2.1562` patch and release-agent provenance.

Exact evidence:

- True GitHub `main` independently and correctly contains release commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7`, parent `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`; annotated tag `v1.2.1562` peels to it.
- The active Cara tail/base branch `fix-slackiq-nodes` is `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, also parented by `80bf4eac` and carrying the separate `fix ms agent scope` patch.
- Cara-created/reused PR https://github.com/harryaskham/cacophony/pull/2080 targets `fix-slackiq-nodes` from `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- Its first commit is `ac701198`, parent `c059bf15`, authored by Cacophony Daemon at 23:04:11Z. Its title/body were initially `release: v1.2.1562` and copied update-helper identity/head `e3026e0461`, despite the operator working on `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- `ac701198` contains only the unrelated release metadata patch (`Cargo.toml`, twenty workspace entries in `Cargo.lock`, and `CHANGELOG.md`). It is a duplicate replay of the patch already landed on true main as `d9fad17e`.
- The operator's intended `fix cara timeoutes` commit `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633` was subsequently added on top of the contaminated release commit; live PR 2080 therefore now contains both `.caravan/config.yaml` and the unrelated release patch.

The operator reports Cara first observed an empty diff while he was on `fix-cara-timeouts`, then created PR 2080 and inferred/replayed the diff from main to the Caravan tail. An empty caller patch must never fall back to another agent's most recent reintegration patch, global generation, main-to-tail delta, or stale receipt.

Required behavior:

- Bind join materialization to the exact caller owner, source branch/head, expected base/tail, and patch identity receipt.
- If the caller's patch against the selected tail is empty, return an explicit empty/no-op/refusal receipt; do not mutate the caller branch and do not create a PR.
- Refuse when receipt owner/head/patch differs from the branch being joined, even if a recent reintegration has a reusable-looking diff or commit message.
- Preserve the caller branch on any ambiguity and surface exact candidate provenance for diagnosis.
- Add a regression test with two concurrent patches: release patch A lands on main while operator branch B joins an active tail with an initially empty diff; B must never receive A.

Do not mutate or close PR 2080 as part of triage; preserve it as live evidence until the owner chooses repair.

## Operator clarification

The initiating `fix-cara-timeouts` PR/branch was believed to have no effective diff. The suspected failure mode is therefore earlier than duplicate-patch replay alone: candidate range inference selected the immediately preceding release commit when the intended source branch was empty, then physical rebase replayed that inferred commit onto the caravan tail.

The fix must first prove the intended provider PR's exact base/head range and reject an empty effective source diff without borrowing a predecessor commit. The already-landed-on-default check remains a necessary independent backstop, because the inferred release commit was already represented on current `main`.

The mechanical merge is conflict-free but semantically incomplete. The first-party repair flow has no exact audited way to authorize restoration of known same-PR contract paths outside `conflicting_paths`.

## Required outcome

- Add an explicit repair semantic-path grant surface (CLI/JSON/MCP) that amends one existing session with a bounded allowlist of repo-relative paths plus rationale/source evidence.
- Bind each grant receipt to repository, PR number, exact expected remote head, target/base OID, session ID/manifest fingerprint, caller/authority, timestamp/expiry, exact path list, and reason. Re-read all identity before accepting or using it.
- Permit edits/staging only within `conflicting_paths ∪ granted_semantic_paths`; continue must reject any changed/staged/untracked path outside that union.
- Distinguish a semantic grant from declaring a conflict. Preserve mechanical conflict evidence and make the grant visible in status/continue/publication receipts.
- Support content provenance for restoration, such as a reviewed source commit/blob/patch digest. For this live case, bind README.md and SPEC.md to the previously routed c915e231/bd-b85ed6 contract rather than allowing arbitrary prose.
- Fail closed on head/target/session drift, symlinks/path traversal, generated/forbidden paths, expired grants, authority mismatch, or content/diff scope beyond the reviewed receipt.
- Keep non-force publication, exact provider remote verification, operation-lock bounds, object-cache isolation, and no raw Git fallback.
- Add fixtures for empty-conflict semantic omission with two granted paths, unauthorized third-path edit, changed source blob, head/target drift, grant expiry/revocation, and successful fresh-CI publication receipt.
- Prove the canonical packaged-binary grant/status/continue flow and publish a landed SHA/version before live PR #1962 restoration. Preserve the current resolving session until then.

title: Make caravan-force bypass pending required checks through an explicit force path
description:
Operator contract from Harry: `caravan-force` means bypass required checks for a known spurious CI failure and force/admin-squash the exact eligible caravan head. It must not merely arm normal auto-merge or wait indefinitely for the checks being bypassed. Non-bypassable guards remain: exact current head/base, open same-repository PR, no conflict, clean compatibility, no source/security red evidence, clear ownership, no competing lander/overlap, no active hold, and configured/admin force authority.

Live reproduction on Cacophony with Cara 0.0.2: PR #1991 is OPEN at exact head `97d698c0f514148e5baa03ce952ad05afdaf8389`, base/main `251d04e9be9742cbf9a9d2cfa0a194601e5a2561`, labels `[caravan, caravan-force]`, clean compatibility tree `f6457acc09b87f82bac29164f166faa61f0b4b4b`, sole squash auto-merge, no active hold, and `force_merge: true`. Independent exact-candidate run `29650048521` on candidate `c2e83233f76639b04d9ab7d5c416303c81ebdca4` passed Changed surface admission, Public Fast Tests preparation, Rust Check & Lint work, Rust Fast Tests work, Check & Lint, and Fast Tests; only non-required macOS UI acceptance failed. A later provider run `29651416115` remained in progress.

`cara sync --all` did not execute force merge. Source contract currently classifies any Expected/Queued/InProgress check as `Waiting` before checking `failed && forced`, so `caravan-force` cannot bypass a pending required check. No `cara force` command exists (`unrecognized subcommand 'force'`).

Implement an explicit audited force path, preferably `cara force --pr <N> --match-head <sha> --reason/evidence ...`, or equivalent sync semantics that distinguish bypassable required-check state from non-bypassable source/security/compatibility guards. It must re-read exact provider state immediately, require configured force policy and ADMIN permission, prove no competing lander/hold, record evidence and rollback, force-squash once with an exact-head guard, remove/consume force intent idempotently, and advance the child safely. title: DO NOT RESTART sync loop unaudited - force_merge true means a tick MAY MERGE under the explicit-actor hold - loop was never running - joining is automatic - choice-019fa6d6
description:
Short by design. bd-3f99dc is truncated at 8000 of 11004 bytes, so this content is unreadable there; filed separately per the split-before-the-boundary rule.

## Two findings that collapse the queue stall

### 1. JOINING WAS NEVER AN AGENT ACTION

From `.caravan/config.yaml` at main 923c05cf, established by helsinki-cacophony-caco-ctrl against their own earlier position:

    line  5   rebase_on_join: true
    line 14   sync.actions.join_unlabelled_prs: TRUE
    line 30   join_failed hook -> ./scripts/cara-hook

Cara joins unlabelled PRs BY ITSELF during sync. No `cara new`, no `cara join`, no membership verb, no hold to lift.

Hours of fleet reasoning about admission verbs and membership holds addressed a lane that does not gate joining. The canary never needed `caco agent complete` either.

### 2. THE OPERATOR SYNC LOOP WAS NEVER RUNNING

`pgrep -f "cara sync"` and `ps aux` checked at 00:41, 02:00 and 04:46 — three times across four hours, NEVER PRESENT.

The `while true; do cara sync --all; sleep 600; done` announced at 00:51 produced ZERO ticks, not twenty. A bare shell loop dies with its terminal.

## Version hypothesis tested and REFUTED

caco-ctrl hypothesised the loop resolved a cara below the 0.0.12 config floor, dying at 0s per tick like the three dark Linux nodes. Tested from the agent shell AND a stripped login shell approximating the operator PATH:

    command -v cara -> /Users/harryaskham/.cargo/bin/cara
    cara --version  -> cara 0.0.13   (parses this config)

PATH puts /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin, /bin first, none containing cara; `~/.cargo/bin` precedes `~/.nix-profile/bin`.

ms-mac is NOT a fourth dark node. The binary was always correct. The join_failed hook has nothing recorded because no tick ever attempted a join.

## THE ENTIRE REMEDY

Restart the sync loop under something that survives terminal close — launchd, tmux, nohup. Joins begin on the first tick.

No membership decision. No hold lifted. No admission verb. No queue defect.

## DURABLE REQUIREMENT for the cron design

A bare `while` loop is not a supervision strategy.

The cron needs PROCESS SUPERVISION and PER-PASS RECEIPTS, because four agents spent hours unable to distinguish "loop running and refusing to join" from "loop absent" — and the answer was the second. Every hypothesis tested (head-of-line, DIRTY head, max_candidates_per_tick, head_merge_actor, binary version, membership holds) was investigating a process that did not exist.

A single receipt line per tick naming the verb, the caravan count, and the unqueued count would have ended it immediately.

## CRITICAL AMENDMENT: restarting the loop is a MERGE-AUTHORIZATION decision, not process management

The remedy above — "restart the loop under supervision, joins begin, nothing else required" — is TRUE AND INCOMPLETE. Do not act on it as written.

`.caravan/config.yaml` line 4, verified directly on main 923c05cf:

    force_merge: true

So `cara sync --all` does not merely JOIN. **A tick may MERGE.**

Merging sits inside the explicit-actor hold active at revision 7, renewed seven times on unmet conditions. Restarting the loop would therefore start a process that can merge fleet-wide under a hold specifically forbidding unaudited merge actors — an accidental bypass rather than a deliberate authorization.

Found by helsinki-cacophony-caco-ctrl on a config re-read, after both they and the router had published the incomplete remedy.

### Raised as choice-019fa6d6, safe option first

1. LEAVE STOPPED until the operator wakes and restarts it themselves, having seen the force_merge implication
2. authorize ONE bounded tick by a named owner on a verified-0.0.13 node, accepting it may merge
3. authorize a tick AND narrow the explicit-actor hold so cara-driven merges are legitimate rather than accidental

caco-ctrl recommends 1; the router concurs. Nothing degrades overnight — all 15 candidates are CLEAN or repairable and lose nothing by waiting. Merging fleet-wide with PR2245's cancelled-producer fix still unlanded, after a night in which several confident instructions proved wrong, is precisely when not to widen a lane.

## METHOD LESSON, volunteered by caco-ctrl against themselves

They narrowed the membership lane, then observed `cara check` begin reporting eligible/canonical, and read that as the hold releasing.

**It was not.** Joining was never gated by the hold — `join_unlabelled_prs: true` means Cara joins unlabelled PRs by itself. The eligibility observed had nothing to do with their change.

A CHANGE FOLLOWED BY A CORRELATED OBSERVATION IS NOT A DEMONSTRATED MECHANISM. They did not test the alternative because the result matched what they expected.

That is the same failure named hours earlier — test the case in front of you, skip the complement — committed after naming it. The defence requires asking "what else would produce this observation?" even when, especially when, the change appears to have worked.

title: sync --all exceeds bounded client window and strands a dead operation lock
description:
## Helsinki Cacophony canary

Installed `cara 0.0.1` SHA-256 `2c4b26031301d6730c54029eb24abc2765550ebeb406e1794a13ee4fb7b3ee99` successfully created Caravan #2008 and enrolled its configured maximum eight members. A subsequent root-checkout command:

```text
cara --json sync --all
```

exceeded a 180-second bounded client/tool window and was terminated without a JSON receipt. Provider re-read via `cara --json status` was healthy and showed the complete intended chain with exactly one head auto-merge, but `cara lock status` reported:

```json
{"pid":3406790,"operation":"sync_decision_checkout","token":"3406790-1784334101494090487-1","owner_alive":false,"age_secs":198,"stale_after_secs":1800,"stale":false}
```

No Cara process remained alive. This leaves all later mutations blocked for the default 30-minute stale floor after an ordinary client cancellation/timeout, despite affirmative dead-owner proof.

The merger safely recovered only after re-reading provider state and using exact-token first-party recovery with `--stale-after-secs 180 --confirm`; recovery receipt proved owner dead and token verified.

## Acceptance

- Bound `sync --all` provider inventory/decision work below documented command/client ceilings for a 30-PR repository and an eight-member caravan, or stream/return an accepted operation receipt before the ceiling.
- Release the operation lock through cancellation/termination-safe ownership cleanup when the owning process exits; a dead owner must not strand a fresh non-stale lock solely because the client timed out.
- Preserve fail-closed exact-token recovery for genuinely ambiguous/live ownership.
- Add canaries for SIGTERM/client disconnect during `sync_decision_checkout`, dead owner below the default stale age, live owner, PID reuse/token mismatch, and provider mutation indeterminacy.
- On cancellation after possible provider writes, persist enough operation phase/provider receipts that the next `status`/`sync` can prove replay/no-op safely.
- Keep bounded status JSON and stdout/stderr contracts from bd-f7c3bc.

Implementation/live canary checkpoint on rebased e98eff main: sync now owns one absolute budget `min(5*command_timeout,150s)`, shares it across initial/final status and provider runners (normal child cap remains 30s), and avoids a third full discovery by checking out the exact PR snapshot already embedded in a decision. Operation owner files persist compact phase/exact-precondition receipts and provider-indeterminate state. A later acquisition automatically removes only a twice-read exact-token owner whose PID is affirmatively dead, at any age; live/PID-reused/changed-token cases remain fail-closed. Unit canary sends real SIGTERM to a child holding `sync_decision_checkout`, verifies fresh dead checkpoint survives, then exact recovery succeeds below 30m. Read-only live GitHub canary used a clean Caravan clone and local config with no priority labels: pre-status saw fresh dead pid999999, age0, stale=false, auto_recoverable=true, exact decision_checkout checkpoint. `cara --json sync --all` returned success changed=false, zero caravans/provider writes, exact token-verified lock_recovery including checkpoint, timing total=13,620ms (initial status6,160/provider0/final7,378) under deadline150,000ms; post lock status absent. Provider graph remained healthy.

title: Fail closed when a merged Caravan branch name is reused under a child
description:
Current PR identity and provider mutations are bound to PR number plus exact head/base OIDs, but graph edges are derived by matching an active child baseRefName to active PR headRefName. Race: Caravan parent A on branch B merges; child C still targets B; before sync retargets C, an unrelated new PR D reuses branch name B. GitHub moves B, C now resolves against D, and derive() can silently treat D as C parent because active heads_by_branch takes precedence over merged_by_head. Clean compatibility may not reveal the provenance change.

Fail closed on this historical/active branch-name collision rather than silently reparenting. At minimum, when a child base name is exposed by both a retained merged Caravan PR and a different active PR, report a typed branch-reuse/ambiguous-predecessor graph problem with old/new PR numbers and exact OIDs; do not arm/merge/retarget until operator resolves or the old child is safely advanced. Prefer a durable edge identity bound by join receipt/audit (predecessor PR + generation) if needed beyond conservative detection.

Acceptance:
- Parent merged + child still targeting old branch + new active PR reuses name: invalid graph, zero provider mutation.
- Reuse after every old child has been retargeted: allowed as independent PR.
- Multiple historical uses, active duplicate heads, deleted/fork heads, and provider head/base movement remain fail closed.
- Current/open PR lookup still identifies by unique PR number and exact OIDs; explicit safe historical unlabelled --create-pr behavior remains supported.
- Sync midpoint/concurrent race test proves reuse between discovery and mutation hits exact preconditions.
- CLI/JSON/MCP/status expose actionable old/new provenance; docs warn against premature branch reuse.

description:

5. Add tests for create, root rebase/head rewrite, CI transition, external disarm, idempotent replay, stale provider response, and no mutation of child members.
6. Validate against Cacophony caravan2208 without manually mutating its children.

Authenticated Cacophony choice `choice-019fa07d-03ef-7180-b0ee-98556a35f2d7` selected one exact re-arm. Therefore controller performed no duplicate provider mutation. Durability defect remains: root arming disappeared at least twice across transitions and required subsequent convergence.

## Provenance correction and duplicate consolidation

The re-arm observed at 2026-07-26T22:13:58Z was performed by `helsinki-cacophony-cluster-ctrl` under the `caco-ctrl` lease, not by Cara or the operator. Provider state did not expose who/why clearly enough for controllers to distinguish engine convergence from human repair. This strengthens the acceptance requirement for auditable engine arming provenance.

Cacophony bead bd-8db3a1 captured the same defect and is consolidated here because the source fix belongs in Caravan. Its useful additional framing is incorporated: distinguish required root arming from unrelated-candidate exclusion, and never normalize periodic operator re-arm as the solution.

## Third root arming loss

PR2208 lost required squash auto-merge a third time on the same caravan. Cluster control re-armed it under lease and canonical state immediately returned healthy. Two of the three observed losses occurred without agent/controller disarm action, confirming a real scheduler/provider durability defect rather than only the original mistaken manual disarm. Preserve exact arming provenance and transition receipts in the fix.

## Live caravan2208 validation (read-only; zero provider mutations)

Observed on ms-dev-5 between 2026-07-26T22:5xZ and 23:1xZ with the fix build. No Cacophony provider action was taken and no child was mutated.

**1. The defect recurred again and needed a further out-of-band re-arm.**
A direct GraphQL read showed PR2208 head `79abc31d4efc07a579145cf904c83c1420f8b4ac`, base `main`, `autoMergeRequest: null`, caravan label/membership intact -- the same DEGRADED shape as originally reported. By 23:11Z the same PR read back armed with `enabledAt: 2026-07-26T23:06:11Z`, `enabledBy: harryaskham`, `mergeMethod: SQUASH`. That is another out-of-band re-arm, not engine convergence: exactly the operator-babysitting loop this bead removes.

**2. Root cause proven from live no-write planning output.**
`cara plan sync --all` (no-write path; `provider_mutations: 0`, `branch_mutations: 0`) returned every physical plan for the caravan2208 chain as `already_satisfied: true` with `old_head_oid == new_head_oid`:

No branch is being rewritten at all, yet pre-fix `apply_physical_chains` disarmed native auto-merge on *every* selected member including root #2208 on *every* tick before applying nothing. Any later failure in that same tick (CI stop, budget error, provider error) then left the root disarmed with nothing to re-arm it. That is the durability window behind the repeated DEGRADED `auto_merge_invariant` and the repeated manual re-arms.

Two contributing defects were found alongside it:
- `reconcile_caravan` returned the CI decision *before* re-arming, so any failing member generation guaranteed the root stayed disarmed;
- required root arming was decided from the discovery list projection, which can still expose a pre-rewrite `autoMergeRequest`.

**3. The live generation is pinned as a hermetic regression fixture.**
`live_caravan2208_root_converges_without_touching_its_children` reproduces members `[2208,2210,2213,2215]`, root head `79abc31d...` on `main@b464e1ae...`, `autoMergeRequest` null; asserts the reported `auto_merge_invariant` problem appears; then proves the engine converges it with a sealed receipt on the exact resulting head, `root_head_rewritten` provenance, exactly one provider mutation, and byte-identical child snapshots. `live_caravan2208_replay_is_a_proven_no_op` proves the following tick writes nothing.

Out of scope, not actioned: the live plan stopped on the pre-existing `physical_sync_budget_insufficient` guard (`minimum_additional_ms: 1105823`), a Cacophony `sync.max_duration_secs` budget matter unrelated to this fix.

## Fix summary (Caravan)

- New `src/root_auto_merge.rs`: sealed `RootAutoMergeReceipt`, auditable `RootAutoMergeProvenance` (owner `caravan-scheduler`, component, operation id, derived trigger, observed-before state and provider actor, `engine_armed`), derived `RootAutoMergeTrigger` (`idempotent_replay`, `root_admitted`, `root_head_rewritten`, `root_base_advanced`, `externally_disarmed`, `non_squash_method`) and typed `RootAutoMergeFailureCause`.
- `SyncProgress::ensure_root_squash_auto_merge` re-reads the exact current root from a fresh single-PR provider read, refuses to prove anything against a generation the tick did not verify, arms and re-reads until squash auto-merge is proven on the *resulting* head, and seals a receipt. Bounded arming attempts and confirmation reads; on exhaustion it emits retryable `root_auto_merge_not_durable` with `operator_action_required=false`.
- Root arming now converges *before* a failing-CI stop.
- Physical rebase only disarms members whose branch generation is actually rewritten.
- Receipts surface in `SyncOutput.root_auto_merge`, in decision error details, in human output, and as a new `root_auto_merge_armed` event.
- Raced state/draft/base/`caravan`/`caravan-evicted` transitions still stop with an exact-field `stale_precondition`; unrelated label churn does not.
- Preserved distinction: native auto-merge on an unadmitted candidate remains structural ineligibility; only the admitted root requires SQUASH auto-merge.

title: cara status segfaults on an adopted current-PR worktree
description:
## Reproduction

Installed binary was built from exact Caravan main `e451ed9c02860f9dea408cd68890fdde56c8846a` after bd-f7c3bc and installed as:

```text
~/.cargo/bin/cara --version
cara 0.0.1
sha256 57674ebff36f28fa576d14bb73044ee4981ba88bec899b4071c52c3f5fc1129b
```

The managed Cacophony root checkout now passes `~/.cargo/bin/cara --json status` (schema 1, healthy, 29 PRs).

From the Cacophony merger's first-party adopted PR #2008 worktree:

```text
cd /home/harry/.cacophony/agents/cacophony/helsinki-cacophony-caco-merger/pr-adoptions/pr-2008
~/.cargo/bin/cara --json status
```

Cara crashes deterministically:

```text
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
exit=139
stdout_bytes=0
stderr_bytes=0
```

Worktree context:

- branch: `agent/pocket4/cacophony/pocket4-cacophony-caco-android-po4-0-pr-g2765f0b235b020fef1b794ef6ebe2cd829c49ce5`
- PR: #2008
- current local/published head: `971386cf4ee1453e7af53d299c823ae888d7e505`
- the branch was adopted through first-party `caco pr adopt`, merged current main, resolved one SPEC conflict, committed, and pushed non-force to the same PR;
- git status is clean.

This blocks `cara check/new/join/sync` formation from the actual PR checkout. Caco-merger must not attempt `cara sync` after a crashing status and remains on its existing audited native path for this PR.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce with a current PR branch whose local/published head contains a merge commit and whose branch name is a Cacophony immutable generation ref.
- Eliminate all panic/abort/unsafe crash paths: every current-PR resolution failure must return a structured JSON error/decision envelope and nonzero normal exit, never SIGSEGV.
- Add deterministic tests for: root checkout with no current PR; ordinary current PR branch; Cacophony generation branch; adopted PR worktree; merge-commit head; stale metadata source head versus newer published head.
- Preserve stdout/stderr separation and large JSON handling from bd-f7c3bc.
- Prove `cara --json status`, `cara --json check`, and the preflight for `cara new/join/sync` are safe from the adopted PR #2008 worktree shape.
- Return an installed-path Helsinki canary request with exact fixed Caravan SHA/version/receipt.

## Regression after operator updater — root status and sync also crash

The operator updater replaced the previously passing installed binary with another `cara 0.0.1` binary:

- current installed SHA-256: `0e88ba61fcb6df4aaf95b609d714d8caae9942be4a0cfcccabb4912e4e59f813`;
- daemon Caravan checkout still reports `e451ed9c02860f9dea408cd68890fdde56c8846a`;
- all three required GitHub labels are present with correct metadata.

From the managed **Cacophony root checkout** (not the adopted worktree), both operator-requested commands now deterministically SIGSEGV:

```text
~/.cargo/bin/cara --json status
exit=139 stdout_bytes=0 stderr_bytes=0

~/.cargo/bin/cara --json sync --all
exit=139 stdout_bytes=0 stderr_bytes=0
```

This broadens the blocker: the crash is no longer limited to current-PR/adopted-worktree resolution. `sync --all` can crash before producing any receipt or decision envelope even with repository labels initialized. No PR mutation was observed; caco-merger stopped immediately.

Acceptance must now include root-checkout installed-binary status and sync-all canaries in addition to adopted-PR coverage, and identify why the operator-installed build hash regressed while the earlier exact-e451 build (`57674e...`) passed root status.

Diagnosis complete; no Caravan status/domain patch. Canonical Helsinki job tj-cc939cc0 proves installed SHA 2c4b2603 (fresh ambient cargo build, glibc 2.42 coherent) returns healthy 30-PR status when `NIX_LD` and `NIX_LD_LIBRARY_PATH` are unset, and SIGSEGVs with inherited managed runtime variables. Preserved core PID 3112435 NT_FILE proves loader/libc mismatch: glibc 2.40 loader plus glibc 2.42 libc; crash is dlsym inside std::Thread::new before a structured status result is possible. Independent matrix: installed/fresh ambient SHA 2c4b passes root and adopted PR #2008; devshell SHA 57daaa and Nix package SHA be2931 use glibc 2.40 and pass clean but deterministically exit139 on both shapes under foreign 2.42 library injection. Cacophony P1 bd-d7d543 owns invocation sanitization and deployment bd-0b9bec depends on it. Accidental duplicate bd-b93947 was marked duplicate. This bead should close redirected; the acceptance demand for a Caravan panic fix is inapplicable because failure occurs in the dynamic loader/runtime environment.

## Current-checkout fallback also SIGSEGVs

Direct operator recovery instructed caco-merger to use `nix run ~/.cacophony/daemon/checkouts/caravan -- <args>` while the installed binary is stale. On Caravan source checkout exact clean head `10db52bcc3415d480a42a7729ecb29691f8fa01b` (`cara 0.0.1`), from the clean first-party PR2012 worktree:

```text
nix run /home/harry/.cacophony/daemon/checkouts/caravan -- check --json
exit=139
stdout_bytes=0
stderr_bytes=0
```

The same current checkout returns `cara 0.0.1` for `--version`, so Nix evaluation/build succeeds and the crash occurs in Cara's PR/current-worktree check path. A prior global-form invocation (`-- --json check`) also produced no usable output. No provider mutation followed: caco-merger failed closed and used its audited exact-head manual path only for the independent green P0 PR2012, outside the active PR2008 hold.

Acceptance should canary both argument orders through installed and `nix run <checkout>` paths and require a structured success/error envelope rather than zero-output exit or SIGSEGV.

### Root-cause clarification

This fallback observation does **not** overturn the closed loader-environment diagnosis above. The managed merger runtime inherited the same foreign `NIX_LD` / `NIX_LD_LIBRARY_PATH` class; wrapping Cara in `nix run` does not sanitize those variables before the produced binary starts. Treat the zero-output SIGSEGV as additional invocation-sanitization evidence for Cacophony `bd-d7d543`, not as a new Caravan domain/status defect. A valid fallback canary must explicitly unset the foreign loader variables before invocation.

title: Detect required contexts with zero reporting runs on a rebased head
description:
Live evidence on caravan root 2208: Cara rebase head 79abc31d had ZERO workflow runs while the branch requires Check and Lint plus Fast Tests (unit), so the PR sat MERGEABLE/BLOCKED indefinitely with 0 failed and 0 pending while canonical status reported healthy with problems=0. The other three rebased members each got a run, so the missed trigger is intermittent and provider-side.

Confirmed source cause: sync::classify_checks treats an empty check set as pending. `let pending = checks.is_empty() || ...` returns CiDisposition::Waiting, so "no run was ever created for a required context" is indistinguishable from "runs are queued". Sync then waits forever and status shows no problem.

Required behaviour: after a bounded grace period measured from the exact rebased head publication, verify that every REQUIRED status context has a reporting run bound to that exact head OID. If a required context has zero reporting runs, emit typed caravan_member_missing_required_runs carrying PR number, exact head OID, and the precise missing contexts, and keep it clearly distinct from pending and from failing. Optionally retrigger the same-head workflow through a reviewed first-party path; never fabricate a check result. The empty-checks-equals-waiting shortcut must no longer silently mask a never-triggered required context.

Constraint learned from the live workaround: closing and reopening the PR did retrigger CI on the same head and proved recovery, but it also disarmed root auto-merge. Root auto-merge is REQUIRED by Cara, so any recovery path must preserve or re-arm it. Arming provenance and disarm reporting are tracked separately in bd-93e366; keep these deduped.

title: Cara owns squash-merge and base retargeting so auto-merge is not needed
description:
Operator directive 2026-07-27: an accidental merge into the next caravan member instead of main was observed. Auto-merge will be disabled on the cacophony repo, and Cara must own the full landing lifecycle so behaviour is not a mix of Cara and provider auto-merge.

## Problem

Today landing is split between two actors. Cara selects and validates admission, while GitHub auto-merge performs the actual merge. Because each chain member is based on its predecessor rather than main, provider auto-merge can fire against a stale base and land a member into the next caravan member instead of into main. That is the accidental merge the operator saw. Two actors mutating the same refs also makes ordering and blame hard to reason about.

## Required behaviour

1. Cara performs the squash-merge itself, on each tick, for the valid and compatible HEAD, rather than delegating to provider auto-merge.
2. Cara retargets the base of the next chain member to `main` once its predecessor lands, so no member is ever merged into a sibling.
3. Compatibility is revalidated against current `main` immediately before mutation; abort on drift rather than merging a stale evaluation.
4. Exactly one merge actor. With auto-merge disabled, Cara must not re-arm it, and must fail closed rather than falling back to a provider merge path.
5. Preserve existing FIFO admission ordering, priority labels, and the rule that rejection never causes automatic leapfrogging.
6. Preserve pause and suspension semantics: an active pause record must still stop landing.
7. Emit exact receipts per landing: PR number, head SHA, base SHA, resulting main SHA, and the retarget applied to the successor.

## Explicitly accepted trade-off

The operator accepts that one-merge-per-tick is slower than parallel auto-merge. Safety and reasoning clarity are the priority.

## Acceptance

- With repository auto-merge disabled, a multi-member chain drains fully through Cara alone.
- No member ever lands into another member; every landing target is `main`.
- A stale-base member is retargeted and revalidated before landing, or refused.
- Suspension and pause records still block landing.
- Receipts are sufficient to reconstruct the exact landing order after the fact.

## Context

Current canonical Cacophony queue state is degraded with auto-merge suspended under pause record actor `ms-mac-cacophony-caco-dev-msm-0`, caravan_head 2053, reason "External runner pin failures bd-536622/bd-617fb3". Related recent evidence includes the Caravan root #2210 arming decision and the physical-sync budget refusals tracked under bd-bbc981. This bead is the architectural fix that removes the dual-actor hazard rather than re-arming auto-merge.

---

## Merged duplicate: bd-e1c6ce

Title: [P0] Make Caravan the sole squash-merge actor with retarget-before-merge ordering

Direct operator architecture decision: disable native GitHub auto-merge for Cacophony. Caravan becomes the sole leased merge actor. On each tick it must retarget the current caravan head to main when its predecessor merged, revalidate against the new base, squash-merge exact head into main, then promote the next member. Remove the existing `auto_merge_invariant` in the same release; otherwise repo-level auto-merge disable makes every caravan permanently degraded.

Strict operation order:
1. If caravan head base != main and predecessor is merged, retarget head base to main.
2. Wait for/recompute exact merge-base, compatibility, required contexts and zero-run diagnostics against the NEW base/head.
3. Only when exact head is valid/compatible/green, squash-merge it to main under Caravan lease.
4. Emit provider receipt and verify main contains the resulting tree before promoting next member.
5. Promote next member and repeat on a later tick; no native auto-merge actor.

Never merge before retarget/revalidation. Live failure receipt: PR2213 was CLEAN but still based on predecessor generation branch. Native auto-merge landed commit `3da6addbf0b1` into `agent/ms-dev-3/cacophony/8x5t4zp7luvs0a4q-pr-gf9e8151b76a9dae6b883c59a249700a7ca933540`, not main; compare against main is DIVERGED, behind_by=3, so content never reached main. Caravan then re-rooted to2215 with the same dangling-base condition. Fix must safely handle the whole remaining chain, not one head.

Safety/acceptance:
- single leased mutation actor; exact repository/head/base/required-check re-read and abort-on-drift;
- idempotent squash receipt, provider request IDs, main tree containment postflight;
- retry/indeterminate classification with no duplicate merge;
- atomic promotion plan integrated with bd-9ead1b realistic sync budgeting;
- tests for stale predecessor branch, wrong-target refusal, required checks becoming stale after retarget, concurrent main movement, provider timeout after merge, and multi-member drain;
- migration of existing caravans with no native auto-merge and no content loss;
- SPEC/config/status update: no `auto_merge_invariant`; report Caravan merge authority and next exact action.

Coordinate Cacophony removal of native arming/rearming and runner provisioning. Do not mutate Cacophony PRs in tests.

## Operator refinement 2026-07-27 08:39 BST — exact mechanism and interim policy

The operator specified the concrete design rather than leaving it open:

### New typed option: `auto_merge_head`

Caravan gains an explicit `auto_merge_head` option controlling whether Cara itself merges the caravan head. It will be **disabled in cacophony**, so Cara performs the sync on head rather than delegating to provider auto-merge. This makes the behaviour a typed configuration decision per project rather than an implicit split between two actors.

### Required sequencing

1. Cara syncs/merges the caravan **head** when it is valid and compatible.
2. When PR2 subsequently reaches head, its target is retargeted to `main`.
3. Provided nobody else has pushed to `main` in the interim, that retarget is a **content-identical rebase** — no semantic change, no re-review needed.
4. The no-other-push condition must be checked, not assumed. If `main` moved, the member is revalidated (or refused) rather than silently rebased onto different content.

### Interim operator policy, until this lands

The operator will **manually merge** items that reach caravan head, to work around auto-merge being disabled. Agents must therefore expect operator-performed merges at head during this window and must not:

- interpret an operator merge at head as a queue fault, race, or drift to repair;
- re-arm provider auto-merge to "unblock" the chain;
- open replacement PRs or re-land already-merged content because a landing was performed manually.

Verify against real `main` before concluding anything is unlanded; a stale local mirror has already produced one false not-landed report this cycle.

### Operator intent

Stated explicitly: "Lets get this right once and for all." This is a durable architectural fix, not a workaround, and the interim manual merges are scaffolding to be removed once `auto_merge_head` exists and Cara owns head sync.

## Field refinement: prefer tree equality over "main did not move" (from ms-dev-3 ex9vj4iedmpf8g3y, 2026-07-27)

The retarget safety check should compare **trees**, not merely assert that `main` has not moved.

Rationale, with live evidence from that agent: Cara `rebase_on_join` already produces content-identical rebases whose old and new commits share a tree — observed going `20b4a8d887` -> `ccc3af5c2d` with tree `3efd0de751` on both. A tree-equality check therefore:

- **accepts** the common safe case where `main` moved but touched disjoint paths, which a naive "main did not move" check would reject;
- **still refuses** a genuinely different rebase where content actually changed.

This widens the safe path without weakening the guard, and reduces spurious refusals during normal concurrent activity on main. Recommend implementing the no-other-push condition as: retarget is permitted when the resulting tree is identical to the validated tree; otherwise revalidate or refuse.

Corroborating context from the same report: PR #2239 was verified against the real GitHub API rather than the local mirror — real main `12eee6c279` does not contain the change, PR is OPEN/CLEAN with all six required contexts green on head `616dcfcbf9`. That agent is holding it untouched and unarmed per the interim policy.

## Postcondition requirement: assert REACHABILITY, not merge-state (from ms-dev-3 33t2dm7w5ou3zetd, 2026-07-27)

This is the check that would have caught the incident at the moment it happened rather than hours later.

`#2213` reported `MERGED` while its merge commit was **unreachable from `main`**, and nothing surfaced that. Provider merge-state is therefore insufficient as a landing postcondition.

Required after any head merge:

```
git merge-base --is-ancestor <merge_commit_oid> origin/main
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/<merge_commit_oid>...main --jq .status   # expect "ahead" or "identical"
```

Cacophony already holds itself to this pattern in the `bd-98b2fc` merged-generation preflight, so this is consistency with an existing product contract rather than a new invention.

Live evidence from the provider API, independently reproduced against `ssh://git@github.com/harryaskham/cacophony.git` with local `origin/main` = `12eee6c279` byte-identical to `gh api .../commits/main`:

```
#2213 merge 3da6addbf0 ...main -> diverged  ahead_by=4  behind_by=3
#2213 head  c9fe0b2baf ...main -> diverged  ahead_by=4  behind_by=3
#2210 merge 176fd149d3 ...main -> ahead     ahead_by=1  behind_by=0   (control)
```

A true ancestor of `main` compares as `ahead, behind_by=0`, as the `#2210` control shows. `#2213` returns `diverged`, so its work is genuinely not on `main` by the providers own reckoning. Note this is explicitly **not** a claim of lost work: `#2213` head is an ancestor of `#2215` head, so the chain still carries the content and the ordinary drain lands it. No hand-recovery, cherry-pick, or re-land should be attempted.

## Sizing correction: revalidate-or-refuse is the HOT path, not an edge case

Measured on `origin/main` by the same agent: **30 commits in 24h, 10 in 12h, 4 in 6h** — roughly one push every 45 minutes, during a period when the queue was largely stalled. 4 of the 30 were releases independent of the caravan.

So "main moved in between" will be the common branch, not the exception. The revalidate-or-refuse path must be engineered as the hot path: efficient, well-tested, and not a rarely-exercised fallback. This also strengthens the case for the tree-equality check above, since strict "main did not move" would refuse constantly at this commit rate.

## Canonical tracking correction

This bead is CLOSED as duplicate. Canonical live implementation is `caravan:bd-f8cf99`, owner `caravan:oqzipq640ex5hh6t` on ms-dev-6. All unique operator acceptance and `auto_merge_head` refinement were copied there. Do not claim, reopen, implement, or route work against this record.

## Implementation aid: Cara already emits the tree oid needed for the check (from ms-dev-5 r0clfm7p8z1dgv50, 2026-07-27)

Caras existing check output already carries the material required to implement the no-other-push condition — no new computation is needed.

For that agents candidate, the check returned a synthetic **merge tree oid** `883fa5bd8e9518ec610c9d7c06c4d114859ceec3`, identical to the compatibility rows `merge-tree result`. Comparing that tree oid before and after a retarget is:

- a **deterministic content-identity test**, and
- an **automatic detector of an intervening push to main**, because a moved `main` simply produces a different merge tree.

This converges with the tree-equality proposal already recorded above, and means the implementation can reuse existing compatibility-analysis output rather than adding a separate main-movement probe. One comparison satisfies both requirements.

Independent provider-truth verification from the same agent, using `gh pr view` / `gh api` against `harryaskham/cacophony` directly rather than any local mirror: main tip `12eee6c279974d2695a9273d77beefd7e1d2fc44`; PR #2223 OPEN at head `c17fd2b9e1d97790a2827721d7c2490d0df23745`; compare main -> that head reports `diverged`, so main genuinely does not contain #2223. This independently corroborates the same main sha reported by ms-dev-3, from a different agent and node.

Also recorded for chain state: PR #2224 head `1b81d50f9607e34a3c221ff35f92bd5e45f1e578` is based directly on main, never auto-merge armed, join-skipped label and dead letter intact, local tree clean, parked under the caco-ctrl hold.

## CORRECTION to the reachability postcondition: content-existence is the sound test under squash merge (from ms-dev-5 ln8ys7uvrmriol3i, 2026-07-27)

This partially corrects the reachability postcondition recorded above, and the correction is right.

**In a squash-merge repository, testing whether a PRs merge commit is an ancestor of `main` is an unreliable landed-test.** Squash merging never places the PRs own merge commit on `main`, so a `diverged` result can be a false negative. The `compare/main...<merge_commit_oid>` probe must not be trusted on its own by anyone.

**The sound test is content existence at the ref:**

```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/<path-the-PR-adds>?ref=main
```

A 404 means the content is genuinely absent from `main`. This cannot be fooled by squash, rebase, retarget, or mirror staleness, and it is a content-level fact independent of commit topology.

**Router independently verified this**, directly against github.com rather than accepting the report:

```
gh api repos/harryaskham/cacophony/contents/docs/design/pr-cara-join-live-canary-generation4.md?ref=main
  -> HTTP 404 Not Found
gh api repos/harryaskham/cacophony/commits/main --jq .sha
  -> 12eee6c279974d2695a9273d77beefd7e1d2fc44
```

So PR2213s sole added file is confirmed absent from `main` at that exact sha. Three agents on two nodes independently report the same main sha.

### Reconciling the two postconditions

They are complementary, not contradictory, once the subject of the check is stated precisely:

1. **Landed test (strongest, use this to conclude landed/unlanded):** does the PRs content exist at `?ref=main`. Immune to squash/rebase/retarget/mirror.
2. **Merge-target postcondition (use this immediately after a merge operation):** assert that the commit the merge operation actually produced is reachable from the branch it was supposed to land on. This is what catches the original incident, where the merge landed onto the predecessor branch instead of `main` while reporting `MERGED`.

Check 2 must be applied to the resulting `main` sha returned by the merge, not to a PR merge-commit oid interpreted as an ancestor of `main`. Implement both; do not implement only the ancestry form.

Disposition note: PR2213s owner is `h8e3rwcgdxmggus0` on ms-dev-3. No re-land, replacement, or claim is proposed by any reporting agent; the point is only that a verified content-level absence must not be written off as mirror staleness, since that owners bead may read done while the file is absent from main.

## CORRECTION to the reachability postcondition: content-existence is the sound landed-test under squash merge (from ms-dev-5 ln8ys7uvrmriol3i, 2026-07-27)

This partially corrects the reachability postcondition recorded above, and the correction is right.

**In a squash-merge repository, testing whether a PR merge commit is an ancestor of `main` is an unreliable landed-test.** Squash merging never places the PR own merge commit on `main`, so a `diverged` result can be a false negative. The `compare/main...<merge_commit_oid>` probe must not be trusted on its own.

**The sound test is content existence at the ref:**

```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/<path-the-PR-adds>?ref=main
```

A 404 means the content is genuinely absent from `main`. This cannot be fooled by squash, rebase, retarget, or mirror staleness, and it is a content-level fact independent of commit topology.

**Router independently verified this directly against github.com** rather than accepting the report:

```
gh api repos/harryaskham/cacophony/contents/docs/design/pr-cara-join-live-canary-generation4.md?ref=main
  -> HTTP 404 Not Found
gh api repos/harryaskham/cacophony/commits/main --jq .sha
  -> 12eee6c279974d2695a9273d77beefd7e1d2fc44
```

PR2213 sole added file is confirmed absent from `main` at that exact sha. Three agents across two nodes independently report the same main sha, each using provider-truth methods.

### Reconciling the two postconditions

They are complementary once the subject of each check is stated precisely:

1. **Landed test (use to conclude landed/unlanded):** does the PR content exist at `?ref=main`. Immune to squash, rebase, retarget, and mirror staleness.
2. **Merge-target postcondition (use immediately after a merge operation):** assert that the commit the merge operation actually produced is reachable from the branch it was supposed to land on. This is what catches the original incident, where the merge reported `MERGED` while landing onto the predecessor branch instead of `main`.

Check 2 must be applied to the resulting `main` sha returned by the merge, not to a PR merge-commit oid interpreted as an ancestor of `main`. Implement both; the ancestry form alone is insufficient.

Disposition note: PR2213 owner is `h8e3rwcgdxmggus0` on ms-dev-3. No re-land, replacement, or claim is proposed by any reporting agent. The point is only that a verified content-level absence must not be dismissed as mirror staleness, since that owner bead may read done while the file is absent from main.

## Two combined corrections from field agents (2026-07-27)

Recorded together because neither is complete without the other. Router previously attempted to append the first of these; the write returned ok=true twice without persisting, so this is a single consolidated append.

### A. Landed-test correction: content existence, not merge-commit ancestry (ms-dev-5 ln8ys7uvrmriol3i)

In a SQUASH-merge repository, testing whether a PR merge commit is an ancestor of main is an unreliable landed-test. Squash never places that commit on main, so `diverged` can be a false negative. Do not trust `compare/main...<merge_commit_oid>` alone.

Sound test is content existence at the ref:

```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/<path-the-PR-adds>?ref=main
```

404 means genuinely absent from main. Immune to squash, rebase, retarget, and mirror staleness.

Router verified independently against github.com: `docs/design/pr-cara-join-live-canary-generation4.md?ref=main` returned HTTP 404 while `commits/main` returned `12eee6c279974d2695a9273d77beefd7e1d2fc44`. Three agents on two nodes independently reported that same main sha using provider-truth methods.

Reconciliation with the reachability postcondition recorded earlier: they are complementary once the subject is precise.
1. Landed test: does PR content exist at `?ref=main`. Use this to conclude landed/unlanded.
2. Merge-target postcondition: assert the commit the merge OPERATION produced is reachable from the branch it was meant to land on. Apply to the resulting main sha, not to a PR merge-commit oid treated as an ancestor of main. This is what catches the original incident where a merge reported MERGED while landing onto the predecessor branch.

Implement both. The ancestry form alone is insufficient.

### B. Carry-forward must be ASYMMETRIC: carry PASSES only, never FAILURES

This completes the tree-oid proposal recorded above. Tree-oid identity proves content identity, so prior validation genuinely applies — but only for passes.

Rule: on merge-tree-oid match across a retarget, carry forward SUCCESSFUL required checks; DROP failures and re-run them.

Rationale, and it is logical rather than a special case: a PASS asserts a property of the CONTENT, so it transfers with identical content. A FAILURE may assert a property of the ENVIRONMENT — a closed sibling generation, a provider metadata timeout, a cancelled run — none of which are properties of the tree.

Worked example from PR2227, whose three red checks are all bogus and none examined source:

```
Changed surface admission  fail 24s  <- verdict belongs to CLOSED PR2229 sharing the head SHA (bd-b47dec)
Check & Lint               fail  6s  <- downstream of admission, compiled nothing
Fast Tests (unit)          fail  5s  <- downstream of admission, ran zero tests
```

That content genuinely has not changed, so the tree oid would match perfectly. A SYMMETRIC carry-forward rule would therefore treat a tree-identical rebase as licence to reuse those verdicts and make the false red PERMANENT. Today the only escape is that a rebase mints a new SHA and yields fresh check runs; symmetric carry-forward would remove that escape and strand correct candidates forever.

A second observed failure mode was `provider_metadata_unavailable`, a transient GitHub API failure that died in materialization before any validation ran (bd-51c6cf) — again a property of the environment, not the tree.

Cost asymmetry favours this: worst case is re-running a genuinely failing check, which is cheap relative to permanently stranding a correct candidate.

### Optional defence in depth: duration sanity check

A required check that failed in under about 10 seconds validated nothing. Observed calibration: genuine lint failure on 2210 took 3m37s; a real admission pass takes about 50s; the bogus failures above took 24s, 6s, and 5s. A sub-threshold failure is a strong signal of an environment/admission artefact rather than a content verdict.
