## LIVELOCK NOW OBSERVED, NOT PREDICTED — carry-forward is load-bearing (ms-dev-5 ln8ys7uvrmriol3i, 2026-07-27, router-verified)

Router independently verified both findings against github.com.

### 1. Main advances faster than a pipeline can complete

Actual commit timestamps on main:

```
09:05:42 39998c2396
09:11:13 e473cb91ba
09:11:34 13077396ab
09:11:45 4a0da91bd0
09:12:01 8abaf9221a
09:12:20 7524b3b9e9
09:21:45 bebbac7322
```

Six advances inside about sixteen minutes, five of them within sixty-seven seconds. (Not asserted to be six discrete pushes rather than batched commits; the CI effect is identical either way.)

Measured requirement for a full pipeline is thirty-five to forty minutes of stable head. At this cadence the head member can NEVER finish validating: each advance mints a new SHA, starts a new run, abandons the previous one. The queue therefore cannot drain, so main only moves by manual merges, which advance main and re-trigger the rebase. That is a closed livelock loop and it is now observable rather than theoretical.

PR2215 confirms it: head moved 90ce3e98bef2 -> 255db7da1c95 via retarget-rebase, invalidating everything previously reported about its runs. Current state head 255db7da1c95, mergeable MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED.

### 2. The duplicate-run pattern is systematic, not an occasional race

On the brand-new head 255db7da1c95, verified via the actions API:

```
2026-07-27T09:52:19Z run 30255739415 completed CANCELLED
2026-07-27T09:53:19Z run 30255809635 pending
```

Sixty seconds apart, same SHA, first cancelled by the second. Same shape as the previous head (07:26 cancelled, 07:33 live, seven minutes apart), reproduced IMMEDIATELY on a fresh SHA. So bd-6b6bb8 is not an occasional race: a single dispatch appears to reliably produce a doomed run plus a real one. Cost: one wasted runner slot per attempt, plus cancelled-job rows left in the rollup, which is the origin of the sub-ten-second false reds recorded earlier.

### Design consequence

This is the strongest argument yet that carry-forward on merge-tree-oid match is LOAD-BEARING rather than an optimisation. Without it, at the current main cadence the head cannot validate at all. With it, a content-identical rebase inherits its passing checks and the cycle breaks.

The asymmetry rule still governs: carry the PASSES, drop and re-run the FAILURES. That also prevents the cancelled twin runs 5s/6s/0s rows from being inherited.

Independent cheap win: if one dispatch reliably produces a cancelled twin, fixing that halves runner load and removes the main source of false red rows, independently of the carry-forward work.

## Landed-test provenance: two questions, not one (ms-dev-3 ex9vj4iedmpf8g3y, router-verified, 2026-07-27)

The `?ref=main` content-existence test recorded earlier is necessary but NOT sufficient on its own, and the failure is instructive: the same test produced two different WRONG answers about the same PR within fifteen minutes.

`?ref=main` answers "is this content on main NOW". It does not answer "did this PR land". Those diverge in two distinct situations:

1. **Closed-looking window before a sweep completes.** PR2215 sampled at 17:43:36Z appeared closed with its added files 404 on main; conclusion drawn was work loss. Wrong — it merged nine minutes later at 17:52:45Z as `cbb5de5cfb5f5015967332eafc73a289d4f56c2d`.
2. **Revert after merge.** At 17:56:57Z commit `ca0ac5362047` by Harry Askham reverted that merge, so the files were 404 again. Concluding "never landed" would also be wrong.

Correct discriminator, verified by two agents independently:

```
gh pr view N --json mergedAt,mergeCommit
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/<mergeCommit>...main --jq .status   # expect ahead/identical
```

For PR2215 this returns `ahead, ahead_by: 2, behind_by: 0`, proving the merge commit IS an ancestor of main and the PR genuinely landed before being reverted.

**Rule:** deciding whether a PR LANDED requires mergedAt + mergeCommit + ancestry of that commit against main. Content-existence at `?ref=main` then separately answers whether it is STILL there. Report both; do not collapse them into one verdict.

The reporting agent characterised this well: it is the same failure mode as stating which tree a measurement came from, in a different costume — provenance on the measurement rather than care in taking it. Both wrong answers came from a correctly-executed test answering a different question than the one asked.

Main moved `42ccf635e3` -> `cbb5de5cfb` -> `ca0ac53620` -> `c19dd0727b` inside roughly thirty minutes, so conflict scope is being re-checked rather than assumed stable.

## OPERATOR POSTURE CHANGE 2026-07-27 19:35 BST — supersedes pin/path scope, adds cron+hooks target

Operator statement: "CI is disabled on Cara Sync, cara is pinned only by flake.lock only which can be nix flake updated to get new versions, and most PRs now conflict. our posture is: remove all useless defensive checks for paths on cara etc, trust the cara we get from devshells, and for now we drive cara sync manually, and going forwards we will have a caco cron that runs cara sync with appropriate hooks that use pi agents to fix the caravans as they break"

### What is now settled, stop working on it

- **Cara version provenance: SOLVED by flake.lock.** Cara comes from the devshell; new versions arrive via `nix flake update`. The per-node `CACO_CARA_BIN` pin work is SUPERSEDED. Stop repointing pins, stop reconciling `~/.local/bin` vs `~/.nix-profile` vs `~/.cargo/bin`, stop treating multiple cara binaries on a host as a defect.
- **Defensive path/version checks are scope to DELETE, not extend.** Any code or script probing cara location, asserting a version floor, comparing resolved paths, or failing closed on path mismatch should be removed. Trust the devshell cara.
- **The 0.0.12 compatibility boundary** (0.0.7/0.0.10/0.0.11 parse-error; 0.0.12/0.0.13 compatible, verified across three nodes) was correct but is no longer actionable as pin surgery. Keep it as historical explanation of the mixed-reader outage only.
- **Cara Sync CI is disabled deliberately.** Not a fault, not to be diagnosed or repaired.

### Current interim state

Cara sync is driven MANUALLY by the operator. Most PRs now conflict; that is expected under the sweep and is not a fault. No rebasing, no replacement PRs, no re-landing, no re-arming auto-merge.

### Durable target, belongs to this bead

A **caco cron running cara sync**, with **hooks that dispatch pi agents to fix caravans as they break**. This sits alongside the Cara-owns-squash-merge and base-retargeting work already specified here rather than as a separate lane, because they solve the same problem from two directions: this bead makes landing deterministic and single-actor, and the cron+hooks make breakage self-healing instead of requiring operator intervention.

Design constraints already established here still apply to the cron path: exactly one merge actor with no provider auto-merge fallback; tree-oid carry-forward with the pass-only asymmetry rule; revalidate-or-refuse as the HOT path given main advances roughly every 45 minutes; and landed-ness determined by mergedAt + mergeCommit + ancestry, with content-existence answering only whether it is still there.

### Bead re-scoping required

`bd-c3baaf` (user-writable PATH entry silently becomes the canonical queue Cara runtime) and any CACO_CARA_BIN pin-repointing scope should be re-scoped or closed against this posture rather than implemented as written. Owners must not silently continue implementing superseded scope.

## OPERATOR SCOPE ADDITION 2026-07-27 20:26 BST — clean unwind on eviction, plus cron/hooks confirmed here

Operator: "for now cara sync should be run only by caco-ctrl to advance the queue and highlight any failures. we want eventually cara sync to be run in a cron which has hooks that trigger agents to spin up cheaply and fix the queue. For the dirty PRs that conflict with the main due to the cara stack that unwound, drop those commits. in future we need cara to cleanly unwind these on eviction"

### NEW REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR: clean unwind on eviction

When a caravan member is evicted or the stack otherwise unwinds, Cara must cleanly unwind the affected members rather than leaving them carrying inherited commits from a stack that no longer exists.

This is the ROOT FIX for a conflict class that has cost real operator time today. Concrete evidence: after the stack unwound, six of thirteen open PRs went DIRTY/CONFLICTING against main purely because they still carried inherited commits from removed predecessors. The operator had to authorize owners to manually drop those commits — a per-PR manual remedy for what should be an automatic consequence of eviction.

Requirements:
- eviction of a member must leave remaining members in a state that merges cleanly against the current default branch, or explicitly report why it cannot;
- a member must never silently retain commits belonging to an evicted or landed predecessor;
- the unwind must be observable, with receipts naming the evicted member, the affected successors, and the commits dropped from each;
- it must be idempotent and safe to re-run, and must fail closed rather than partially unwinding.

Interim manual remedy, now operator-authorized: owners of PRs conflicting due to stack inheritance may drop the inherited commits and keep only their own work. Scoped strictly to that case — not general rebasing, replacement PRs, re-landing, or re-arming auto-merge. Note `ahead_by` includes inherited commits, so it cannot be used to size a PR own contribution; PR2227 is nine commits of which six are inherited.

### Sync ownership, interim

Cara sync is run ONLY by helsinki-cacophony-caco-ctrl for now, to advance the queue and surface failures. This supersedes the earlier operator-drives-it-manually posture. The cron target recorded above remains the destination: cara sync on a caco cron whose hooks spin up cheap agents to fix the queue as it breaks.

### Related direction

Ephemeral agents are being wound down now that most PRs have landed. Longer term the operator wants pi-daemon matured in caco until it is the main agent type, which is relevant to how the cron hooks should spawn their repair agents — cheap logical agents rather than full tmux workers.

title: Publish a reusable CI-admission gate action
description:
Counterpart to cacophony/bd-5d71e6 (consumer) and cacophony/bd-52b4d2 (interim workflow fix). Caravan should own the question "is existing CI evidence still exactly valid for this PR generation" so adopting repositories do not re-derive Caravan semantics from fragile GitHub event heuristics.

Ship a reusable GitHub action plus the underlying typed command. It reads the repository-owned .caravan/config.yaml and exact provider facts (PR number, head OID, base ref/OID, merge tree, membership, labels, generation) and returns a decision other jobs can be conditional on:
- ci_valid: content-identical promotion retarget; prior head-SHA checks still apply; no re-run needed.
- ci_required: physical rebase produced a new head, or base retarget changed the merge tree; run CI, scoped to changed surface.
- ci_force_accepted: caravan-force head where the operator explicitly accepted CI state; no blocking re-run, audit preserved.
- ci_not_applicable: unenrolled or ordinary PR; Caravan has no opinion.
- ci_unknown: anything unproven; fail open to RUNNING CI, never to skipping it.

Evidence requirements: every decision names the exact facts it rests on, so a human can audit why CI was skipped. The promotion path must record tree equality between the pre- and post-retarget merge trees in its receipt, since Caravan already computes the would-be-rebase tree to choose retarget versus rebase. That receipt is the authoritative source for ci_valid.

Safety boundary, explicit: the gate is advisory about COST, never about SAFETY. It may only assert that exact existing evidence still applies; it may never assert that a head can merge without evidence. It must never report success for a head with no prior successful run, and consumers must keep required contexts reporting.

Rejected alternative, recorded: making repository CI workflow_dispatch-only and having Caravan drive which refs run when. That inverts ownership, makes the queue engine a single point of failure for all testing, and breaks CI for ordinary contributors on unenrolled PRs.

Sequence after caravan/bd-f8cf99 lands, since the promotion receipt and retarget-versus-rebase decision are its outputs.

title: Foreground loop must survive retryable ticks and provider read-after-write lag
description:
Live Cacophony dogfood: `cara loop` exited on a `rebase_stale_lease` retry_tick error after the default branch advanced mid-tick (expected 94d6ebb, actual d65aba6), and a separate `cara sync --all` aborted with `rebase_midpoint_head_stale` right after a successful force-with-lease push, leaving the caravan head with auto-merge disabled until an operator reran it. Human evidence for both was dumped as "structured evidence is too large" instead of the exact OIDs.

## Required behavior

- The unbounded foreground loop must never exit on a domain failure. Each failed tick dispatches its canonical event to configured hooks, records bounded evidence (code, disposition, wake class, retryable, next action), streams a compact operator line, and ticks again. Only an explicit stop signal ends the loop, and the summary reports total, failed, and consecutive-failure counts. `loop --once` keeps returning one typed error for schedulers, and manual mode keeps its TTY decision shell while surviving ordinary failures.
- Provider read-after-write lag must not be reported as a stale generation. After an exact proven push, verification retries the exact expected OID under a bounded attempt/delay budget, and midpoint discovery gets one bounded re-read. Any other observed generation still fails closed.
- Compact human rendering for `rebase_stale_lease`, `rebase_midpoint_head_stale`, and `rebase_midpoint_pr_missing` shows branch, expected/observed OIDs, auto-merge state, and the safe next action instead of a size-truncated JSON blob.

## Acceptance

Hermetic driver fixtures prove retryable and external-decision failures keep ticking with hook dispatch and bounded retained evidence, that retained failures stay bounded, and that a signal still stops cleanly. Live Cacophony ticks converge across default-branch movement without operator restarts.

title: Allow unique exact open PR on a historically reused branch
description:
## Live reproduction

Operator-allowlisted exact Cacophony root PR #2056 is OPEN/MERGEABLE on main at head f010ce9d267bcb79eaec01fcef1d5402213f2371. The PR head branch `repair/pr1961-tts-terminal-outcomes` is reused historical branch text but the exact open PR has no Caravan/evicted label and is intended as a fresh root.

From an exact single-branch clone, reviewed Cara v0.0.6 `new --priority-label caravan-priority:high` refuses before mutation:

- code: `historical_current_pr_missing_caravan_label`
- reason: `missing_caravan_label`
- candidates: `[2056]`

## Required behavior

- Resolve the unique exact OPEN same-repository PR for the current branch/head before classifying old branch history.
- Permit a unique open, non-draft, supported-base current head to enter fresh `new` admission even when the branch name has older merged history, provided exact head/repository identity is unambiguous and no active/evicted membership conflicts.
- Preserve fail-closed behavior for duplicate open PRs, head mismatch, forks, ambiguous branch reuse, or conflicting historical Caravan labels.
- Add CLI/JSON tests for old merged branch name reused by one new exact open PR and for ambiguous multi-PR reuse.

PR #2056 was not mutated by the refusal.

## Live PR2080 reproduction after implementation, before reviewed pin

Harry created PR #2080 from branch `fix-cara-timeouts` at 23:06 UTC while its diff was empty. The PR title was initially `release: v1.2.1562`. Cara then force-pushed head `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680` at 23:08:19, whose commit message/tree are the prior release reintegration (`release: v1.2.1562`, parent `c059bf15...`) rather than a candidate-only timeout patch. The intended `fix cara timeoutes` commit was authored only at 23:12:52, after PR creation, and subsequent rebases produced heads `829e768b`, `77199f25`, and final `2fbe7597`.

This matches the fixed reused-branch/provider-limit failure: the deployed old Cara omitted the new exact OPEN PR from its bounded open rollup, treated branch history as the source generation, and physically replayed the historical release commit instead of rejecting the empty candidate range. title: Publish a first-party Caravan CI-admission gate over promotion/merge receipts
description:
Counterpart to cacophony/bd-5d71e6. That bead needs a reusable gate that answers exactly one question -- 'is this existing CI evidence still exactly valid for this exact head/base?' -- without re-deriving Caravan semantics from GitHub event shape in workflow YAML.

bd-f8cf99 already lands the evidence this needs:
- sealed root_promotion receipts (exact head, base before/after, default branch, predecessor and its merged state, derived trigger);
- sealed root_merge receipts with the authorizing CumulativeTreeProof (candidate_tree, merge_result_tree, identical, and the exact target default-branch OID);
- physical rebase receipts for the 'new head, must re-run' case.

What is missing is the publication surface. Recommended shape: one first-party 'cara gate --pr N --json' subcommand emitting the typed decision from the same code path sync uses, with the composite action as a thin wrapper. No decision logic in YAML or JS, one implementation, one set of receipts.

Design points to settle while implementing:
- distinguish head-SHA-attached check runs (survive a retarget, because promotion never rewrites the head) from merge-ref-computed jobs (refs/pull/N/merge is recomputed on base change). The cumulative-tree proof is exactly what makes a merge-ref job provably content-identical; without it the gate must fail open to running CI.
- a proof is only valid against the exact default-branch OID it was constructed against; a moved default branch is 'unproven', never 'valid'.
- decide whether the gate should compute member-level tree proofs (currently proofs are collected for caravan roots) and price the extra merge-tree per member.
- caravan-force needs an explicit tie-break: cacophony/bd-5d71e6 asks the gate both to report success for required contexts and never to report success for a head with no prior successful run. A forced head must surface a visibly distinct forced conclusion, never a plain green indistinguishable from a real pass.

Do not implement inside bd-f8cf99: that bead is complete as the landing contract, and this is an additive publication surface.

title: Cara join must reject or sync stale tail before replaying source commits
description:
## Live reproduction

Operator joined Cacophony branch `fix-cara-timeouts` to stale caravan tail/root PR #2079 (`fix-slackiq-nodes`). Cara produced child PR #2080:

- PR: https://github.com/harryaskham/cacophony/pull/2080
- Base/tail: `fix-slackiq-nodes` at `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3` (PR #2079)
- Head: `fix-cara-timeouts` at `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633`
- Label: `caravan`
- Head is diverged from true main: ahead 3, behind 1.

PR #2080 contains two commits:

1. `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680` — `release: v1.2.1562`, rebased onto stale tail `c059bf15`.
2. `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633` — the operator's actual `fix cara timeoutes` commit.

True main already contains the release as distinct commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7`, parented on main `80bf4eac`, with tree `b54319dc`. Cara replayed that already-main release delta into the child because the selected tail was stale. Consequently PR #2080 includes unrelated `CHANGELOG.md`, `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock` release changes alongside the intended `.caravan/config.yaml` change. Initial PR title/body also came from the replayed release/update-helper commit rather than the unique source commit; the operator subsequently corrected the metadata manually.

Provider events show force-pushes as the branch was materialized. Preserve PR #2080 and branch/event evidence until diagnosis is complete.

## Expected behavior

Before any rewrite, push, PR creation/update, or enrollment, Cara join must prove the selected caravan root/tail is current with the configured base or otherwise has a safe, explicit sync plan. Joining a branch based on newer main to a stale tail must never silently absorb missing-main commits into the child.

Cara must either:

- transactionally sync/rebase the caravan root/tail to current main and then replay only the source branch's unique commits/patch; or
- fail closed with an exact stale-root decision before provider mutation.

Join planning/apply must receipt-bind source repo/branch/head/parent/tree/patch identity, selected caravan/root/tail heads, configured base head, and expected resulting tree. Apply must revalidate all identities and verify the published child contains exactly the unique source patch. PR title/body provenance must come from the intended source commit/operator metadata, never an absorbed main/release commit.

## Regression fixtures

- A source branch based on newer main joining a stale one-PR caravan tail: assert no missing-main commit is replayed into the child.
- Root-current-main invariant drift between preview/apply: fail before push/PR/label mutation.
- Unique source commit plus unrelated release commit already on main: resulting child contains only the unique source patch and uses its title/body provenance.
- Empty unique source patch after subtracting current-main ancestry: return an explicit no-op and perform zero provider mutations.

## Safety

Do not merge PR #2080 in its current form: it duplicates main's release delta and is based on stale non-main ancestry. Do not close, retarget, join again, or otherwise mutate it while preserving the reproduction evidence.

## Canonical Cara 0.0.6 graph and audit evidence

Read-only `cara status --json` with released 0.0.6 confirms:

- active caravan id/root `2079`, members `[2079, 2080]`;
- configured default branch observation `main@d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7`;
- PR2079 root `main@80bf4eac -> fix-slackiq-nodes@c059bf15`, auto-merge armed;
- PR2080 child `fix-slackiq-nodes@c059bf15 -> fix-cara-timeouts@21097975`, auto-merge disabled;
- PR2080 synthetic merge/tree `0bd617a166018d3f2c9b949fa67e9cbd746ecc01` / `4413f2fa0dc545e8df41671b8cad6a72a2d7a0ac`;
- compatibility reports both stale-root-to-current-main and child-to-tail as mechanically clean, demonstrating that clean mergeability alone failed to enforce root-current-main ancestry/provenance.

The same released binary's `cara log --pr 2080 --limit 100 --json` returns zero matching records even though provider history records the branch force-push and caravan label. Therefore no durable operation receipt is discoverable from the canonical journal for this mutation. The fix must also guarantee a durable preview/apply operation receipt for join attempts, including no-op/refusal outcomes and every provider mutation identity, so this class of provenance failure is auditable without reconstructing it from GitHub events.

## Merged duplicate: bd-0fe6ad

Title: Reject Cara join when candidate patch already landed on default branch

## Live reproduction

While joining Cacophony PR #2080 (`fix-cara-timeouts`) to an active caravan, Cara physically rebased an already-landed release patch onto caravan tail `fix-slackiq-nodes` and enrolled the result instead of rejecting it as already present on the default branch.

Exact observed generations:

- default branch `main`: `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7` (`release: v1.2.1562`), parent `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`
- caravan tail/base: `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, also parented by `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`
- rewritten PR head: `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680`, parented by the caravan tail
- `git patch-id --stable` for both the main commit and rewritten PR commit: `c8c875993b7fed870c2082837caea490559260e2`
- PR #2080 was force-updated to the rewritten head at 23:08:19Z and then labelled `caravan` at 23:08:56Z.

The rewritten PR therefore contains a patch already integrated on exact current `main`. Its diff against the caravan tail is the release patch, while its diff against current main consists only of unrelated caravan-tail drift. The operator described the source PR as empty/already landed before join.

## Gap

`physical_rebase.rs` rejects `commit_count == 0` relative to the candidate's old provider base (`rebase_empty_patch_range`), but does not reject a non-empty candidate range whose stable patch identity/content is already present on the exact default-branch generation. Rebasing that range onto a stale caravan tail resurrects an already-landed change as a new PR commit.

## Required contract

Before a physical join rewrite or enrollment, compare the candidate-only patch range with the exact current default branch and fail closed when every candidate patch is already represented there (stable patch-id and tree/content proof, with ambiguity rejected). Return a typed `already_landed`/empty-effective-diff decision and do not rewrite the head, retarget, label, or enroll the PR.

Add a fixture for sibling histories from one merge base where branch A's patch has already landed on default and joining branch A onto branch B's caravan tail would otherwise replay that patch. Preserve ordinary joining when the candidate has genuinely new effective content.

## Merged duplicate: bd-915573

Title: Cara empty-diff join replays another reintegration patch onto caller branch

Operator reproduction on 2026-07-21 exposed cross-reintegration patch contamination while joining Cacophony branch `fix-cara-timeouts` into the active Caravan/Cara tail. The intended operator change was `fix cara timeoutes`, but before that commit was added, Cara/Cacophony synthesized daemon-authored commit `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680` on `fix-cara-timeouts` with the complete, unrelated update-helper `release: v1.2.1562` patch and release-agent provenance.

Exact evidence:

- True GitHub `main` independently and correctly contains release commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7`, parent `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`; annotated tag `v1.2.1562` peels to it.
- The active Cara tail/base branch `fix-slackiq-nodes` is `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`, also parented by `80bf4eac` and carrying the separate `fix ms agent scope` patch.
- Cara-created/reused PR https://github.com/harryaskham/cacophony/pull/2080 targets `fix-slackiq-nodes` from `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- Its first commit is `ac701198`, parent `c059bf15`, authored by Cacophony Daemon at 23:04:11Z. Its title/body were initially `release: v1.2.1562` and copied update-helper identity/head `e3026e0461`, despite the operator working on `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- `ac701198` contains only the unrelated release metadata patch (`Cargo.toml`, twenty workspace entries in `Cargo.lock`, and `CHANGELOG.md`). It is a duplicate replay of the patch already landed on true main as `d9fad17e`.
- The operator's intended `fix cara timeoutes` commit `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633` was subsequently added on top of the contaminated release commit; live PR 2080 therefore now contains both `.caravan/config.yaml` and the unrelated release patch.

The operator reports Cara first observed an empty diff while he was on `fix-cara-timeouts`, then created PR 2080 and inferred/replayed the diff from main to the Caravan tail. An empty caller patch must never fall back to another agent's most recent reintegration patch, global generation, main-to-tail delta, or stale receipt.

Required behavior:

- Bind join materialization to the exact caller owner, source branch/head, expected base/tail, and patch identity receipt.
- If the caller's patch against the selected tail is empty, return an explicit empty/no-op/refusal receipt; do not mutate the caller branch and do not create a PR.
- Refuse when receipt owner/head/patch differs from the branch being joined, even if a recent reintegration has a reusable-looking diff or commit message.
- Preserve the caller branch on any ambiguity and surface exact candidate provenance for diagnosis.
- Add a regression test with two concurrent patches: release patch A lands on main while operator branch B joins an active tail with an initially empty diff; B must never receive A.

Do not mutate or close PR 2080 as part of triage; preserve it as live evidence until the owner chooses repair.

## Operator clarification

The initiating `fix-cara-timeouts` PR/branch was believed to have no effective diff. The suspected failure mode is therefore earlier than duplicate-patch replay alone: candidate range inference selected the immediately preceding release commit when the intended source branch was empty, then physical rebase replayed that inferred commit onto the caravan tail.

The fix must first prove the intended provider PR's exact base/head range and reject an empty effective source diff without borrowing a predecessor commit. The already-landed-on-default check remains a necessary independent backstop, because the inferred release commit was already represented on current `main`.

Duplicate investigation signal merged from bd-6f3cc3: live canary independently identified the same stale-root physical-rebase shape and adds explicit empty/no-unique-change PR refusal plus already-main patch-equivalence/drop acceptance. Canonical bd-35e822 remains the sole P0 under MSM0; do not implement separately.

## Post-reproduction provider repair

Later provider topology was manually repaired without closing the bug:

- PR2079/root was force-updated to `570e26ea`, parented on release main `d9fad17e`; root squash auto-merge is armed.
- PR2080/child was updated to `829e768b`, parent `570e26ea`, containing only the intended timeout commit/diff.
- The absorbed `ac701198` release delta is no longer present in the live child diff.

This repairs the live unsafe topology but does not erase the reproduced Cara defect. Preserve the original force-push/label event history, exact old heads/trees, zero-record `cara log` result, and regression requirements above. The fix must prevent the initial stale-tail absorption and provide durable operation receipts; a later manual topology correction is not proof of correct join behavior.

## Subsequent root movement clarification

A later read after the initial repair observed PR2079 head advanced again from `570e26ea` to `889dfe2779c72f39306ce5e43a364d17c424bb4a`, a merge commit `Merge branch 'main' into fix-slackiq-nodes` with parents `570e26ea` and `6764c4c2`. PR2080 remains at intended-only commit `829e768b`, parent `570e26ea`, while its provider base branch now resolves to PR2079 head `889dfe27`. This later movement does not change the original defect or evidence; it further demonstrates why join/apply receipts must bind exact root/tail/base heads and fail or explicitly resync on drift rather than relying on branch names.

## Descendant invalidation gap after root movement

Canonical `caco agent merge-queue list` / Cara projection later reported `healthy=true` with both candidates fresh after the root branch moved:

- PR2079/root head `889dfe27` is a merge of prior repaired root `570e26ea` plus current main `6764c4c2`.
- PR2080/child remains head `829e768b`, parent/provider-base OID `570e26ea`; its synthetic merge still records parents `[570e26ea, 829e768b]`.
- `compare 889dfe27...829e768b` is diverged; the child is behind the live root by two commits and their merge base is historical root `570e26ea`.
- Despite that branch-name/base-OID mismatch, projection marks PR2080 `stale_base=false`, `stale_head=false`, and a merge candidate.

Acceptance must enforce descendant invalidation/cascade: whenever a caravan root or intermediate member advances, Cara must transactionally cascade/rebase every descendant to the new exact parent, or mark the caravan invalid/paused before any merge candidate can proceed. Status and merge-queue projection must compare each child's recorded provider base OID with the live parent branch head and must never report healthy/fresh/mergeable from a historical base OID after that branch moved. Add fixtures for root force-update and root merge-update with an unchanged child, including drift between discovery and apply.

## Root-advance false-healthy evidence (2026-07-22)

After the repaired root PR #2079 advanced again to `889dfe27`, child PR #2080 remained based on prior root `570e26ea` with head `829e768b`. Read-only ancestry comparison reports diverged and child two commits behind root, while released Cara's canonical projection still reports `healthy=true`.

Acceptance must therefore cover root advancement after enrollment: descendants must be transactionally rebased/cascaded with durable receipts, or canonical status must fail closed with exact root/child ancestry evidence. A diverged descendant must never remain false-healthy. PRs were left untouched and PR #2078 remains held.

## Eventual descendant-cascade recovery receipt

Provider topology was subsequently corrected again:

- PR2080 head `77199f2597` now targets live root/base OID `889dfe2779`.
- `compare 889dfe2779...77199f2597` reports ahead 1, behind 0.
- The child contains only the intended `fix cara timeoutes` commit, parented directly on `889dfe2779`.

This is the desired eventual descendant-cascade topology and repairs the later false-healthy historical-base state. Preserve it as a recovery receipt, not evidence that the original join was safe: the initial stale-tail release absorption, provider mutations without a journal record, and intermediate projection that reported a historical-base child fresh/healthy all remain the reproduced defects. Regression acceptance must prove this exact cascade occurs transactionally or the caravan is marked invalid before status/merge eligibility.

Additional live topology failure 2026-07-21: root PR2079 merged as fe68beb5 at 23:41:52Z. Descendant PR2080 remains OPEN, base branch fix-slackiq-nodes at merged root head889dfe27, label caravan, auto-merge absent. It was not retargeted/promoted to main as new root and now blocks new normal joins. Ordinary PR2082 published_unjoined immediately afterward with provider_mutated_by_cara=false. Acceptance addition: root merge must transactionally promote/retarget the first child to current main, preserve ancestry, enable head auto-merge, update membership/journal/status, and leave later joins unblocked; crash/reconcile must repair this exact partial state.

## Root-merge promotion receipt and missing head intent

After PR2079 merged as `fe68beb5` at 2026-07-21T23:41:52Z, Cara eventually promoted/retargeted PR2080 correctly:

- base is `main` at exact OID `fe68beb5`;
- head is `2fbe7597`, one intended commit directly parented on `fe68beb5`;
- the prior stale root-branch base is gone;
- PR2080 still carries the `caravan` label, but `autoMergeRequest=null` and provider merge state is `BLOCKED`.

Thus root-merge descendant promotion eventually cascaded ancestry correctly, but failed to establish the promoted member's new head intent. Acceptance: promotion/reconcile/sync must atomically retarget/rebase the descendant, verify its exact intended patch/tree, promote it to caravan head, and arm configured squash auto-merge in the same receipt-bound operation. A promoted head with caravan membership but no auto-merge must be classified invalid/actionable, never healthy or complete. Add idempotent recovery fixtures for provider success after partial retarget, partial rebase, label-only state, and missing auto-merge, with drift refusal and rollback/audit receipts.

## Immediate terminal-state clarification

An independent provider read immediately after the promotion snapshot observed PR2080 already `MERGED`, not still open/blocked: head `2fbe7597`, base `main`, intended-only commit/diff, with post-merge `autoMergeRequest=null` and merge-state `UNKNOWN`. Therefore the earlier open `BLOCKED`/null-auto-merge observation was a real intermediate partial state that subsequently converged to merge. Preserve its timestamped receipt as a transient atomicity/reconciliation gap; do not describe it as the current terminal state. Acceptance remains: Cara must either arm head intent atomically during promotion or explicitly classify and reconcile the partial state with durable receipts, so an observer never treats the intermediate caravan-label/null-auto-merge state as healthy or terminal.

Post-land duplicate audit correction: initial 36a491b covers stale-root and source-range provenance but not the merged duplicate requirement where an equivalent patch already exists on current main under a different commit OID. Reopened canonically to add stable patch/content subtraction before final closure.

Live follow-up regression: plain/new root admission without an explicit --pr can enter source-provenance preflight with status.current_pr=None and current_branch=main, producing misleading join_empty_source_noop against main. Restore early operation-shape validation: existing admission requires --pr/current PR; --create-pr requires a non-default topic branch. No source/no-op receipt may be synthesized from main.

title: Accept a backtick-quoted Beads declaration and name the exact PRs in fleet problem rows
description:
`parse_beads` rejects a backtick-quoted `Beads:` declaration that `metadata_value` would accept, so one quoted body invalidates its whole generation. Because the resulting problem is repository-wide and the human-readable renderer drops `problem.prs`, that single body prints an identical `InvalidGenerationMetadata` row on every unrelated candidate's `cara check`, which reads as fleet-wide breakage.

## Exact mechanism

`parse_generation_fact` resolves the five `Cacophony-*` trailers through `metadata_value`, which unquotes a backtick-wrapped value. `parse_beads` does not unquote its tokens, so it filters on a raw `` `bd-74b155` `` that cannot `strip_prefix("bd-")`. The bead set comes back empty, `missing.push("Beads")` fires, and the generation is invalid even though every other field parsed exactly.

Cacophony PR #2215 is a hand-authored recovery body that quotes its bead list to match the surrounding `Agent:`/`Branch:` prose:

    Beads: `bd-74b155`

Every other open generation body publishes the plain form and parses correctly.

## Why it read as fleet-wide

`read.rs` pushes generation findings onto `fleet.problems`, which is repository-scoped. `cara check --pr <any>` therefore prints #2215's row regardless of which candidate was asked about. The three human-readable renderers in `main.rs` formatted only `{kind}: {message}` and dropped `problem.prs`, so nothing on screen attributed the row to #2215. The JSON envelope was always correct (`.data.problems[].prs == [2215]`).

Three independent Cacophony agents concluded from that output that every generation PR was failing metadata parsing, and a P1 blocker was filed against the wrong side of the contract. Verified by reproduction: `cara check --pr 2233 --json` returns `prs: [2215]` while the text row names no PR at all.

## Fix

1. `parse_beads` unquotes each token before validating it, so plain, per-token-quoted, and whole-list-quoted declarations all resolve to the same ids. Already-open plain bodies are unaffected; a declaration naming no well-formed bead is still incomplete.
2. All three `main.rs` problem renderers share one helper that names the exact PRs, so a repository-wide row can no longer read as a defect in the candidate the operator asked about.

Filed from Cacophony bd-e4dbcb, where the symptom was first reported. No PR body was mutated, and no generation was retargeted, merged, or replaced.

title: Resolve Git repository root before config discovery and init
description:
Operator reproduction: invoking Cara from a nested directory inside a Git repository reports the repository as uninitialized and then attempts to create `.caravan/` in that nested working directory. Cara currently binds `AppContext.repository_path` and the default `.caravan/config.yaml` to ambient cwd instead of the canonical worktree root.

Resolve the exact repository/worktree root before default config discovery and every Git/GitHub/domain operation (for example, a bounded `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` contract). Default `.caravan/config.yaml`, common Git metadata, operation locks, repairs, status cache identity, dashboard repository IDs, and init writes must consistently use that root. Explicit `--config PATH` remains explicit: define whether relative overrides resolve from invocation cwd or canonical root, preserve the documented contract, and reject symlink/path escape where existing safety requires it.

Acceptance:
- From root and multiple nested subdirectories, `cara status`, `init`, `sync`, navigation, lock, log, web/action context, and JSON/MCP resolve one identical repository/config identity.
- Nested `cara init` creates only `<root>/.caravan/config.yaml`, never `<cwd>/.caravan`.
- Outside Git returns a typed repository-not-found/config continuation and writes nothing.
- Linked worktrees resolve their own worktree root while shared common-Git state remains common where intended.
- Bare repository, symlinked cwd/config, relative and absolute explicit config overrides, `-C`/environment edge cases, and paths containing spaces are covered.
- Root discovery is bounded, noninteractive, secret-free, and occurs before mutation.
- Focused fixtures, CLI/JSON/MCP parity, strict Clippy/fmt, full configured tests, docs/help.

title: Add bounded greedy caravan growth mode to cara sync
description:

title: cara sync --all NO-OPS on empty caravan - cron must call ADMISSION verb new/join then sync - checkout-free via --pr - admission ONLY when caravans=0
description:
Continuation of bd-f8cf99, which is at the ~8000-char description cap (cacophony/bd-48d9c1) and can no longer accept appends. This analysis was lost FOUR times to that cap before being filed here.

## First live evidence from the operator 10-minute ticker (ms-mac, 2026-07-28)

Operator ran: while true; do cara sync --all; sleep 600; done

Observed candidate order and states:

    pos 1  #2216  DIRTY     <- the actual head
    pos 2  #2223  BLOCKED
    pos 3  #2227  BLOCKED
    pos 4  #2234  DIRTY
    pos 5  #2245  DIRTY
    pos 6  #2254  CLEAN
    pos 7  #2255  CLEAN

Cara processes IN ORDER, so the only two MERGEABLE candidates sat sixth and seventh behind five unmergeable members. The ticker faithfully re-confirmed every ten minutes that the head could not move, and landed NOTHING.

Confirmation: last merge PR2251 at 19:20:56Z, main head unchanged at 923c05cfb7 from 21:26:41Z, board byte-identical before and after the loop started.

## Design consequence: more frequent sync CANNOT fix this

DIRTY is a merge conflict and no amount of syncing resolves a conflict. The queue was never starved of sync passes; it was starved of REPAIR.

That makes the repair-agent HOOKS the load-bearing half of the cron target, not the timer. The correct trigger is not "time has passed" but "the head of the queue is unmergeable", and the correct hook action is to repair or evict THAT SPECIFIC MEMBER.

Requirements this adds:

- detect HEAD-OF-LINE STALL specifically, distinguishing "nothing to do" from "cannot proceed past member N"
- report WHICH member blocks and WHY; DIRTY and BLOCKED need different remedies (conflict repair vs check failure)
- escalate after N identical no-progress passes rather than re-confirming forever
- offer EVICTION as a remedy, not only repair, which ties directly to the clean-unwind-on-eviction scope on bd-f8cf99

## Second-order lesson: QUEUE ORDER, not notice order

The tempting first move was PR2245: the only member with a repair already built and unpushed, and itself the bd-c04d9b fix that removes the cancelled-producer stall mechanism. But repairing position 5 changes nothing while position 1 is DIRTY.

Any repair-hook implementation must select work by QUEUE POSITION, not by which member is cheapest or most attractive to fix. A hook that greedily fixes the easiest DIRTY member would burn effort without ever moving the head.

## No receipts makes failure indistinguishable from success

Router could see the queue was not moving but could not tell whether the loop had died, was failing every pass, or was succeeding-but-blocked. Process inspection found no cara sync process at all and still could not discriminate. The correct diagnosis came from reasoning about ORDERING, not from any signal the loop emitted.

Concrete argument for per-pass receipts: a bare loop makes total failure and quiet success look identical from outside.

## Head disposition note

PR2216 (bd-b5d189) measured ahead 2, behind 43-44 against main 923c05cfb7, carrying only two own commits across SPEC.md and three hot caco crate files. That is neither a stale base nor a one-file collision; rebase, RECREATE or evict are all plausible and it is a bigger decision than the others. Escalated to the operator as the sole critical path.

## SUPERSEDING FINDING: the head-of-line analysis above was WRONG. The real cause was the VERB.

Recorded here rather than replacing the text above, because the earlier analysis is honest evidence of how the failure looked from outside and is worth preserving as such. But do not design from it.

### What actually happened

The operator loop ran `cara sync --all` every ten minutes for three and a half hours and moved nothing, while reporting healthy.

Cara reported: `caravans: []`, `unqueued: [2216, 2223, 2227, 2234, 2245, 2254, 2255, 2257, 2258, 2259]`, `merge_candidates: []`, `problems: 0`, `healthy: true`.

From cara 0.0.13 help, verbatim:

    sync   "Idempotently synchronize one or all caravans until a decision point"
    --all  "Synchronize every caravan rather than only the current branch's caravan"

With zero caravans there is nothing to iterate. `sync --all` synchronized an EMPTY SET and correctly reported success.

### Membership verbs are separate and were never invoked

    new      "Create a one-PR caravan from the current branch"
    join     "Append the current PR after a caravan tail"
    renew    "Reevaluate an evicted PR as a new caravan"
    rejoin   "Reevaluate and append an evicted PR after a caravan tail"

`sync` ADVANCES. It cannot CREATE. A timer calling only `sync` can never start a queue.

### THE REQUIREMENT THIS ADDS TO THE CRON DESIGN

**The cron must invoke an ADMISSION verb, not bare `sync`.** Otherwise it reproduces exactly this failure: a loop that runs forever, reports healthy, emits no problems, and accomplishes nothing.

Specifically the cron must:

- detect `caravans == 0` with `unqueued > 0` as a distinct state requiring ADMISSION, not synchronization
- invoke the admission verb (`new` for the FIFO head, then `join` for successors) under whatever authority the design grants it
- treat "synchronized successfully, zero caravans, N unqueued" as an ALERT condition, not a healthy tick

### Why no receipts made this cost hours

Four agents watched the stall. None could tell whether the loop had died, was failing, or was succeeding-but-empty, because every observable signal said healthy. The correct diagnosis came from reading the binary HELP TEXT, not from any signal the system emitted.

A per-pass receipt naming the verb invoked, the caravan count before and after, and the unqueued count would have made this obvious on the first tick.

### Admission itself was never broken

`cara next-candidate --json` returned status=success with generation_integrity confirmed for 2216, 2223, 2227, 2234 and 2245, FIFO-ordered by immutable provider `created_at`, 2216 first at 2026-07-26T18:41:20Z. Cara knew exactly who to admit and refused nobody.

Full detail on cacophony/bd-1764a1.

## THE DURABLE CRON SHAPE IS AVAILABLE TODAY - no Cara change required

Found by helsinki:unknown:harry, verified independently by the router against cara 0.0.13 `--help` on ms-mac.

### The obvious objection, and why it is unfounded

Admission LOOKS checkout-bound: `new` says "from the current branch", `join` says "the current PR". A central cron has neither.

But both verbs support CHECKOUT-FREE admission by exact PR number. Verbatim from the binary:

    cara new  --pr <PR>        "Exact remote candidate PR for checkout-free root admission"
    cara join --pr <PR>        "Exact remote candidate PR. Required for checkout-free atomic integration"
    cara join --tail-pr <PR>   "Exact tail PR to use as the proposed merge target"
    cara join --head-pr <PR>   "Caravan head PR; resolve its current tail immediately before mutation"
    both:     --reason <TEXT>  "Human/agent admission rationale; otherwise a deterministic mechanical reason is used"
    new:      --priority-label "Exact configured agent-priority label. Without it, admission is FIFO"

### The three-step shape a cron can perform with no checkout

1. read `cara next-candidate --json` for the canonical FIFO head
2. if `caravans == 0`: `cara new --pr <head> --reason <automated admission receipt>`
   else: `cara join --pr <candidate> --head-pr <current head> --reason ...`
3. `cara sync --all` to advance

No working tree, no current branch, no PATH guessing once `runtime_bin` is pinned. Each step returns a structured envelope, which is exactly the hook surface needed to trigger a repair agent at a decision point.

### REQUIREMENT for whoever implements

`--reason` MUST carry the automated actor identity and the tick number, so an admission receipt is distinguishable from a human one after the fact. Membership is currently reserved by the Cara holds; if the cron and an operator both admit, the audit trail must be able to tell them apart. Without that, receipts cannot answer "who admitted this".

Note `--head-pr` explicitly "resolve its current tail immediately before mutation", which is the re-derive-at-moment-of-action discipline already built into the verb. Use it rather than caching a tail.

### Also confirmed

`--priority-label` exists if ordering ever needs to be explicit rather than FIFO. Not needed today; `next-candidate` already returns a correct FIFO order by immutable provider `created_at` with PR-number tie-break.

## RESOLVED: the loop was never running. Joining is AUTOMATIC and needs no admission verb.

Two findings that together collapse this bead. Both established 2026-07-28 ~03:47Z.

### 1. JOINING WAS NEVER AN AGENT ACTION

caco-ctrl established this against their own earlier position, from `.caravan/config.yaml` at main 923c05cf:

    line  5   rebase_on_join: true
    line 14   sync.actions.join_unlabelled_prs: TRUE
    line 30   join_failed hook -> ./scripts/cara-hook

**Cara joins unlabelled PRs BY ITSELF during sync.** No `cara new`, no `cara join`, no membership verb, no hold to lift.

So the extensive reasoning on this bead and elsewhere about admission verbs, membership holds, and who is authorized to admit was reasoning about a lane THAT DOES NOT GATE JOINING. The canary never needed `caco agent complete` either.

### 2. THE OPERATOR SYNC LOOP WAS NOT RUNNING AT ALL

Router checked `pgrep -f "cara sync"` and `ps aux` at 00:41, 02:00 and 04:46 — three times across four hours. NEVER PRESENT.

The `while true; do cara sync --all; sleep 600; done` announced at 00:51 produced ZERO ticks, not twenty. A bare shell loop dies with its terminal.

### The version hypothesis was tested and REFUTED

caco-ctrl hypothesised the loop might resolve a cara below the 0.0.12 config floor and die at 0s per tick, matching the three dark Linux nodes. Router tested from BOTH the agent shell and a stripped login shell approximating the operator PATH:

    command -v cara  -> /Users/harryaskham/.cargo/bin/cara
    cara --version   -> cara 0.0.13        (parses this config)

PATH order puts /usr/local/bin, /System/Cryptexes/App/usr/bin, /usr/bin, /bin first — none contain cara — and `~/.cargo/bin` precedes `~/.nix-profile/bin`.

**ms-mac is NOT a fourth dark node.** The binary was always correct.

### The join_failed hook avenue is empty

No ticks ran, so no join was ever attempted, so the hook never fired and has nothing recorded.

## THE ENTIRE REMEDY

Restart the sync loop under something that survives terminal close — launchd, tmux, nohup. Joins should begin on the first tick with no further action.

No membership decision. No hold lifted. No admission verb. No queue defect.

## What this bead should now carry forward

The DURABLE requirement is unchanged and is now better evidenced: a bare `while` loop is not a supervision strategy. The cron design needs process supervision AND per-pass receipts, because four agents spent hours unable to distinguish "loop running and refusing" from "loop absent" — and the answer was the second.

title: Bind caravan-force intent to the exact head generation
description:
Architecture review found one important force-generation gap for deterministic join/sync.

Existing protections are good: membership join removes caravan-force rather than adding/carrying it as a control label; force executes only for a non-successful explicitly labelled head; graph/compatibility and physical-rebase preflight happen first; force re-verifies exact default OID, open/non-draft state, label presence, ADMIN, durable audit comment, non-head auto-merge disable, and exact provider precondition. Routine pr_cara_join must expose no force input and its receipt should prove force absent/removed.

Gap: with rebase_on_join=true, sync physically rewrites a head, rediscovers it, and then evaluates CI in the same tick. An old caravan-force label survives the head-SHA rewrite. Checks on the new generation are initially empty, so the old label can immediately force-merge the newly rewritten generation even if operator intent was attached to the prior SHA. The existing passing-with-stale-force test does not cover this rewrite transition. This weakens stale-head/operator-only semantics.

Required contract: bind force intent to an exact observed head generation (durable comment/marker or equivalent). Any Cara-owned head rewrite must consume/remove or invalidate pre-rewrite force intent; force after rewrite requires a fresh operator action on the new SHA. Add tests for forced-old-generation + physical rebuild + empty checks, stale force label during pr_cara_join, and explicit re-application on the new generation. Keep force absent from healthy sync/join receipts except an explicit invalidation/removal step.

Implementation landed true main at 35c08e6 (reintegration attempt r3jo86y5v9h80nf2-20260719T101948.863Z-26c489eb). Sync removes/audits old-generation caravan-force only after the complete global physical write barrier; membership now prepare_candidate first, then invalidates/audits stale force, then apply_prepared, so planning conflicts consume no intent. Already-satisfied exact generations preserve intent; rewritten generations require a fresh label. Composed with atomic join 780ac5d JoinReceipt. Focused atomic join/force/reapplication tests and strict all-target Clippy passed; prior full suite passed before the one-commit atomic-join rebase. Lifecycle finalization is blocked only by Caco invoking a nonexistent claude-plugin before_complete hook for this Pi worker despite refresh/reload; controller repair requested. Do not manually close; retry caco agent complete after hook resolution.

title: Add optional cumulative rebase mode for physically chained caravans
description:
Operator-directed design/implementation lane. Add strict repository config `rebase_on_join: false` (safe default). When true, Caravan represents a chain both in GitHub PR bases and in Git ancestry so head A is based on exact default, joining B contains only B's patch rebased onto exact A, joining C is rebased onto exact B, and CI on each member validates cumulative A, A+B, A+B+C content.

This mode is explicit history rewriting, not the current virtual compatibility-only contract. Implement with isolated temporary worktrees, exact remote OID fetches, no caller-worktree mutation, full conflict simulation before the first provider write, same-repository/owned-branch and push-permission preflight, and exact `git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<old-oid>`. Rediscover after every push/base mutation and return old/new head OIDs plus provider receipts. Never force a branch that moved or whose patch range is ambiguous/nonlinear unless a documented safe merge-preserving strategy exists.

Membership: `new` rebases the candidate-only series onto the exact current default; `join`/`rejoin` rebase candidate-only commits from its exact old base/merge-base onto the selected parent before setting the GitHub base. Sync must detect parent OID movement and cascade child-only rebases head→tail under exact leases. Eviction of B from A→B→C must preflight and perform `C --onto A B` (and cascade later descendants) so B content is actually dropped; falling back to the old base while retaining B's patch is not a successful eviction. Split at B must transplant B-only commits onto main and cascade descendants. Any conflict or ambiguous range is a typed resumable decision with zero speculative push.

Preserve current `rebase_on_join=false` behavior and SPEC compatibility. Add interruption/replay, stale lease, merge commit, signed commit, parent update, cascading descendants, evict middle/head/tail, split, conflict, and partial provider failure tests. Live-prove using clearly named disposable PRs on harryaskham/caravan only; do not use Cacophony fixtures. Verify CI trees are cumulative and attach exact tree/OID receipts.

Important limitation to document/test: because current heads squash-merge, retargeting B after A lands can still change GitHub merge-ref/check identity and trigger provider CI even when cumulative tree content is already proven. This mode improves semantic cumulative testing but must not claim instant no-rerun landing until an ancestry-preserving merge mode or audited exact-tree/check receipt policy is implemented.

CI trigger requirement discovered on live Cacophony chain: PR #1991 targets main and has CI; rebased child #1972 targets #1991's `agent/...` branch and has no checks because `.github/workflows/ci.yml` filters `pull_request.branches: [main]`. Rebase mode must preflight/report a compatible workflow trigger contract: CI pull_request must include all possible caravan parent base branches (e.g. remove the main-only filter or include `agent/**`/configured head patterns), and include the `edited` action because changing a PR base emits an edited event; current explicit types omit it. Ensure the post-rebase/base-update event runs on the correct cumulative merge ref. Add fixtures proving A(main), B(agent/A), C(agent/B) each receive the required check. For cumulative semantic proof, use an unfiltered dedicated Caravan stack check/full suite rather than path-skipping required checks. Fail closed with actionable config evidence when required CI cannot trigger on a non-main parent.

CI integration requirement discovered from live Cacophony chain #1991→#1972: GitHub Actions `pull_request.branches` filters the PR base. Repositories whose validation workflows trigger only for `main` will not run CI on downstream members based on another PR branch, so rebase_on_join cannot deliver cumulative validation by itself. Preflight/status must detect absent downstream expected checks and return a typed repository-policy decision with guidance. Documentation/acceptance must require validation workflows to trigger all Caravan base branches (or configured branch patterns) while deployment/release remains main-only. Live Caravan proof must confirm each downstream PR receives its required CI. Checks from a non-main merge ref still do not transfer after retarget/squash; retain the existing limitation.

CI trigger requirement discovered on live Cacophony chain: PR #1991 targets main and has CI; rebased child #1972 targets #1991's `agent/...` branch and has no checks because `.github/workflows/ci.yml` filters `pull_request.branches: [main]`. Rebase mode must preflight/report a compatible workflow trigger contract: CI pull_request must include all possible caravan parent base branches (e.g. remove the main-only filter or include `agent/**`/configured head patterns), and include the `edited` action because changing a PR base emits an edited event; current explicit types omit it. Ensure the post-rebase/base-update event runs on the correct cumulative merge ref. Add fixtures proving A(main), B(agent/A), C(agent/B) each receive the required check. For cumulative semantic proof, use an unfiltered dedicated Caravan stack check/full suite rather than path-skipping required checks. Fail closed with actionable config evidence when required CI cannot trigger on a non-main parent.

Operator-selected CI setup: GitHub Actions cannot filter `on.pull_request.branches` by PR label; that field matches the base branch. Recommended label-gated contract is an unfiltered `pull_request` trigger with types including opened/synchronize/reopened/edited/labeled/unlabeled, then job-level `if` running the stack/full check when base is main OR the PR has the `caravan` label. Thus ordinary main PRs and labelled non-main caravan children run, while unrelated non-main PR jobs skip. Rebase mode must inspect workflow/config and emit a clear project-configuration warning/error (`rebase_ci_trigger_missing`) with remediation when non-main parent bases cannot produce the configured stack check. `cara init/status/check` should surface readiness; sync must not treat an empty child check set as evidence CI passed.

Operator CI contract clarification: GitHub cannot event-filter by PR label and branches have no Caravan tag. Supported pattern is pull_request with no branches filter and types including opened,synchronize,reopened,ready_for_review,edited,labeled,unlabeled; job-level heavy-suite condition checks pull_request label caravan. Labeled covers enrollment and edited covers base retarget. Prefer an always-reported lightweight check plus conditional full suite so missing/skipped evidence is deterministic. Add strict config for expected Caravan check names and a bounded grace period; status/sync must warn/fail closed with code/evidence when an active downstream member has no expected exact-head check/workflow run, without constraining branch names.

title: Refresh physical-rebase lease after external default advance

The first call may return a retry-tick stale precondition if the default moved during planning; the next exact tick must use current main, rebuild the head and descendants under exact force-with-lease, and then require fresh CI. title: Head creation requires native auto-merge even when cara owns the merge
description:
Live operator report on cacophony, running the correctly nested `sync.head_merge_actor: caravan`:

    cara auto_merge_not_enabled: repository settings must allow squash
    auto-merge before creating a caravan head

    "next": "enable GitHub repository auto-merge and keep squash merge
             enabled, then rerun the same command"

The config was right; the gate was wrong. `src/sync.rs` already conditions its `auto_merge_not_enabled` precondition on the merge actor — the check sits in the `else` branch and only runs when the provider merges. `src/membership/policy.rs::preflight_repository` did not: it required `repository_allows_auto_merge` for every non-join operation regardless of actor.

So a repository that deliberately disabled provider-native auto-merge because cara owns the merge could still sync, but could never create a caravan head. The remediation text made it worse by naming only the repository setting, steering the operator toward re-enabling a native auto-merge that the single-merge-actor work exists to remove — and re-arming it is exactly what the standing directive forbids while that work is open.

Fix: gate the precondition on the actor and say so in the error. `preflight_repository` now takes `head_merge_caravan` from `status.head_merge.actor.caravan()` at all three call sites, and the `next` offers both routes, matching the sync path.

Native auto-merge is a precondition only when the provider performs the merge. When cara merges the green head itself, requiring a repository setting it will never use blocks the caravan for no reason.

description:
Live Cacophony cara new on branch fix-slackiq-nodes created PR #2079 and successfully force-with-lease rewrote exact head 98b89de→c059bf1 onto main 80bf4ea, then attempted mandatory `gh pr view 2079` with only 212ms left in the shared operation deadline. Before apply_prepared/provider mutation, reserve/prove a minimum remaining phase budget for post-rewrite status/candidate refetch, exact head/base verification, labels/base/auto-merge/comment operations, and final receipt. If insufficient, fail before branch mutation with typed membership_operation_budget_insufficient, required/remaining ms, zero-write evidence, and config guidance. Preserve one absolute operation deadline; do not silently extend it. Interrupted/indeterminate provider phases remain resumable from GitHub state.

Acceptance:
- Fixture consumes budget during discovery/preflight until below reserve: no branch/provider write and exact next action.
- Successful rewrite leaves enough budget and completes membership.
- Crash/timeout after an externally completed rewrite still resumes idempotently on the same PR/head without duplicate PR/rewrite.
- Already-satisfied rebase path uses a smaller accurate reserve and can resume the live #2079 generation.
- Cover New/Renew and Join/Rejoin, slow provider refetch, command_timeout > operation duration, and exact completed-prefix receipts.
- Human/JSON/MCP docs explain rerun safety and budget tuning.

title: cara init creates an untracked config that makes sync refuse its own worktree
description:
## Cacophony canary

Sanitized packaged Cara (`cltv-run caravan#cara`, version 0.0.1, store binary `/nix/store/04rswfnfk55a8rpcims63c82zay8v2aq-caravan-0.0.1/bin/cara`) ran from the clean managed Cacophony checkout.

Read-only status correctly reported `repository_not_initialized` for mutations despite all three labels matching. `cara init` then succeeded and returned:

```json
{"ready":true,"config":{"path":".caravan/config.yaml","state":"created"},"labels":[{"name":"caravan","state":"already_present"},{"name":"caravan-evicted","state":"already_present"},{"name":"caravan-force","state":"already_present"}]}
```

The immediately following `cara sync --all` failed before any provider mutation:

```json
{"code":"head_conflict","details":{"checkout":{"error":{"code":"dirty_worktree","details":{"status":"?? .caravan/\n"},"message":"refusing to switch branches because the worktree has tracked or untracked changes"}}}}
```

Cara's own init-created config therefore makes the same repository ineligible for sync's required decision checkout. This deadlocks the documented init→sync recovery path unless the operator manually relocates/ignores the file.

Acceptance:
- `cara init` must place local operational config where its own dirty-worktree guard ignores it safely, or create/verify a reviewed repository-local ignore contract without hiding unrelated files.
- A successful init followed immediately by status/check/sync in an otherwise clean worktree must not fail `dirty_worktree` because of the exact init-owned file.
- Never weaken the dirty-worktree guard for arbitrary `.caravan/` content; recognize only the exact validated config path/inode or use an external state path.
- Add fixtures for newly created config, pre-existing correct config, tracked config, unrelated untracked file beside config, symlink/path escape, alternate `--config` outside the worktree, and branch checkout cleanup.
- Preserve idempotent repository-label/resource receipts and ensure no provider mutation occurs before checkout safety passes.

title: Candidate snapshot reports a superseded base as fresh (stale_base=false on an outdated base.oid)
description:
Cara's merge-candidate snapshot records a base OID that has been superseded on the provider for over an hour, while simultaneously asserting the candidate is fresh and its base is not stale. The two fields contradict each other inside a single snapshot entry.

Observed on live Cacophony, captured in one pass with sources labelled:

- `cara status --json`, `data.merge_candidates` entry for PR `#2210`: `base.name=main`, `base.oid=1a09ceecefa7...`, and in the same entry `freshness=fresh`, `stale_base=false`, `stale_head=false`, `stale_reasons=[]`.
- True `main` at that moment was `9d6278a10f08a9ac1e4c3669aca2dceee572ed12`. `1a09ceecefa7` was superseded by the `release: v1.2.1575` commit at 03:30 UTC; the snapshot `observed_at` was `unix:1785128898`, roughly 05:08 UTC, so the base had been superseded for about 1h38m.
- PR `#2232` shows the same shape, `base.oid 1a09ceec` with `stale_base=false`. PR `#2233` was the only candidate recorded on current `main`.

Why this matters:

- `stale_base` is the field a planner or an operator would trust to decide whether a rebase is required. If it can report `false` against a demonstrably superseded base, then any decision keyed on it is unsound, including forward-progress and rebase-cost work.
- It is a self-inconsistency rather than mere staleness. A snapshot that is simply old would show an old base AND old freshness metadata. Here the base is old while the freshness assertion is affirmatively negative, so a consumer cannot detect the problem by comparing timestamps.
- It plausibly bears on `bd-e99fe6` (physical-sync budget deadlock), because projected rebase work and base drift are exactly what a planner would derive from these fields. Plausibly only: this is NOT asserted as the cause, and the budget formula `required_ms = command_slots x command_timeout_secs` is independently established.

Suggested acceptance:

1. `stale_base` must be true whenever the recorded `base.oid` is not the current provider tip of `base.name`, or the field must be renamed to describe what it actually measures.
2. Snapshot entries should carry the provider tip they were compared against, so a consumer can verify the freshness claim rather than trust it.
3. Add a regression test where the base advances between snapshot capture and read, asserting the freshness fields flip.

Related but distinct, and NOT a defect: the same capture showed `auto_merge.enabled=false` for `#2210` while live GitHub showed it armed. That one is ordinary snapshot staleness, since the arm was restored at 05:12:47Z and the snapshot predates it. Recorded here only so a future reader does not conflate the two.

Environment: Cara `0.0.10` as resolved on the helsinki runtime; `ad14f74` not deployed. Observed by the helsinki profile worker under a read-only watch, which explicitly declined to propose a mechanism; base and provider state verified independently by cluster control.

title: Joining a child onto a stale root absorbs already-main deltas into the child generation
description:
## Live reproduction

During the `pr_cara_join` canary, operator-created root PR #2079 (`fix-slackiq-nodes`, head `c059bf15b65de83aac8053be5a0c57f785e9c6b3`) remained based on stale main `80bf4eacae7451390c2c59c369f1221affcb1c87`. Live main later contained release v1.2.1562 as squash commit `d9fad17e1866272e69a50a47bbd018a890ec33a7` with parent `80bf4eac`.

The local branch used for child PR #2080 (`fix-cara-timeouts`) inherited the release source commit `ac701198a85e07d7964298fe181549b0f2724680`, whose parent is stale-root head `c059bf15`, then added intended timeout commit `21097975f0377f3294eaa3798be6b83e301a7633`. Cara admitted #2080 after stale root #2079 without first converging the root onto current main. Provider state became:

- caravan: `2079 -> 2080`
- #2079 base: `main@80bf4eac` (stale)
- #2080 base: `fix-slackiq-nodes@c059bf15`
- #2080 displayed files include Cargo/CHANGELOG v1.2.1562 even though equivalent release patch is already on live main as `d9fad17e`.

The operator began from what appeared to be an empty `fix-cara-timeouts` branch and expected only the timeout edit. Cara's stale-root admission made the child look as though it invented/absorbed the release delta. This is unsafe/misleading canary topology; PR #2078 is being held until #2079/#2080 are resolved.

## Required behavior

Before appending a child, Cara must converge or refuse a caravan whose root base OID is not live default-branch OID. It must not construct a child generation on a stale root where an already-main patch is represented by a parallel squash/source commit.

## Acceptance

1. Reproduce with stale root `R` from main `M0`, live main `M1` containing squash-equivalent patch `S`, and child source ancestry `R -> S-source -> C`.
2. `join` either atomically advances/rebuilds the root to `M1` before calculating the child, or returns a typed stale-root decision with zero child/provider mutation.
3. After successful convergence, the child provider diff contains only `C`; the duplicate `S-source` patch is dropped as already satisfied.
4. Receipt records old/live main OIDs, root rewrite, duplicate/empty patch disposition, final child base/head/tree, and exact provider mutations.
5. Empty/no-unique-change branches are refused before PR creation/admission instead of allowing inherited predecessor commits to masquerade as the requested change.
6. Add a live/hermetic regression and ensure status/dashboard never describes the absorbed main delta as child-authored work.
creator: ms-mac:cacophony:ms-mac-cacophony-caco-dev-msm-1

title: Add best-effort queue optimisation and auto-admission to sync
description:
## Operator direction — 2026-07-20

Make repeated `cara sync --all` ticks reconcile the fleet and continuously adopt eligible unlabelled PRs, so one Cara loop/controller can eventually drain a long queue without external orchestration scripts.

## Configuration

Add a strict opt-in config surface such as:

```yaml
sync:
  actions:
    join_unlabelled_prs: true
```

Default remains false. Cacophony will opt in.

## Required algorithm

1. Reconcile and validate existing caravans first using normal idempotent sync. A real invalid graph, provider invariant, mechanical/semantic decision, or operator action stops the tick; do not hide it by admitting around it. Waiting CI, held, and healthy states remain structurally valid.
2. If no caravan exists, use the canonical priority/FIFO candidate to form one. Otherwise inspect candidates in configured-priority then immutable-FIFO order and caravans in existing deterministic caravan order.
3. For each candidate, try current tails deterministically. Join to the first exact tail for which candidate/tail and whole-fleet compatibility preflight succeeds. Use the landed atomic remote join receipt, rebase-on-join, and exact-lease contracts; rediscover after every mutation.
4. If no tail works, mark the exact candidate generation with `caravan-join-skipped` plus a durable reason/comment receipt, then consider later candidates in the same tick. This opt-in behavior is an explicit exception to current no-leapfrog automatic admission.
5. A skip must not block manual `new`/`join`/`rejoin`. Bind it to repository, candidate PR/head/base, tested tail generations, default generation, config fingerprint, heuristic version, compatibility reasons, actor, and time. Candidate head/base/config/tail/default/heuristic changes make evidence stale and eligible for automatic retry/removal; unchanged generations are not retried every tick.
6. Bound one tick by wall clock, GitHub API budget, and maximum mutations/candidates. Return exact joins/skips, remaining candidates, and continuation. Retry is idempotent.
7. Expose the heuristic version in status/sync receipts. It is deliberately evolvable; deterministic behavior is required for one version, not permanent optimisation semantics. `priority_fifo_greedy_v1` is sufficient and need not claim a global maximum.
8. `cara loop` and `cara loop --once` consume the same sync behavior. GitHub Actions normally run bounded `--once` ticks from PR/check/workflow/default-branch events plus a schedule, rather than one unbounded hosted job.

Cover empty fleet, one/many caravans, compatible/incompatible candidates, generation-bound skip invalidation, manual override, concurrent tail movement, candidate push, partial crash, API/mutation budget exhaustion, repeated drain, and no admission before existing-fleet convergence. Preserve exact provider rereads, operation lock, and complete audit receipts.

This is the sync-owned best-effort fleet optimiser. Do not add a separate top-level reconcile command unless needed for read-only planning.

---

title: Separate explicit membership authority from automatic FIFO admission
description:
An agent preflighted explicit PR #2081 against tail #2080, saw remote `cara check --pr` reject because older unqueued #2078 was canonical FIFO, then treated `--priority-label caravan-priority:high` as required authority for `cara join --pr 2081 --tail-pr 2080`. - Remote `cara check --pr B` clearly distinguishes `automatic_order_allowed=false` from mechanical eligibility and points to explicit join+reason rather than suggesting priority mutation.

title: Classify unreachable compare refs instead of failing candidate selection
description: Cara-owned A/B handoff from Cacophony P0 bd-220916 (Harry, 2026-07-26). A) A provider compare 404 / unreachable ref must become a typed PER-PAIR unproved diagnostic and must never fail whole-stream selection. Today generation::analyze marks a pair Unknown, contains() returns false for it, no maximum exists, and the ENTIRE component collapses to AmbiguousGeneration "same-stream open generations are divergent or unproved", dead-ending every sibling. Scope the unprovable evidence to the affected pair, keep classifying the rest of the component, and elect a canonical when the remaining relations still prove one. B) Same-stream strict-prefix ancestry is benign supersession and is already handled when the provider compare succeeds (Ahead/Behind produce containment and a canonical maximum); it fails only because the compare was unreachable. Add an exact local-ancestry fallback (git merge-base --is-ancestor over objects already present in the checkout) before declaring a relation unknown, and at minimum keep the row excluded with blocks_order=false rather than wedging selection. Historical sets 2196/2197/2198, 2200/2201 and 2204-2212 predate the Cacophony fix and must become inert under this classification without controller inventory closure. Exact tests: unreachable base, unreachable head, mixed component where one pair is unreachable and the remainder elect a canonical, local-ancestry fallback proving strict prefix, and unchanged divergent fail-closed behaviour. Coordinate release with bd-0629ce for 0.0.11.
