title: Classify failed CI decisions with exact failed-step lineage evidence
description:
Operator-requested Cara information gap. `cara sync --all` correctly returned `ci_failure` for Cacophony PR #1991 and listed failed check names plus rerunnable run ID `29646903145`, but it did not expose why the run failed. The merger had to inspect the GitHub Actions job log directly to discover that the selected ref was stale: expected head `affacaba74132a4642c6aa06021bb8fa5e381097`, selected merge ref `ff68423484b0be2ffe0a2dd70999c8d518c0887b`, parents `[251d04e9be9742cbf9a9d2cfa0a194601e5a2561, 329c42e2a22db8146dada382811927e38ee80e50]`. A blind `cara sync --rerun-failed` would have rerun the same stale event rather than validate the current candidate.

Extend CI decision evidence with bounded structured failure diagnostics: failed job and step names; provider run/job IDs; exact selected ref/SHA; expected and observed base/head; selected-ref parents; current synthetic candidate identity; and a deterministic classification such as stale-merge-ref, retryable-infrastructure, source/test failure, cancelled, or unknown. Prefer first-party structured outputs/check annotations and bounded log extraction; never expose credentials or unbounded logs.

The suggested actions must be generation-aware: do not recommend rerunning a run whose immutable event SHA/merge ref excludes the current head; instead report that a fresh exact-candidate trigger/head refresh is required. Acceptance: a merger can choose rerun, repair, wait, or fresh-trigger from the Cara decision alone without `gh run view --job --log`. Add CLI/JSON/MCP parity fixtures for stale merge-ref versus genuine source failure.

Progress slices (publication blocked by Caco assignment binding): rebased current commits de658f6 add policy-free bounded structured Actions diagnostics (max 10 run IDs, 25 failed jobs/run, 25 failed steps/job, no logs/secrets); 02d7b56 adds deterministic run-vs-current PR generation classes and actions fresh-trigger/rerun-failed/repair/wait; 3c0b53d records provider slice. Live PR #1991 run 29646903145 REST evidence confirms run association head 97d698c differs current expected affacaba despite run head_sha affacaba; failed job 88086568032 step `Verify exact CI ref lineage`. Thus stale generation must recommend fresh candidate, never rerun. Coordinating with bd-021727 shared MergeCandidateIdentity/SyntheticMergeCandidate/Freshness commit faa55fe; that slice must land first, then this lane will reference it in sync decisions/suggested actions. Focused diagnostics tests and strict clippy green. Full broad gate hit reopened unrelated bd-dfea55 parallel output-loss; isolated rerun passed.

Completed dependent integration locally after bd-021727 owner runtime vanished, preserving and cherry-picking the reviewed shared candidate generation. Current coherent tip de820c4 on main@397d1a5 includes: bounded raw Actions facts; shared MergeCandidateIdentity with independent stale_base/stale_head; sync-owned deterministic stale/current/infra/source/cancelled/unknown classification; exact fresh-trigger/rerun/repair/wait actions; stale runs excluded from rerunnable_run_ids; current infrastructure only rerunnable; CI decision/event JSON carries bounded job/failed-step receipts. Added stale-run vs current-source tests, including --rerun-failed fail-closed behavior. Also corrected default movement attribution: a caravan label alone is Unknown, never unproven CaraOwned. Validation: focused ci 2/2, sync 31/31, strict all-target clippy, full cargo test all-targets 203/203, and Darwin nix flake check 47/47 all green. Commits ahead of true main: de658f6, 3c0b53d, 02d7b56, 33c5021 (rescued bd-021727), ac38b77, 8ce8882, de820c4. Publication still requires administrative recovery because caco reintegration assignment binding rejects this preserved worker generation.

Post-land live acceptance found one remaining requirement gap: structured run/job APIs expose stale PR association but not the exact selected synthetic SHA/parents. GitHub's job-log endpoint honors HTTP Range and live run 29646903145 is only 22,969 bytes; a bounded 64KiB read contains one machine receipt `ci-selected-ref-receipt ... selected_ref=ff684... selected_commit=ff684... expected_head=affacaba... expected_base=251d04e... parents=251d04e... 329c42e...`. Reopening to implement strict bounded Range extraction of only this allowlisted receipt, with no raw log retention/exposure and fail-closed secret-safe parsing, so Cara alone carries exact selected lineage.

Final exact-lineage slice 7a8a7e5 on main@3a2a140: failed lineage jobs issue `gh api --include -H Range: bytes=0-61439 .../actions/jobs/<id>/logs`, max 5 lineage jobs/run and max 10 runs. Only strict safe-character `ci-selected-ref-receipt` fields escape; raw text and unrelated lines are discarded, parser requires exact commit/base/head and two parents, and test proves a nearby TOKEN value is absent from serialized evidence. Missing/non-206/malformed/truncated receipts are typed and sync fails closed to fresh-trigger. Live endpoint verified 206 and receipt exact selected ff684... parents [251d04e...,329c42e...]. Green after rebase: ci 2/2, sync 31/31, strict all-target clippy, full cargo all-targets 212/212, Darwin nix flake check.

title: Initialize required Caravan labels safely on first repository use
description:
Operator asked whether Cara initializes a repository by creating its operational labels. Current `cara` v0.0.1 does not.

Source contract in `membership.rs` defines required labels `caravan`, `caravan-evicted`, and `caravan-force`, calls `require_labels`, and fails before provider mutation with `required_labels_missing`: “Caravan's operational labels must exist before the first mutation”, next “create caravan, caravan-evicted, and caravan-force labels, then rerun the same command”. No `gh label create`/repository-label creation implementation exists.

Acceptance:
- Add an explicit idempotent repository initialization surface (`cara init`) or a clearly documented safe first-mutating-use initialization phase.
- Create exactly the required labels with stable names, colors, and descriptions: active member, evicted member, and operator force exception.
- Read-only `status`/`check` must never mutate; they should report initialized/missing/mismatched label state and the exact next command.
- Before first `new`/`join`/`renew`/`rejoin`/`sync` mutation, require initialization or perform it only through an explicit opt-in flag; never silently broaden permissions.
- Use optimistic repository-label preconditions and idempotent create-if-absent behavior. Existing correct labels no-op; concurrent creation converges.
- If an existing label has unexpected metadata, fail with a bounded decision point rather than overwriting operator-owned configuration.
- Report missing GitHub label-write permission distinctly and make no PR/base/auto-merge mutation when initialization fails.
- Add fixtures for empty repo, partially initialized labels, existing correct labels, metadata mismatch, concurrent init, permission denial, status read-only, and retry after indeterminate create.
- Update `cara help`, SPEC, and first-use docs with repository initialization workflow.

Related live cutover blocker: `caravan/bd-f7c3bc` (Cara status JSON parsing failure). caco-merger must stay on its audited manual provider path until inventory and initialization are safe.

## Helsinki first-use/label acceptance finding

Independent live inspection confirms the current implementation does **not** initialize repository labels:

- daemon Caravan checkout: `e451ed9c02860f9dea408cd68890fdde56c8846a`;
- installed binary: `cara 0.0.1`, SHA-256 `0e88ba61fcb6df4aaf95b609d714d8caae9942be4a0cfcccabb4912e4e59f813` (operator updater refreshed the binary after the earlier installed-path proof);

Cacophony's live repository is now externally/manual-initialized with all three correct labels, so the requested idempotent create is a no-op rather than a write:

Title: Add idempotent Cara repository initialization for required labels

## Operator expectation

While integrating Cara into Cacophony, Harry asked whether first use correctly initializes a repository by creating the `caravan`, `caravan-evicted`, and `caravan-force` labels.

Current behavior does not initialize them. `cara status` can inventory an unlabelled repository, but mutation paths call `require_labels` and fail before provider mutation with `required_labels_missing`, instructing the operator to create all three labels manually and rerun. There is no `cara init` command.

The Cacophony repository currently has all three labels, verified through GitHub, but they were provisioned externally rather than by Cara first-use initialization.

## Acceptance

- Add an explicit, idempotent first-party initialization surface such as `cara init` (CLI/MCP), or an equally clear reviewed first-use path.
- Create exactly the required labels with documented names, descriptions, and colors:
  - `caravan`
  - `caravan-evicted`
  - `caravan-force`
- Preserve compatible existing labels without mutation; fail closed on incompatible definitions unless an explicit repair option is chosen.
- Return stable receipts distinguishing created, already-present, incompatible, and provider-failed labels.
- `cara status` should report repository initialization readiness and the exact next command when labels are missing.
- `new`, `join`, `renew`, and `rejoin` continue to fail before graph mutation if initialization has not completed.
- Add provider fixtures for empty repo, partial labels, compatible existing labels, incompatible metadata, retry after partial provider failure, and idempotent replay.
- Document whether automatic initialization is ever allowed; avoid hidden label mutation from a read-only `status` call.

Filed from the first Cacophony Cara cutover. This belongs in the Caravan project, not Cacophony.

Then idempotently create or verify all three required labels without changing compatible existing labels. Before reporting ready, preflight repository write/admin capability, default branch identity/protection and required-check policy, and repository squash auto-merge support, reusing existing typed provider evidence where possible. CLI, stable --json, bounded MCP input/output schemas, help/SPEC/docs, and provider fixtures must match. Live acceptance is against the Cacophony repository, where config and all three labels already exist: init must be a no-op verification, preserve exact label metadata, avoid every PR label/base/auto-merge mutation, and prove repeated idempotence. bd-046d79 was compared in full and marked duplicate because its scope is a strict subset of this bead.

title: Reserve physical-sync apply budget before control-label mutation
description:
Live two-member Cacophony caravan #2079→#2080 repeatedly failed to converge after main moved. Exact no-write `cara plan sync` on v0.0.6 spent ~110s preparing both members under sync.max_duration_secs=120, then invoked mandatory `git push --dry-run --force-with-lease` with only 9.635s remaining and returned rebase_command_failed. The mutating sync path had already passed the global write barrier and removed generation-bound caravan-force labels/comments for #2079/#2080 before later rewrite apply failed, leaving no branch receipts and lost operator intent. A prior attempt also saw provider base-ref lag (child expected old parent OID 570e26e while branch already 889dfe2) and returned retry_tick.

Make whole-chain physical sync budget admission phase-aware and zero-write before commitment. Before disabling auto-merge, invalidating control labels, or any branch write, prove/reserve enough absolute-deadline budget for per-member final remote/PR revalidation, exact lease pushes, midpoint provider rediscovery, base/CI reconciliation, and final receipt. If insufficient, return typed physical_sync_budget_insufficient with required/remaining ms, prepared-plan count/hash, zero provider/branch mutation, and config guidance. Preserve the one absolute deadline; do not silently extend.

Avoid redundant expensive dry-run permission checks after the global barrier where exact lease push itself safely detects movement, or explicitly account for every repeated verification in the reserve. A provider race remains retryable, but unchanged provider lag/deadline exhaustion must not hot-loop or consume control intent.

Acceptance:
- Two-member fixture consumes planning time until below apply reserve: no labels, auto-merge, comments, or refs change.
- Sufficient budget rebuilds head onto exact main then child onto simulated rewritten head, with midpoint/final receipts.
- Slow second verify/dry-run cannot occur after irreversible control mutation without a resumable exact phase receipt.
- Plan sync reports complete/partial bounded plans and typed budget continuation without mutation.
- BaseRefOid lag vs exact branch ref is distinguished from a true writer race and converges on bounded rediscovery.
- Cover main movement, parent/child branch movement, command_timeout greater than whole-tick duration, N-member scaling, and crash/restart.
- Coordinate with bd-4e4615 (membership post-rebase reserve) and the separate force-invalidation atomicity bead being filed/routed by msm1.

title: Give each Cara candidate an independent bounded discovery budget
description:
## Live Cacophony blocker

An operator-authorized Cara enrollment pass reached deterministic provider time-budget exhaustion without mutation:

- Cara v0.0.5 sync preserved PR #2053 enrolled/paused at exact head `53d8ed4e` and recorded skips for PRs #1952, #1955, #1978, #1980, and #1989.
- The retry tick then returned `github_discovery_timeout` at PR #1994 with only 339 ms of Git-fetch budget available.
- A direct, operator-allowlisted attempt to enroll clean PR #2059 exact head `27a06a55` refused `git_compatibility_timeout` with 1 ms remaining after full-fleet preflight.
- Provider state was not mutated.

## Required behavior

- Separate full-fleet discovery/preflight budget from exact candidate compatibility/admission budget.
- Allocate each explicitly selected candidate a fresh bounded budget that prior candidate scans cannot consume.
- Reuse safely cached provider/topology data where exact head/base/freshness permits, with drift refusal.
- Persist a deterministic continuation cursor/receipt so retry ticks resume rather than restart the full fleet scan.
- Exact allowlisted admission must not traverse every unrelated PR before checking its target.
- Return typed timing breakdowns for provider listing, Git fetch, compatibility, and mutation phases.
- Preserve fail-closed no-mutation semantics on every timeout.
- Add regressions for a large candidate fleet followed by exact candidate enrollment with near-exhausted global budget.

## Acceptance

PR #2059 or an equivalent exact candidate can receive a full independent compatibility budget and either enroll successfully or return a semantic refusal; it must not fail merely because previous full-fleet discovery consumed the shared deadline.

Title: Reserve exact candidate Git budget after full-fleet Cara discovery

## Reproduction

title: Skip merge-preserving replay for a squash-merged root
description:
Live block on Cacophony PR2215 under cara 0.0.13 with head_merge_actor caravan. Cara refused with rebase_merge_replay_conflict: the independently clean final merge tree cannot be reproduced by the audited merge-preserving sequencer without an intermediate conflict. Evidence: expected_merge_tree 1a13539e7485e3219dc7e16334ffd5b9d8f8aff1 is independently CLEAN, conflicting_paths crates/caco-cli/src/lib.rs and crates/caco-daemon/src/canonical_queue.rs, merge_commits 255db7da1c95b82a03f7a9cdcfa65bb73882c2c7 and 25876d4f856f7b22079c156671c7ad928eb42cc2, stderr shows Rebasing 7/9 then Could not apply the "merge: resolve main into cumulative root PR2215" commit. No remote or provider mutation was attempted, which is correct.

Root cause: the PR merged main into itself, so its history contains merge commits. Replaying that history commit-by-commit re-hits conflicts the author already resolved by hand in the merge commit, with no stored rerere resolution to replay them. The destination tree is fine; only the reproduction path fails.

Product gap: under head_merge_actor caravan the ROOT is squash-merged, so its history is discarded at landing. Insisting on a merge-preserving replay of a root whose squash merge tree is already proven clean is work that can only fail and buys nothing. History replay genuinely matters for CHILDREN, whose ancestry must physically follow the chain, and it matters when rebase output is published as the new head; it does not matter for a root about to be collapsed into a single commit.

Required behaviour: when the actor is caravan and the candidate is the root that will be squash-merged, and the squash merge tree against the exact current default branch is independently proven clean, land it directly without requiring a merge-preserving replay of its history. Keep every existing guard: exact head and base re-read immediately before mutation, proven clean merge tree, required checks satisfied or explicit force, merged-main reachability postflight before the landing counts, and zero-write abort on any drift. Do not extend this to children, and do not use it to bypass a genuinely conflicting tree.

Also note the sync_failed hook for this event exited 124, a timeout, so the refusal was not reported to any external actor.

Operator confirmed the intent: we squash merge it in the end anyway.

title: Add cascading and whole-caravan eviction
description:
Live operator block 2026-07-27 on Cacophony. `cara evict --pr 2223 --reason Incompatible` fails with reshape_would_break_fleet: the proposed reshape does not satisfy Caravan graph/compatibility invariants. Single-member eviction must close the gap by retargeting the evicted member children onto its predecessor, and when that new edge is incompatible the eviction is refused. The operator therefore cannot dismantle a caravan whose members are mutually incompatible: the only tool for breaking up a broken chain is itself blocked by the chain being broken. PR2215 was reverted on main and the operator wants to evict everything and rebuild from scratch, and there is no first-party way to do it.

Required: an ordered multi-member eviction.
- `cara evict --cascade --pr N`: evict N and every member after it, so no surviving edge ever needs to be re-linked across a removed member.
- `cara evict --all` (or an explicit dissolve verb): unenroll every member of the caravan.

Design point that makes this safe: process TAIL FIRST. Removing the current tail never requires closing a gap, because it has no child, so each individual removal is trivially compatible and the whole operation avoids the invariant that blocks single-member eviction today. A cascade is therefore a bounded sequence of tail removals, not a graph rewrite.

Preserve every existing guard per member: exact PR state and head re-read immediately before mutation, add caravan-evicted, remove caravan and caravan-force, disable auto-merge, durable control-label audit comment, and zero-write abort on drift. Emit one receipt per evicted member plus a summary naming the caravan, the ordered members evicted, and the final fleet state. Partial failure must leave a resumable, honestly reported state rather than a half-dissolved chain with no record.

Decide and document what happens to each evicted member base: leaving it pointed at a now-evicted predecessor is wrong, so members should be retargeted to the default branch as they are released, making each PR independently reviewable and re-admittable.

Operator also asked for this because the Cara Sync CI job is being disabled and run from inside Cacophony instead; a broken chain that cannot be dismantled blocks that migration.

title: Exhausted operation deadline is reported as a command failure
description:
Live report from cacophony on v0.0.21. A `cara sync --all` tick ran to the end of its `max_duration_secs: 3600` budget and then failed with:

    cara rebase_command_failed: could not run isolated cumulative rebase command
    "source": "`git fetch --quiet --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head --refmap= origin
               refs/heads/main` exceeded its 285ms deadline and was terminated"

The command did not fail. The operation deadline was exhausted, and `effective_timeout` in src/command.rs only refused when the remaining budget was *exactly zero*. Any positive sliver was passed through as a real timeout, so a network fetch was launched with 285ms to live, reaped, and reported as a command failure.

That sends a reader to debug git or provider latency when the actual cause is budget: the tick consumed its full hour. The error must name the deadline, not the command.

Fix: introduce a minimum viable command budget. Below it, refuse with the existing exhaustion shape and a message that states how much remained, what the floor is, and which knobs move it (`sync.max_duration_secs` up, or `sync.max_candidates_per_tick` down). 750ms is chosen to be under any real local git invocation while still well above the sliver range where a launch is guaranteed waste.

Context from the same report: initial discovery alone took 51,741ms for 15 unqueued PRs, so a fleet of that size genuinely approaches an hour of work per tick. The budget refusal is correct; only its explanation was wrong.

title: Release workflow schedules an aarch64-darwin job no runner can ever accept
description:
Every release since v0.0.11 has required a manual `just release-backfill-target <tag> aarch64-darwin`, nine consecutive times. The cause is not flaky infrastructure.

`.github/workflows/release.yml` pins the darwin leg to `runs-on: [self-hosted, nix, aarch64-darwin]`. Queried live, the repository has seven registered runners and every one is Linux X64:

    caravan-ms-dev, caravan-ms-dev-2..6, caravan-pocket4
    labels: self-hosted,nix,Linux,X64,x86_64-linux,nixos,<host>

No runner advertises `aarch64-darwin`. The job is unschedulable by construction: it queues until the run is cancelled or times out, and the release run never reaches a terminal state. `fail-fast: false` makes this present as an indefinite hang rather than a failure, which is why it read as flakiness for nine releases.

Second, smaller issue: the `aarch64-linux` leg pins `runs-on: [self-hosted, nix, ms-dev-2]`, a single host. When ms-dev-2 is busy (it was at filing time) that leg queues behind unrelated work. That one is slow rather than broken, and the pin is deliberate since only ms-dev-2 advertises aarch64 in Nix extra-platforms, so it should stay pinned unless another host gains that capability.

Remedy: stop scheduling a leg no machine can accept. Either register a darwin runner, or drop the matrix entry and make the documented `just release-backfill-target` path the contract, so a release run concludes honestly instead of hanging on an impossible job. A workflow that cannot succeed should not be presented as pending.

title: Add CLI manual decision mode with an interactive shell
description:
## Operator goal

Provide a human-operated way to exercise Cara's full decision/recovery flow without turning production machine hooks into PTY sessions.

## Product surface

Add a CLI-only mode such as:

```text
cara loop --manual [--shell 'zsh -i']
```

or an equivalent explicit `sync --manual` driver. Normal hooks remain noninteractive machine integration.

## Required behavior

- Run the ordinary bounded `sync --all` tick. Healthy/waiting/held/retry outcomes retain normal behavior.
- On `wake_class=external_decision`, persist the complete bounded decision event to a secure temporary/durable file and expose `CARA_DECISION_FILE` plus event/operation/repository/caravan/PR/session continuation variables.
- Checkpoint and release the repository operation lock before launching anything interactive.
- Launch the configured shell with inherited stdin/stdout/stderr and a real controlling TTY, from the exact safe affected checkout or Cara-owned repair workspace when one exists. Refuse non-TTY, JSON, MCP, daemon, or hosted noninteractive invocation rather than degrading silently.
- Do not infer resolution from shell exit alone. Zero exit triggers full provider rediscovery and another sync tick; nonzero exits manual mode while preserving evidence. Exact repair publication still uses `repair continue`, provider head/target checks, and non-force branch rules.
- Bound/recover temporary decision files, redact secrets, preserve a manual-session audit receipt, and handle signals/terminal restoration.
- Document suggested shell helpers for inspecting JSON with `jq`, running tests, invoking authorized repair, and exiting to retry.

Tests should cover inherited TTY and cwd, lock release, decision-file integrity, zero/nonzero exit, signal handling, stale provider movement while shell is open, repair workspace continuation, recursive hook avoidance, and refusal from MCP/noninteractive environments.

Existing hooks already receive JSON on stdin and are synchronously awaited with timeout/blocking policy. Production repair scripts may submit durable agents and poll until exact resolution; this feature is only the human flow-testing/controller surface.

- Cara-created/reused PR https://github.com/harryaskham/cacophony/pull/2080 targets `fix-slackiq-nodes` from `fix-cara-timeouts`.
- Its first commit is `ac701198`, parent `c059bf15`, authored by Cacophony Daemon at 23:04:11Z. Its title/body were initially `release: v1.2.1562` and copied update-helper identity/head `e3026e0461`, despite the operator working on `fix-cara-timeouts`.

- Preserve the caller branch on any ambiguity and surface exact candidate provenance for diagnosis.
- Add a regression test with two concurrent patches: release patch A lands on main while operator branch B joins an active tail with an initially empty diff; B must never receive A.

Do not mutate or close PR 2080 as part of triage; preserve it as live evidence until the owner chooses repair.

## Object-cache/minimal-fetch extension ready

Commit `1a176a0` on landed base `35dffd1` removes the full cold provider clone. Repair now records/canonicalizes the current repository/object-cache Git identity, creates an independent `--shared --no-checkout` local seed with a `cache` remote, binds explicit provider `origin`, and fetches only exact recorded head/target refs using protocol v2 + `--filter=blob:none` + command-scoped SSH batch/connect/keepalive bounds. Full 218 lib + 6 bin + 7 CLI + 3 parity tests, strict all-target Clippy, canonical fmt, Nix flake, Cara 0.0.2/version/repair-help all green. title: Add cara next --status with optional checkout
description:
Operator request: scheduler and cron systems (caco's in particular) have no good place to host one long-lived `cara loop`, so they need manual primitives to reconstruct the loop's routing themselves.

Agreed design, after reconciling against the existing surface:

- ONE verb with a status filter, not `next-conflicting` / `next-evicted` / `next-failing`. Three verbs means three copies of FIFO, priority and skip semantics that will drift.
- `cara next --status <set>` REPLACES `cara next-candidate` outright. It is early enough to be backwards incompatible, so no alias is kept. `--status ready` must return byte-identical selection to what sync admits, or two surfaces give agents different answers.
- JSON-based, not exit-code based. The caller parses the payload and moves itself; "no match" is a normal outcome carried in the JSON, never an error envelope, so a cron can distinguish "nothing to do" from "provider down".
- `--checkout` is an opt-in convenience on `cara next` and on `cara loop --manual`: it still returns the same JSON but moves the working tree to the selected branch, fetching as needed.

Two load-bearing constraints on `--checkout`:

1. It must route through `navigation::ensure_safe_worktree` and FAIL CLOSED on a dirty tree. A cron that clobbers uncommitted work is worse than one that does nothing.
2. The JSON must carry a receipt naming what it moved FROM and TO, so the move is auditable and reversible.

`--status skipped` must re-derive validity rather than trusting the label, because a skip is bound to the exact head it was proven against; a stale label would otherwise route agents at PRs that have since been force-pushed.

Documented as gap 2 in docs/lifecycle.md.

title: Own the full merge lifecycle: squash the passing head each tick
description: Operator direction 2026-07-27: native GitHub auto-merge will be disabled on the Cacophony repository because a member could be merged into the next caravan member rather than main, mixing two merge actors. Caravan must therefore own the whole lifecycle. On each sync tick, when the caravan root is the exact current head, is mechanically compatible with the default branch, and every required check on that exact head is passing, Cara must squash-merge it itself and then atomically advance the next member to target the default branch, in one reserved and idempotent plan. Requirements: exact-head and exact-base preconditions immediately before the merge, with zero-write refusal on any drift; no admin bypass on the ordinary path (the existing admin squash stays reserved for audited caravan-force); one merge per tick per caravan so ordering stays observable; the promotion must not be separable from the merge by a budget refusal, matching the bd-9ead1b promotion-atomicity requirement; typed receipts naming merged PR, merge commit, promoted successor, and its new base; and safe behaviour when auto-merge is still armed externally so Cara never races another actor. Also stop requiring squash auto-merge arming as a graph invariant once Cara owns merging, or the invariant will report a permanent problem on a repository that has deliberately disabled it. Add regressions for passing head merged and successor promoted in one tick, red head not merged, drifted head refused zero-write, and a repository with native auto-merge disabled reporting no auto_merge_invariant.

title: Retire merged caravan heads from checkpoints and dashboard after post-merge receipt failure
description:
## Problem

Cara successfully provider-merged Cacophony PR #2053 at `293bc9bb46e01792ac601f1a8798f33006fe9071`, then returned `operation_lock_checkpoint_too_large`. PR #2056 also merged at `967e304c6ef27f646c9cd3be388a3e7e2c7e757d`. For substantially longer than one controller cycle, the Cara dashboard still presented both as one-member caravan heads with force intent and no auto-merge, making the operator reasonably conclude that Cara was not merging its heads.

Fresh provider truth contradicted the dashboard:

- `gh pr view 2053`: `MERGED` at 2026-07-21T19:12:35Z.
- `gh pr view 2056`: `MERGED` at 2026-07-21T19:15:52Z.
- fresh `cara status --json`: `healthy=true`, `analysis.fleet.caravans=[]`, `merge_candidates=[]`.
- the persisted PR2053 pause remains in status as `state: stale` / `auto_merge_suspended: true` with old expected-open facts; it is not a live provider caravan.

This is a post-provider-success recovery/UI correctness bug: a checkpoint-size failure must not leave merged provider heads displayed as actionable open caravans.

## Acceptance

1. After a provider merge succeeds, checkpoint/event-journal compaction stays within its bound; large check histories use hashes/counts/bounded samples rather than overflowing the operation-lock checkpoint.
2. If durable checkpoint publication still fails after provider merge, the next status/dashboard refresh rediscovers GitHub and retires the merged head from active caravans.
3. Stale pause records whose exact head is merged are shown only as historical/stale diagnostics, never as active caravan cards and never as requiring auto-merge repair.
4. Add a regression with a force-labelled head carrying many historical check runs: provider merge succeeds, checkpoint publication fails or is bounded, then fresh status/dashboard shows zero active caravans and the merge receipt remains observable.
5. Provider truth remains authoritative; local checkpoint cleanup never attempts a second merge.

## Live recurrence — Cacophony PR2101, 2026-07-25

Cara admitted PR2101 as a sole-member caravan, then provider truth merged it at `3ad8d2843fe2f05e4617081d14837482f51b448c` on 2026-07-25T01:07:18Z. Fresh first-party `caco pr reflect --project cacophony --pr 2101` reports `pr_state=merged`, and timeline/main contains `fix(tui): decouple remote pane refresh from input (bd-8ffd54) (#2101)`.

After merge, canonical Cara remained degraded/unavailable with the stale PR2101 caravan and `auto_merge_invariant`: the caravan head supposedly must have squash auto-merge enabled. Attempting to repair auto-merge on an already merged PR would be invalid provider mutation. The stale caravan also blocked the fresh ordinary `pr_cara_join` generation-3 root, causing PR2167 to publish unjoined and earn zero canary credit.

This recurrence elevates the bug to P0 while it blocks queue admission. Required immediate behavior: provider discovery must retire merged PR2101 from active topology, preserve its merge receipt, and return healthy zero-caravan status without any raw/provider auto-merge toggle. Do not merge or mutate PR2101 again. Regression coverage must assert merged provider truth dominates stale auto-merge invariants during post-merge checkpoint failure.

title: [operator] Make Cara join transactional for agent reintegration and sync event-driven
description:
## Operator direction — 2026-07-19

Move Cacophony from an LLM-driven merge-train cadence to deterministic Cara ownership:

1. Every new agent PR is opened and atomically appended to the current Caravan tail through a new Cacophony `pr_cara_join` reintegration mode.
2. `rebase_on_join` is configured true. Join rebases the candidate onto the exact current tail and targets the tail branch, preserving a valid root-to-tail chain.
3. A join conflict/failure returns an exact error to the authoring agent. Cacophony refuses reintegration completion/handoff, so that owner fixes the conflict and retries until the same PR joins successfully.
4. Routine `cara sync` ticks are deterministic and do not wake caco-merger. caco-merger wakes only for real typed repair/semantic decisions or terminal CI failures.
5. The Caravan root remains current with main, descendants remain rebased/targeted onto their exact parent, and required CI runs on the exact active heads.

This extends the landed `rebase_on_join`/chain-rebuild work from bd-cacf7c into the transactional author-ingress and event-driven operations contract.

## Required Caravan contract

- Expose stable CLI/JSON/MCP check/join surfaces suitable for Cacophony orchestration, with exact repository/PR/head/current-tail/config/provider identity receipts.
- Require and report `rebase_on_join=true` for this integration. Disabled/missing mode fails before mutation with the exact config action.
- Under the repository operation lock, rediscover the tail immediately before mutation and preflight ancestry, patch compatibility, force-with-lease authority, base target, labels, and required-check trigger behavior.
- Successful join must leave the same PR OPEN with its reviewed patch rebased onto the exact tail head, `baseRefName` equal to the tail branch, Caravan membership durable, prior CI invalidated, and fresh exact-head/base CI requested. No unrelated PR or provider-owned head may be changed.
- Join failure/conflict must not claim success or Caravan membership. Return exact conflicting paths/patch receipt/current tail and a first-party owner repair instruction. Any already-open source PR remains preserved as unjoined/owner-held; no duplicate PR, queue label, auto-merge, or ambiguous partial state.
- Exact retries on unchanged PR/head/tail are idempotent. Concurrent joins serialize and the loser rechecks the new tail rather than building a forked chain.
- Emit a durable join receipt/event that Cacophony can bind to generation, agent, bead, PR, head, base/tail, and config fingerprint.
- Make routine `sync --all` a no-LLM deterministic tick. It advances healthy chains, retargets/rebuilds after root merge under `rebase_on_join`, requests fresh CI, and returns typed decisions.
- Emit/wire a bounded wake event only for semantic repair decisions, unresolved mechanical conflicts requiring an owner, provider invariant failure, or terminal required-CI failure. Healthy/waiting/success ticks do not wake caco-merger.
- Enforce the root invariant: the Caravan root targets current main and is up to date before merge eligibility; each descendant targets and descends from its exact parent. A stale root such as PR #1962 must be synchronously advanced or returned as a typed blocker, never left indefinitely without checks.
- Add fixtures for two concurrent authors, join conflict then same-PR retry, tail moving between preflight/mutation, root main advance, descendant rebuild, missing checks, CI failure wake, healthy no-wake tick, and crash/restart idempotency.
- Document the integration contract for the Cacophony companion implementation and return the exact landed SHA/version before cutover.

## Operator correction — 2026-07-19 10:00 BST

The consuming Cacophony repository must explicitly set `rebase_on_join: true` in checked-in `.caravan/config.yaml`. Deterministic Cara continues to own serialized topology and routine sync, but its agent-in-loop repair contract must allow an authorized caco-merger to edit arbitrary repository paths after a typed real CI/semantic/provider failure. Do not limit that repair role to textual `conflicting_paths` or pre-granted semantic paths. Keep exact repository/PR/head/base/session binding, same-PR non-force publication, reviewed diff, fresh CI, and audit receipts. The narrow grant mechanism may remain useful for deterministic automation, but it cannot block the broad authorized merger repair path.

Post-v0.0.4 board audit (2026-07-20): v0.0.4 includes major Caravan-side slices—atomic remote join receipt (`780ac5d`, bd-6e7179), deterministic sync scheduler/wake status (`ec3a4db`, bd-d38dbf), deterministic receipt hashing (`091abe6`, bd-0f8b68), and force-generation invalidation (`35c08e6`, bd-4342ee). The umbrella is not complete: its later operator correction requires broad session-level authorized merger edits (bd-17375b reopened; narrow grants alone are insufficient), plus the companion Cacophony `pr_cara_join`/event-driven cutover and live acceptance. Added bd-17375b as an explicit dependency; do not close umbrella from the landed slices alone.

Board administration follow-up: added `bd-6f463b` as the explicit sync-owned best-effort queue optimiser/auto-admission dependency alongside broad authorized repair `bd-17375b`. The umbrella remains blocked until both land and companion Cacophony cutover/live acceptance is complete.

title: cara new cannot flatten a squash-merged root, only sync can
description:
Live report from cacophony: `cara new` on PR 2271, with no existing caravans, refused with

    tree_mismatch: merge-preserving replay tree differs from the independently
    computed clean merge tree
    expected_tree af776f4e19062301e4def629ded5780a52aad3f3

The operator's reasonable reading was that `rebase_on_join` had not applied. It had — the refusal comes from inside the physical rebase. The real gap is which *kind* of rebase was authorized.

bd-85b71d established that a caravan ROOT squash-merged by cara has its history discarded at landing, so replaying its merge topology proves nothing; the root is flattened onto the independently proven merge tree instead. That reasoning was wired into `src/sync.rs` only. `src/membership.rs` builds its own `RebaseExecutionBudget` for `new`/`renew`/`join` and never set `flattening_squashed_root`, so a branch containing a merge commit could be flattened by a later sync but not by the `cara new` that creates the caravan.

Result: exactly the bd-85b71d shape (a branch that merged main into itself with hand-resolved conflicts) is admitted by sync but refused at creation, which is where an operator actually hits it first.

Fix: authorize flattening in the membership path under the same two conditions sync uses — the candidate is a root (no join target, so its base is the default branch) and `sync.head_merge_actor` is `caravan`. A member joining behind a tail is still never flattened, because its ancestry must physically follow the chain, and an unauthorized merge-preserving replay still fails closed.

title: auto_merge_invariant should re-arm a caravan head after a transient red; GitHub disarms automatically but never re-arms
description:
A caravan head that ever goes red permanently loses its auto-merge invariant, because the disarm is automatic and the re-arm is not. Nothing in the system notices. The queue then sits with a head that will never merge unattended, and the symptom reads as "the owner never armed auto-merge", which sends whoever investigates down the wrong path.

Observed live on cacophony PR #2210 on 2026-07-27, where it held a six-member caravan for roughly ninety minutes overnight.

## Sequence

    02:26:12Z  owner arms squash auto-merge on #2210 (with `gh pr edit --base main`, clearing a DanglingBase row)
    03:38:00Z  required check `Check & Lint` goes red on runner cacophony-ms-dev-2
               -> GitHub silently DISARMS auto-merge
    03:38-05:12 head sits unmergeable; nothing re-arms; caravan of six blocked
    05:12:47Z  owner manually re-arms after cross-agent investigation
               head 2e02a53116 unchanged, no new generation, Cara's own rebase intact

The red was not the owner's diff. It was `tests/source-guard-tooling-fixtures.sh` aborting silently when `nix print-dev-env .#ci-source` failed on the runner host — filed separately as cacophony bd-bcb813. A re-run of only the failed jobs went green, confirming it as transient.

## Why this is systemic rather than a one-off

The disarm is GitHub behaviour and will not change: any failing required check disables auto-merge, and GitHub never re-enables it. So the invariant Cara relies on for unattended landing is silently destroyed by any transient red on the head, and only a human restores it.

That matters much more when transient reds are common, which they currently are. Under cacophony bd-603883, every native runner unit on two nodes is in a `226/NAMESPACE` restart loop, leaving three surviving `x86_64-linux` runners — and the red above happened on `cacophony-ms-dev-2`, one of those three. So the survivors are flaky rather than healthy. Flaky runners produce transient reds; every transient red on a head permanently disarms it; each occurrence needs a human. Those compound, and the queue wedges repeatedly for a reason no single component reports as a fault.

It also mimics a different failure. `auto_merge_invariant` reporting "head is not armed" is indistinguishable to a reader from "owner never armed it", so investigation starts at the owner rather than at the check history. Both agents who looked at this initially assumed a Cara or lifecycle bug.

## Suggested change

`auto_merge_invariant` repair should **re-arm** the head when it finds the invariant broken but the head otherwise eligible, rather than only reporting it. Guard rails worth having, offered as suggestions rather than requirements:

- re-arm only for the exact current head OID that Cara already selected, never a moved head
- re-arm only when the disarm is attributable to a check transition, not to an owner explicitly disabling auto-merge
- bound it, so a head that is genuinely and repeatedly red does not get re-armed in a loop; a small retry ceiling with a reported give-up is better than unbounded
- record the re-arm in the receipt, so it is visible that Cara did it rather than the owner

Reporting-only is defensible if re-arming is judged too much authority for the scheduler. In that case the report should at least distinguish **"never armed"** from **"armed at T, disarmed by a failing required check at T+n"**, because those two states need completely different responses and currently look identical.

## Provenance

Root cause and sequence established by cacophony:8x5t4zp7luvs0a4q on ms-dev-3, who owns #2210 and re-armed it. Filed here at their explicit suggestion ("durable follow-up for whoever owns queue health") by cacophony:d23tqrb17ss3e6xo from ms-dev-6, who was queued behind the head and narrowed the failing fixture. Neither of us has modified Cara, any runner, any queue state, or another agent's PR.

Related: cacophony bd-bcb813 (silent fixture abort that produced the red), cacophony bd-603883 (runner restart loop leaving three flaky survivors).

## SUPERSEDED 2026-07-27 ~08:35 BST — do not implement the re-arm recommendation

The operator has decided to **disable native auto-merge on the cacophony repository entirely**, and to make Cara the sole landing mechanism: on each tick Cara should retarget the caravan root to `main`, verify CI, and then directly **squash-merge** the exact root. Rationale given: all lifecycle via Caravan rather than a mix of Caravan and provider auto-merge, which is slower but safer and easier to reason about.

That closes off this bead's central recommendation. **Do not implement auto-merge re-arming.** If auto-merge is disabled repository-wide there is nothing to arm, nothing to disarm, and a scheduler that re-armed it would be reintroducing exactly the hybrid this decision removes.

Tracking for the replacement behaviour is **caravan bd-f8cf99** (P0), which covers Cara performing the retarget-verify-squash-merge itself.

### What remains valid here, and worth carrying into bd-f8cf99

The diagnosis stands even though the fix has changed, and two parts are worth preserving rather than losing with this bead:

1. **The failure mode this documented is real and was live.** A caravan head that went transiently red silently lost its auto-merge invariant, GitHub never re-armed it, and the head sat unmergeable for ~90 minutes blocking six PRs while presenting as "the owner never armed it". Whatever replaces it should not be able to enter a state that is (a) load-bearing for landing, (b) silently cleared by an unrelated transient, and (c) indistinguishable from never having been set.

2. **The wrong-target merge it contributed to.** With auto-merge armed on a chained PR whose base was another member's generation branch, #2213 auto-merged into `agent/ms-dev-3/.../8x5t4zp7luvs0a4q-pr-gf9e8151...` at 2026-07-27T07:15:08Z instead of into `main`, leaving bd-282638 unlanded and riding inside the next member's PR. That is the concrete harm from mixing provider auto-merge with Cara-managed chain topology, and it is the strongest single argument for the operator's decision. Cara's own squash-merge path must retarget the root to `main` **before** merging, or it reproduces the same class of error under a different mechanism.

Superseding note recorded by cacophony:d23tqrb17ss3e6xo, who filed this bead. Not closing it, since that is the caravan owner's call — but it should not be worked as written.

title: Admission capacity still uses worst-case slot pricing and yields an impossible 0-member bound
description:
The bounded-prefix work fixed the physical-sync RESERVE but not the ADMISSION bound, and the admission bound now computes a self-contradictory 0-member capacity that closes the queue to all new work.

Read-only `cara status --json` from the canonical daemon checkout, Cara `0.0.11`, at main `7c0bb4158e13ce20673b3a62699fdfef827406dc`:

```json
"sync_budget": {
  "deadline_ms": 3600000,
  "command_timeout_ms": 600000,
  "deadline_command_slots": 6,
  "max_admissible_members": 0,
  "blocked_candidate": 2234,
  "safe_next_action": "every caravan holds the 0-member bound implied by the configured deadline; admission stays closed with caravan_budget_capacity_exhausted until a caravan drains"
}
```

Per caravan:

```json
{"caravan_id": 2215, "required_command_slots": 21, "required_ms": 315000, "retained_command_slots": 16, "retained_ms": 240000, "at_capacity": true,
 "safe_next_action": "let this caravan drain before admitting another member: 4 members already reach the 0-member bound implied by sync.max_duration_secs=3600s and command_timeout_secs=600s"}
{"caravan_id": 2233, "required_command_slots": 9, "required_ms": 135000, "retained_command_slots": 7, "retained_ms": 105000, "at_capacity": true,
 "safe_next_action": "let this caravan drain before admitting another member: 1 members already reach the 0-member bound implied by sync.max_duration_secs=3600s and command_timeout_secs=600s"}
```

Three problems, in increasing severity.

**1. Two different budget models are in use simultaneously.** `required_ms` is now computed from actual work: 315000ms for 21 slots and 135000ms for 9 slots, both exactly 15000ms per slot, independent of `command_timeout_ms`. That is the fixed model and it works. But `deadline_command_slots` is `3600000 / 600000 = 6`, which is the OLD worst-case model, pricing every slot at the full command timeout. So the reserve says a 21-slot chain costs 315000ms out of 3600000, under nine percent, while admission says only 6 slots fit at all.

**2. The bound is impossible, not merely tight.** It reports a "0-member bound". Caravan 2233 has exactly ONE member and is reported `at_capacity: true` with the text "1 members already reach the 0-member bound". A zero-member capacity cannot be satisfied by any caravan including an empty one, so no member can ever be admitted regardless of drain. The stated remedy, "until a caravan drains", cannot help: draining to zero members still leaves a 0-member bound.

**3. Raising `command_timeout_secs` silently closed the queue.** `command_timeout_secs` moved 120 to 600 in checked-in config. Under the worst-case admission arithmetic that cut `deadline_command_slots` from 30 to 6, which is what produced the 0-member bound. An observer on a stale checkout with `command_timeout_secs: 120` concurrently reads `max_admissible_members: 12` against the identical binary, caravans, and moment, so the divergence is fully explained by that one config field feeding the unfixed admission path.

Requested repair:

- Compute admissible capacity from the same actual-work model that now produces `required_ms`, not from `deadline / command_timeout`. The two must not disagree by two orders of magnitude on the same chain.
- A capacity bound of zero should be impossible to emit. If the arithmetic produces a non-positive bound, that is a defect condition and should be reported as one, not as ordinary at-capacity gating with a drain suggestion that cannot work.
- `at_capacity` on a one-member caravan should be treated as a self-evident contradiction and fail loudly rather than quietly closing admission.
- Guidance text must not recommend an action that cannot resolve the condition it describes.

Live impact at time of filing: `blocked_candidate: 2234`, and candidates have been accumulating since roughly 08:00 UTC behind an earlier operator-directed merge freeze. Existing caravans can still drain, so this presents as a slow silent stall rather than an outage, and it will look like a fresh incident to anyone who sees the queue drain to empty and then refuse everything.

Evidence provenance: measured on the mutable cargo-installed `0.0.11` at `/home/harry/.cargo/bin/cara`, not the reviewed store closure. The reserve-side fix is likewise confirmed only on that build. Cross-vantage comparison contributed by the helsinki profile worker, whose stale `command_timeout_secs: 120` checkout served as the control arm that isolated the config dependency.


---

## Merged duplicate: bd-e99fe6

Title: Guarantee forward progress when caravan physical-sync reserve exceeds tick budget

Cara's correct all-or-nothing apply-budget refusal becomes a monotonic deadlock once a live caravan grows larger than `sync.max_duration_secs` can ever process.

Live Cacophony evidence:

```
physical_sync_budget_insufficient
4560000ms required, 3430138ms remaining (38 command slots)
```

Config: `sync.max_duration_secs: 3600`, `command_timeout_secs: 120`, `max_mutations_per_tick: 64`, `max_candidates_per_tick: 8`. Caravan2208 grew from 4 to 7 members while blocked. At seven members, Cara requires 76 minutes against a 60-minute deadline. Because every pass refuses before mutation, no member drains; because nothing drains, accepting more members only increases the required reserve. Scheduled and manual drivers hit the same bound.

The safety refusal is correct—never start an apply that might overrun mid-chain—but the system must preserve bounded forward progress.

Required, in order:

1. Prefer a checkpointed/resumable bounded-prefix apply: plan/verify the complete graph, reserve enough for an exact prefix plus durable checkpoint, apply strictly root-to-descendant, persist completed-prefix receipts before return, and resume idempotently next tick without replaying completed provider mutations.
2. If complete-graph all-or-nothing is architecturally required, compute maximum admissible chain size from the configured deadline before admission and refuse further joins with typed `caravan_budget_capacity_exhausted` evidence while allowing the existing processable prefix to drain.
3. Required/remaining budget must model actual operations, concurrency and already-completed checkpoints rather than a permanently increasing whole-chain worst case.
4. Preserve force-with-lease, exact provider revalidation, no manual reorder/eviction/split, and fail closed on drift/unknown receipts.
5. Status must expose required budget, processable prefix, blocked candidate, configured deadline and safe next action before the cliff, not only after a sync refusal.
6. Add tests for 1..N members around the threshold, interrupted prefix/resume, provider drift, CI/head transitions, independent caravans, candidate admission at capacity and no duplicate mutations.
7. Validate against the seven-member Cacophony caravan2208 without manually reordering its members.

A temporary deadline increase is an operator-owned stopgap only; it moves the cliff and is not completion. Current manual sync loop is paused to avoid burning rate limit on guaranteed no-write passes.

## Ratchet changes geometry when new arrivals form separate caravans

Observed after the budget refusal: `caravans` went from 1 to 2 with no sync driver running. The second caravan is a single member, PR `#2228`, an ordinary new publication that formed its own caravan rather than joining the deadlocked chain.

That matters for how this is fixed. The original recording of this deadlock assumed a single chain growing without bound until `required_ms` exceeds the deadline. If new arrivals instead form separate caravans, the first chain stops growing, which is better, but drain is still zero and the NUMBER of stuck units now increases rather than the size of one unit. Same deadlock, different geometry.

Consequence for acceptance criteria: a fix that only caps or resumes a single chain would not address the multi-caravan accumulation case. Whatever forward-progress mechanism is chosen should make progress across the set of caravans, not merely within one, and should be measured by total units drained rather than by whether any single chain can be applied.

Credit: observed and reasoned by the helsinki profile worker while under an explicit read-only watch, and verified independently by cluster control, which confirmed caravan 2228 has exactly one member and is an ordinary admission rather than a second sync actor.

## Exact mechanism: required_ms is command_slots x command_timeout_secs, a pure worst-case projection

Three measured datapoints from live refusals, contributed by the helsinki profile worker under a read-only watch, establish the formula precisely:

- 7 members, 38 slots: `4560000ms required` vs `3430138ms remaining`, short by 1129862
- 6 members, 32 slots: `3840000ms required` vs `3455426ms remaining`, short by 384574
- 6 members, 33 slots: `3960000ms required` vs `3425694ms remaining`, short by 534306

In every case `required_ms` equals `slots x 120000` exactly, where 120000 is `command_timeout_secs: 120`. So the reserved apply budget assumes EVERY command consumes its full timeout, and is not informed by observed latency at all. That is the root of the deadlock: real commands complete far faster, but the reserve is computed as though none do.

Two consequences that sharpen the fix options recorded above:

- raising `sync.max_duration_secs` is even more clearly a stopgap than stated. At 120s per slot you need `max_duration >= slots x 120s + planning`, so roughly every five additional slots costs another ten minutes of deadline, permanently.
- lowering `command_timeout_secs` has more leverage than the remedy text suggests, because it divides `required_ms` directly. At 100s, the current 33 slots would need 3300000ms and would fit inside the 3425694ms remaining with no other change. That is a genuine same-night unblock, but it trades against real provider and Git latency, so it needs an owner's judgement rather than a guess.
- the durable ask already recorded, reserving budget per unit of work actually attempted, is exactly right, because the entire gap here is worst-case versus actual.

Also confirmed: a drain does NOT reliably relieve the deadlock. Losing the root cut required_ms by roughly 600000 but left it short, and the requirement then rose again from 3840000 to 3960000 as one slot was added. The ratchet keeps climbing across a successful merge.

Planning consumption is real and must be included in any sizing: the 3600000ms deadline had already dropped to ~3425694ms remaining before apply was reserved.

## Fourth datapoint: formula holds, and parallel caravans do NOT compound the deficit

Datapoint 4 from the helsinki read-only watch: `3960000ms required vs 3429503ms remaining, 33 command slots`. 33 x 120000 = 3960000 exactly, a fourth consecutive exact hit, so `required_ms = command_slots x command_timeout_secs` has still not been falsified.

Full trend:

| slots | required | remaining | short by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 38 | 4560000 | 3430138 | 1129862 |
| 32 | 3840000 | 3455426 | 384574 |
| 33 | 3960000 | 3425694 | 534306 |
| 33 | 3960000 | 3429503 | 530497 |

Remaining is stable across passes at roughly 3425000 to 3455000, so planning consistently consumes about 145000 to 175000ms before apply is reserved. The deficit is therefore driven almost entirely by slot count and not by variable planning cost, which is good news for a fix: slots is the only lever that moves.

Important correction to the multi-caravan concern recorded earlier in this bead: on this pass `caravans` went 1 to 2 again while the SELECTED caravan stayed at 33 slots. The new caravan did not add slots to the selected one. Cluster control verified the second caravan is `2232`, a single member, PR `#2232` "fix(android): bound chat memory and OOM classification", an ordinary new publication.

So parallel caravans are NOT compounding the selected-chain deficit, which is consistent with the per-chain-prefix model in `ad14f74` treating independent chains separately. Accumulation shows up as more units rather than a larger selected unit. That materially narrows the fix: forward progress across the set still matters for total drain, but the deadlock itself is a single-chain slot-count problem, not a cross-chain summation problem.

## Second ratchet driver ISOLATED by controlled comparison: base drift, not chain growth

A controlled quiet-interval test isolates a second and previously unrecorded driver of the deadlock. Slot count changes ONLY when `main` moves, and holds exactly steady when `main` is quiet.

Paired series of (main head, slots):

- `b464e1ae5cb`, 38
- (root #2208 merged), 32
- `b464e1ae5cb`, 33
- `b464e1ae5cb`, 33 — main quiet, slots steady
- `9d6278a10f0`, 36 — main MOVED (release v1.2.1575), slots jumped 33 to 36
- `9d6278a10f0`, 36 — main quiet, slots steady

The decisive pass: two samples roughly 35 minutes apart on an unchanged base produced byte-identical projections, 4320000 required with remaining differing by only 438ms. That rules out a time-based or spontaneous ratchet.

Mechanism confirmed: projected apply cost rises with BASE DRIFT. Mechanism disproven: members re-parenting and consuming slots. Cluster control verified per-member state independently and found the chain stacked on each other's branches with only the root targeting `main`, and the root had NOT re-parented, still at head `2e02a53116` last updated 02:25:35Z with `ahead 2, behind 2` against `main` after the 03:30 release cut. So nothing consumed slots by doing work; the planner is pricing rebase work it has not performed and cannot start.

Why this matters for the fix, and it is worse than pure chain growth:

- unrelated `main` traffic increases projected cost while the chain simultaneously grows staler, because nothing applies the rebases. One event does both.
- a quiet `main` is stable but still deadlocked; a busy `main` actively worsens it.
- there is a perverse loop: a queue that cannot drain forces manual lands, manual lands move `main`, and every such move makes the queue more expensive to drain.

Consequence for acceptance criteria: capping chain size is necessary but NOT sufficient. A fix must also ensure projected cost does not grow unboundedly with base drift on a chain that is not being applied, for example by pricing only the prefix it intends to apply this pass, or by applying rebases incrementally so drift is retired rather than accumulated.

Formula confirmation continues: 36 x 120000 = 4320000, a sixth consecutive exact hit, so `ad14f74` has not yet reached the runtime in use (`cara 0.0.10`, consistent with `bd-bbc981` pending).

Credit: isolation designed and executed by the helsinki profile worker under a read-only watch, with per-member base state verified independently by cluster control.

## RETRACTION: the base-drift isolation above is FALSIFIED — do not act on it

The "second ratchet driver isolated" section above is WRONG and must not be used for fix design or deployment verification. Retracted by its own author on the next pass, and verified by cluster control.

Falsifying observation: `main` head was UNCHANGED at `9d6278a10f0` across three consecutive passes, yet slots jumped 36 to 42 on the third, `5040000ms required vs 3376327ms remaining`. Slots moved while `main` was quiet, which is exactly the outcome that was predicted to break the finding. `caravans` also went 2 to 3 active across that interval.

Why the earlier test was underpowered: the two quiet passes with steady slots showed only that slots do not drift spontaneously with TIME on an unchanged base AND unchanged membership. Membership happened to be static across both, so the test never controlled for it. The single 33 to 36 jump coincided with the v1.2.1575 release cut and was attributed to base drift, but membership change is an equally plausible and unexcluded explanation for that same jump.

Corrected position, deliberately weaker than before:

- `required_ms = command_slots x command_timeout_secs` remains solid, now seven consecutive exact hits including 42 x 120000 = 5040000.
- Slot count is NOT stable, and at least two candidate drivers remain plausible: chain or membership growth, now directly evidenced by a quiet-main pass with slots +6 and caravans +1; and base drift, still consistent with the per-member read but NOT established, since its only supporting datapoint is confounded with membership change.
- The deadlock persists across every observed configuration regardless of which driver dominates.

Consequence for the fix: do NOT scope acceptance to "cost must not grow with base drift" as though that were established. The durable requirements already recorded above stand on their own, since they address worst-case reserve versus actual work whatever moves the slot count. Isolating the driver requires holding membership constant, which no observer here can control.

Improvement adopted for future evidence: capture caravan COUNT and selected-chain membership alongside `(main head, slots)` on every pass, so a future jump can be attributed rather than inferred.

Recorded because the falsified version was previously written up here as a controlled comparison and routed onward; anyone who read it should re-read this section.

## Negative result: slot count varies with every sampled field held constant

A same-instant capture recorded slots moving 41 to 42, `required_ms` 4920000 to 5040000, while every other tracked field was unchanged:

- `main` unchanged at `9d6278a10f0`
- caravans unchanged at 3
- cara `merge_candidates` unchanged at 8, identical PR set `[2233,2232,2227,2225,2223,2215,2213,2210]`
- cara compatibility entries unchanged at 14
- daemon `ordered_candidates` unchanged at 5, with its `observed` timestamp genuinely advancing from 05:08:11 to 05:43:05

Combined with the earlier 42 to 41 decrease, every mechanism proposed during this investigation is now excluded for at least one observed transition:

| proposed driver | excluded by |
|---|---|
| base drift | both the 42→41 and 41→42 transitions, main quiet for both |
| membership growth | the 42→41 transition, membership independently confirmed at six |
| caravan count | the 41→42 transition, steady at 3 |
| candidate set/ordering | the 41→42 transition, identical 8-PR set |
| daemon ordered_candidates | the 41→42 transition, steady at 5 across a real refresh |

The honest conclusion is that slot count varies for reasons not visible in any field sampled here. No sixth mechanism is proposed. Note that CI check state is one dimension neither observer sampled, and PR check transitions did occur during this window; that is offered only as an unsampled dimension, NOT as a proposed cause.

Directly actionable consequence for anyone sizing a stopgap: slots have been observed at 33, 36, 41 and 42, with `main` quiet for most of that range. Any `sync.max_duration_secs` or `command_timeout_secs` value sized against a single observed slot count will be wrong within about an hour. A stopgap must carry headroom above the observed range rather than tracking the current reading, and even then it only moves the cliff.

This also reinforces requirement 3 above: a reserve computed from a quantity that moves unpredictably, while assuming every command consumes its full timeout, cannot be made safe by tuning. It has to be replaced by a reserve tied to work actually attempted.

Formula status: twelfth consecutive exact hit, 42 x 120000 = 5040000, so `ad14f74` had still not reached the observed runtime at this point.

## Head-of-line handoff gap REPRODUCED: autonomous root merge twice, autonomous handoff zero times

The deadlock's user-visible signature has now been observed twice in one night with identical shape, which upgrades it from an incident to a reproduced defect.

Occurrence 1: root `#2208` merged natively once green; caravan re-formed as `2210`; the base retarget to `main` and the squash re-arm were then performed BY HAND by the member's owner after `cara sync` refused pre-mutation on the budget reserve.

Occurrence 2: root `#2210` merged natively at 06:03:38 with all checks green and no intervention; `main` advanced to `176fd149d37ecbcf7b7b90652dde277a80abb7ec`; the caravan re-formed as `2213` with five members `[2213, 2215, 2223, 2225, 2227]`. Canonical immediately went degraded with exactly two problems:

```
dangling_base: PR #2213 still targets merged predecessor #2210; sync must advance it to `main`
auto_merge_invariant: caravan head #2213 must have squash auto-merge enabled
```

Verified independently: `#2213` is OPEN and CLEAN with zero failing and zero pending checks, its base is still the agent branch of its predecessor rather than `main`, and it has no auto-merge armed.

What this establishes:

- Automatic ROOT MERGE works and is proven twice. Given an armed root and green required checks, the provider lands it with no operator or sync involvement.
- Automatic CHAIN HANDOFF has never once occurred. Both times, the two repairs that promote the next member to root, base retarget and root arming, were left undone because physical sync refuses before its mutation phase.
- The two failures are therefore not independent. The budget refusal is precisely what prevents the handoff, so every root merge produces a degraded queue that then requires manual repair to continue.

Consequence for acceptance: a canary or proof that only observes "the root merged" is measuring the half that already works. The falsifiable criterion is that after a root merges, the successor is advanced to `main` and armed WITHOUT manual intervention. That has zero successful observations to date.

Deliberately NOT repaired by hand on this occurrence, so the reproduction is preserved as evidence rather than overwritten.

## The deadline is never fully available: a chain sized exactly to max_duration_secs still cannot start

A later observation reduces this from a large structural gap to a marginal one, and in doing so exposes a clean off-by-planning defect in the admission arithmetic.

Measured: 30 slots, `required_ms = 3600000`, `remaining = 3416655`, short by only 183345. Every earlier pass was short by between 384574 and 1557755.

Two arithmetic consequences, both derived purely from observed numbers rather than any proposed mechanism:

1. At 30 slots the projection is EXACTLY 3600000ms, which is exactly the configured `sync.max_duration_secs: 3600`. So a chain sized precisely to the entire deadline still cannot begin, because planning has already consumed roughly 183000ms before the apply reserve is computed. The reserve is checked against REMAINING budget while the admissible chain size is implicitly reasoned about against TOTAL budget. The two are never equal, so the effective capacity is strictly less than the configured deadline and always will be. Any capacity calculation, cap, or stopgap that uses `max_duration_secs` directly is off by the planning cost.
2. At 28 slots the projection would be 3360000ms, which fits inside the observed 3416655ms remaining. So the chain is roughly two slots from being able to mutate unaided, and may simply begin working after another member or two drains, with no config change at all.

Point 1 should be treated as a durable requirement rather than an observation. Whatever replaces the current reserve must either compare like with like, by computing admissible size against budget actually remaining at reserve time, or must reserve planning explicitly so the comparison is honest. Otherwise the boundary condition is permanently unreachable and the system is guaranteed to refuse a chain it was configured to accept.

Point 2 is also a caution for interpreting any future success. If the queue starts moving after further drain, that is NOT evidence that a deployed fix worked. It would be the chain falling below the marginal threshold on its own. Distinguishing the two requires the behavioural check recorded elsewhere in this bead: a `required_ms` that is no longer an exact multiple of `command_timeout_secs`.

Successor criterion at this point, independently verified by cluster control across all five remaining members:

| PR | mergeStateStatus | armed | base |
|---|---|---|---|
| #2213 | CLEAN | false | `agent/ms-dev-3/...8x5t4` (predecessor #2210 MERGED) |
| #2215 | CLEAN | false | `agent/ms-dev-3/...h8e3r` |
| #2223 | CLEAN | false | `agent/ms-dev-6/...d23tq` |
| #2225 | CLEAN | false | `agent/ms-dev-6/...v2dom` |
| #2227 | UNSTABLE | false | `agent/ms-dev-5/...3ru8p` |

Four of five are CLEAN, unarmed, and dangling on a predecessor branch. Nothing advanced any base or armed anything autonomously in roughly the first hour after the root merged. Formula status at this point: fifteenth consecutive exact hit, 30 x 120000 = 3600000.

## RESOLVED IN BEHAVIOUR: the predicted discriminator fired positive on 0.0.11

The falsifiable test specified earlier in this bead has now run and returned the passing result.

Test as specified in advance: on `0.0.10` the reserve was `required_ms = command_slots x command_timeout_secs` exactly, sixteen consecutive exact hits. The agreed discriminator was that a `required_ms` which is NOT a flat multiple of `command_timeout_secs` proves the bounded-prefix work is live, while an exact multiple would mean the binary changed but the reserve logic did not.

Measured by cluster control via read-only `cara status --json` in the canonical daemon checkout, at main `7c0bb4158e13ce20673b3a62699fdfef827406dc`:

```
sync_budget.command_timeout_ms = 600000
sync_budget.deadline_ms        = 3600000
caravan 2215: required_ms = 315000, retained_ms = 240000, processable_prefix = [2215, 2223, 2225, 2227]
caravan 2233: required_ms = 135000, retained_ms = 105000, processable_prefix = [2233]
```

Neither 315000 nor 135000 is a multiple of 600000. Under the old model a four-member chain at a 600000ms command timeout would have reserved several million milliseconds against a 3600000ms deadline and refused before mutation, as it did all night at 120000ms per slot. Instead it reserves 315000ms, under nine percent of the deadline, and publishes an explicit processable prefix covering all four members.

This satisfies the substance of requirements 1, 3 and 5 recorded above: the reserve now models work actually attempted rather than a whole-chain worst case, a processable prefix is exposed in status rather than only after a refusal, and the deadlock condition no longer arises for these chains.

Three caveats deliberately attached:

- The runtime measured is the MUTABLE cargo-installed `0.0.11` at `/home/harry/.cargo/bin/cara`, not the reviewed store closure. This is evidence that the CODE behaves correctly. It is NOT evidence that the reviewed artifact is deployed; that claim belongs to the Cacophony-side deployment bead and remains unproven.
- Config changed underneath the measurement series. `command_timeout_secs` is now 600 on main and canonical while the sixteen-hit baseline was taken at 120, and `sync.max_duration_secs` was briefly 65525 before being corrected to 3600 at commit `7c0bb4158e13`. The discriminator survives this because it is stated as "not a flat multiple of `command_timeout_secs`, whatever that value is", rather than as a literal 120000.
- Admission remains closed: `max_admissible_members = 0` with at-capacity wording, so existing caravans can drain but new members cannot join. Whether that is intended gating or a second independent bound is not established here.

Credit: the discriminator was formulated by the helsinki profile worker from the original `required_ms = slots x command_timeout_secs` derivation, generalised by it to be independent of the literal timeout value, and specified before the fix was observable, which is what makes this a test rather than a post-hoc reading.

## Reopened: admission capacity still uses legacy full-timeout slots

Canonical Cacophony config now has `sync.max_duration_secs=3600`, `command_timeout_secs=600`; Cara0.0.11 proportional reserve defaults to 15 seconds per command. Read-only canonical status proves physical prefixes work: caravan2215 has 21 required slots but `required_ms=315000`, and 16 retained slots give `retained_ms=240000`, both exactly 15s/slot with the full four-member prefix processable.

However `max_admissible_members()` still calls `deadline_command_slots()`, which divides the deadline by the full child timeout: `3600/600=6`. The minimum ordinary chain-capacity shape exceeds six slots, so capacity is projected as zero and every nonempty caravan is `at_capacity`. `blocked_candidate=2234` and `caravan_budget_capacity_exhausted` close joins even though the same status proves the existing chain fits comfortably under the proportional reserve.

This is a mixed-model regression: apply/drain budgeting uses the landed proportional reserve while admission capacity retains the retired worst-case timeout arithmetic. With no caravans, one independent root may still start, but it cannot accept a second member; normal batching collapses to serial one-member caravans.

Required:

- derive `max_admissible_members` from the same proportional reserve/model used by `admit_physical_prefix`, or deterministically simulate the hardest one-pending-member shape through that model;
- retain worst-case timeout only as evidence, never as the admission bound;
- preserve fail-closed zero capacity only when the proportional model truly cannot process one member;
- tests for deadline3600/timeout600/reserve15 expecting positive multi-member capacity and consistency between projected capacity, processable prefix and typed refusal;
- status must not say a full processable prefix is simultaneously over a zero-member bound;
- preserve existing new-independent-caravan and real no-progress safeguards.

Runtime provenance caveat: measurement used mutable cargo Cara0.0.11, not reviewed store deployment, but source inspection independently confirms the mixed formulas in `src/sync/budget.rs`.
