title: [broken-on-main] Cara repair cold clone cannot survive provider SSH sideband disconnect
description:
## Live failure

Caco-merger independently verified Caravan bd-9264d0 deployment before retrying PR #1962:

- Caravan canonical local and `origin/main` matched `35dffd1488efae1402dc2106987005f1d89641e9`.
- Wrapper-sanitized Cara reported version 0.0.2.
- The stale preparing session targeting old Cacophony main `23369cbb` was inspected, then first-party `repair abort --confirm` succeeded with `workspace_removed=true` and `provider_mutated=false`.
- One fresh repair start re-read exact PR head `05fe82fe80c692613463a888bd4df5bc34d4ddee` and target main `90bebd5c`.
- Its isolated SSH clone failed after 180469ms with `fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet`; the process group was reaped and the manifest remained in typed `preparing/cloning` state.
- Following the exact typed resume hint, one same-session resume failed identically after 180458ms and reaped its process group.
- No third attempt, raw fallback, workspace edit, or provider mutation occurred. PR #1962 remains open at the exact head with auto-merge disabled. Session `pr-1962-05fe82fe80c6` preserves the clone error, partial path, and target `90bebd5c`.

The longer timeout/resume work is functioning as designed, but a full cold SSH clone remains unusable under a persistent provider sideband disconnect. Repeating the same full clone is not a recovery strategy.

## Required outcome

- Replace full cold clone with minimal exact materialization where supported: initialize the isolated repository and fetch only the recorded PR head and target/base OIDs/refs, preferably with provider-supported partial/blobless filtering and no checkout until verification.
- Make the partial repository resumable in place after transport interruption. A same-session retry must reuse already received verified objects rather than deleting and retransferring the whole repository.
- Classify provider transport disconnect separately from wall-clock timeout, preserving stderr/classification/elapsed budget and a bounded retry/resume hint.
- Optionally seed from a canonical verified provider checkout or shared object cache/alternates, but re-read the configured provider remote and exact head/target before use; never trust daemon-internal refs as publication proof.
- Use bounded SSH keepalive/low-speed/progress settings where appropriate, with no unbounded loops and no global SSH/Git config mutation.
- Preserve existing process-group reap, manifest atomicity, exact identity/drift checks, abort semantics, and no-provider-mutation guarantee.
- Add fixtures where the first fetch disconnects mid-sideband and exact resume completes from partial objects, plus head/target drift refusal and repeated-disconnect bounded failure.
- Prove canonical packaged-binary repair start/status/resume/abort against the fixture and publish a landed SHA/version receipt before live PR #1962 retry. No raw Git/worktree fallback is allowed.

title: Recover verified-stale Caravan operation locks safely
description:
Live bd-322e38 outer-killed cara split left .git/caravan/operation.lock owned by dead PID 40920. After the 30-minute stale threshold, every mutation reports stale_operation_lock, but cara has no guarded inspect/clear command; caco agent reap-lock correctly targets Git index.lock and cannot recover this product lock. Add a first-party cara lock status/recovery surface or safe stale takeover requiring age plus dead-owner verification and token compare, with tests that never reap a live owner. Current canonical shared checkout lock must be cleared only through controller/operator-safe recovery, not raw worker deletion.

Post-land Nix sandbox acceptance exposed a remaining portability gap: process liveness used external `ps`, which is absent from the hermetic macOS package build, causing both recovery tests to fail with `git_spawn_failed`. Replace the shell probe with a direct cross-platform process primitive (no PATH/runtime dependency), add the dependency to the pinned build, and prove `nix flake check` on macOS before re-closing.

title: Add bounded event journal with cara log and cara log -f
description:
Operator-requested observability surface after live v1 parity. Persist every canonical secret-free CaravanEvent (including decision/error events) to a versioned append-only repository journal before configured hook delivery, preserving exact event_id and operation_id and never inventing queue authority. Add `cara log` as a bounded human/--json snapshot (safe default limit, kind/PR/time filters, deterministic ordering) and `cara log -f`/`--follow` as a foreground signal-aware stream that prints existing tail then new records without corrupting an active append. Keep unbounded follow out of MCP; expose only the bounded snapshot as an MCP tool with input/output schemas. Journal storage must live under common Git metadata, handle concurrent append/read safely, recover from a truncated final record, enforce configurable bounded retention/rotation, never contain hook stdout/stderr or secrets, and report journal I/O failure without pretending completed GitHub mutations rolled back. Include event+hook-delivery visibility, exact-ID dedup tests, two-process/follow tests, rotation/truncation tests, docs, and live dogfood receipts.

title: Make semantic grant apply and revoke recover from partial persistence
description:
A bounded post-landing audit of `bd-17375b` found two partial-persistence states that the public grant/revoke commands cannot currently reconcile.

1. In `src/repair.rs:1099-1133`, `grant_paths` persists new receipts with `applied: false`, writes/stages each expected blob, then persists `applied: true`. If the second manifest write fails after `git add`, the next identical grant call observes `baseline_oid == expected_result_oid` and takes the idempotent `continue` branch without setting the existing receipt to `applied: true`. It can return `already_applied: true`, while `repair continue` remains permanently blocked by `repair_grant_incomplete`.

2. In `src/repair.rs:1218-1267`, `revoke_grants` validates and mutates one path at a time. A later actor/drift/write failure can leave earlier paths revoked, making an exact retry fail with `repair_grant_not_found`. A manifest-write failure after restoring/staging the baseline but before removing the receipt leaves the receipt expecting the semantic result, so retry fails with `repair_grant_result_drift`.

Make both commands resumable and receipt-driven across every persisted/index state, preferably by validating the whole requested set before mutation and explicitly reconciling `(receipt.applied, actual index OID)` states. Add fault-injection tests around manifest publication after staging and a multi-path revocation where a later path fails. Preserve the fail-closed scope and provider non-mutation guarantees.

2026-07-21 burn-down triage: promoted from draft for v0.0.6 because this is a concrete repair-session correctness hole with known persisted-state reproductions; implementation remains isolated from msm1's owned physical-rebase work.

title: Allow forced self-update into a user-owned PATH directory
description: Depends on updatable-cli/bd-e195f5 (install to an explicit target directory). Today self-update refuses with self_update_package_managed when the running binary is Nix or Homebrew managed. That is correct about never writing into the store, but leaves no escape hatch when the pin lags the release: an operator on a /nix/store caravan 0.0.7 binary had no first-party way to run a newer Cara without a full rebuild. Operator direction 2026-07-27: a forced update must NOT rewrite the store; it downloads into a user-owned directory that PATH already prefers, leaving the package-managed binary untouched underneath. Required: never write into /nix/store or a Homebrew cellar under any flag, since a store path whose contents no longer match its hash is a corrupted closure; install into a user-owned directory defaulting to ~/.local/bin and overridable explicitly; verify that directory actually PRECEDES the package-managed binary in the effective PATH before writing and refuse with exact evidence otherwise, because a silent no-op update is worse than a refusal; emit a loud typed receipt naming both resolved paths, both versions and the artifact hash recording that the new binary shadows a package-managed one; keep it trivially reversible so deleting the file restores the package-managed binary. Safety context: this is the shadowing behind the ms-dev-2 incident where a cargo-installed 0.0.10 sat ahead of the reviewed store 0.0.8, segfaulted under nix-ld with empty output, and looked like a quiet queue for hours. Runtime provenance shipped in v0.0.11 makes shadowing provable from any status receipt, so the forced path must surface that evidence rather than hide it. Document plainly that a forced install is a temporary local override and the durable fix is updating the package pin.

title: Ineligible candidates must not wedge automatic admission
description:
Live Cacophony dogfood: `cara sync --all` reported no caravans with auto-admission enabled, continuation=RejectedCanonicalCandidate, considered=0, joins=0, while 14 structurally valid unqueued candidates existed (2101, 2108, 2113, 2115, 2117, 2119, 2122, 2141, 2145, 2147, 2149, 2151, 2152, 2154).

The canonical attempt resolved to PR 2107, which is rejected as ambiguous_generation; 2109/2112 are ambiguous and 2153 has invalid generation metadata. Every rejection currently keeps blocks_order=true, so one permanently ineligible PR starves the whole fleet and no root caravan is ever created.

## Required behavior

Only PRs that could actually be admitted form the ordered admission attempt list. Structurally ineligible candidates (draft, fork-only, externally enabled auto-merge, superseded/ambiguous/invalid Cacophony generation) are reported with exact reasons but excluded from ordering, so the first eligible candidate becomes canonical and sync proceeds normally, including physical rebase onto the exact current default when it creates a new root caravan.

Rank-indeterminate priority metadata (unknown or conflicting configured labels) must still block, because canonical order cannot be computed. Preserve no-leapfrogging for eligible candidates whose exact mechanical attempt failed: that remains the generation-bound `caravan-join-skipped` receipt path.

## Acceptance

Hermetic fixtures prove a wedging ineligible head does not block a later eligible candidate, conflicting/unknown priority still blocks, mechanical skip receipts still prevent leapfrogging, and the live Cacophony fleet selects an eligible canonical candidate again. Update SPEC, README, and embedded help wording.

title: Order automatic admission by agent priority then FIFO
description:
Operator correction from first Cacophony use: automatic admission is never LIFO. GitHub remains authoritative. Define a GitHub-visible explicit agent-priority policy (for example ordered configurable priority labels); candidates with higher explicit agent priority come first, ties and candidates without priority are FIFO by PR creation time/monotonic PR number, oldest first. Expose the resolved ordered candidate list and per-PR reason in status/JSON/MCP so Cacophony selects the canonical first candidate rather than inventing its own order. Add a nonmutating next-candidate surface if needed for safe automation. Preserve explicit operator canary selection as an override only when a reason is supplied and commented on the PR via bd-dc3983. Add deterministic tests where newer PRs cannot leapfrog older equal-priority PRs, priority can deliberately override FIFO, and invalid/conflicting priority labels fail closed. Update SPEC to state priority-then-FIFO explicitly and live-prove on Cacophony's ready PR set.

---

## Exact operator contract — 2026-07-18 02:46 BST

Queue age is immutable GitHub PR `created_at` ascending. PR number ascending is the deterministic tie-break after explicit agent priority. Head commit timestamps and PR `updatedAt` are forbidden ordering inputs. Cacophony must consume the upcoming Cara `next-candidate` result without local re-sorting. Additional automatic admissions are frozen under Cacophony hold `hold-caravan-admission-ordering` until this bead lands and the live read-only candidate canary passes.

title: Implement reviewed Cara force-intent preview/apply contract required by Caco
description:
## Live blocker

Cacophony's reviewed first-party exception surface (`caco cara force-preview|force-apply|force-revoke`, SPEC 17.2 / bd-2d33b0) invokes the configured pinned Cara wrapper as:

`cara --json force-intent preview|apply|revoke --pr ... --head ... --membership-generation ... --failure-fingerprint ... --reason ... --expires-at-ms ... --auto-merge squash`

Reviewed Cara v0.0.7 rejects `force-intent` as an unrecognized subcommand. Caravan true main `657fb201d1f426de5fcf16339e56a1f4250c3bad` still only exposes the older `force arm|revoke` label surface in `src/force.rs`; it has no membership generation, required-check/decision `fnv1a64` fingerprint, bounded expiry, preview, or atomic force-intent-plus-squash-auto-merge receipt. Therefore Caco's audited force path cannot preview or apply any exact PR, despite being published and specified.

## Exact incident

PR #2120 head `4b5ddd6a9f1d61599d68ccd05e5c831dba1fc239` is an operator/controller-classified CI/control-plane blocker. Fresh true main `6bf8d95128a4e69a5e8517b5b69dc490caa16da0`, clean merge-tree `be437cc6244c9caace9f62deb85a207beff38eb3`, focused 40/40, clippy/rustfmt/SPEC green, and provider failure isolated to merge-ref fetch disconnect. Standing bounded force authority requires the typed force-preview/apply lane, but the reviewed Cara command needed to obtain/validate membership generation and failure fingerprint does not exist. No provider mutation attempted.

## Required behavior

- Implement exact `force-intent preview|apply|revoke` CLI/JSON/MCP parity matching Caco's published arguments and evidence validator.
- Every action independently re-reads exact provider PR/head, current membership generation, required checks, and current decision; stale supplied values fail closed with typed current evidence.
- Preview never mutates and returns exact `membership`, `required_checks`, `current_decision`, shared `fnv1a64` failure fingerprint, and expiry.
- Apply performs one atomic reviewed provider transaction recording exact-head force intent plus squash auto-merge and returns proof fields required by Caco.
- Revoke is idempotent, exact-generation, and rollback-safe even after expiry.
- Add drift/race/replay/expiry/no-op tests and preserve normal queue ownership.
- Include this fix in the sole reviewed Cara successor release tracked by `caravan/bd-1a7201`; no mutable-head/source fallback.
creator: helsinki:cacophony:helsinki-cacophony-cluster-ctrl

title: Budget and reduce authenticated GitHub API usage
description:
## Observed problem

During the post-v0.0.4 audit, authenticated GitHub requests exhausted the shared user-ID API quota. Cara does authenticate `gh` subprocesses: it validates ambient `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`, otherwise resolves a repository-accessible `gh auth` account token and injects it. The issue is query volume and many processes/agents sharing one user bucket, not anonymous access. A single Cacophony `cara status` took about 12.8 seconds and multiple separate `status`/`next-candidate`/`check` calls each rediscovered overlapping repository, open-PR, check, label, default-ref, merge-candidate, and history facts.

## Required outcome

- Add secret-free API budget telemetry to status/check/sync/loop receipts: auth kind/login or app installation identity (never token), GraphQL cost/remaining/reset, REST remaining/reset when available, calls by phase, cache hits, and bounded exhaustion continuation.
- Include GraphQL `rateLimit { cost remaining resetAt }` in existing queries without a separate probe; parse REST rate headers where practical.
- Reuse one exact discovery snapshot throughout a bounded sync/auto-admission tick. Batch repository/PR/check/merge-candidate/history facts and avoid repeated full discovery within one unchanged generation. Mutation boundaries must rediscover exact affected provider facts.
- Add bounded generation-aware caches for read-only snapshots and REST ETags/conditional requests where supported. Never use stale cache as mutation authority.
- Make loop back off adaptively near quota reset and prefer event-driven wakes. Rate exhaustion is a typed waiting/retry result, not an LLM repair decision and never authorizes mutation from stale state.
- Avoid spending an API call solely to validate auth on every short-lived Cara process when the first real request can provide exact access failure, while preserving safe multi-account repository selection.
- Support GitHub App installation-token operation for automation, using a token helper/environment rather than secrets in `.caravan/config.yaml`. Document GitHub Actions `actions/create-github-app-token` or equivalent, least-privilege permissions, installation-bucket behavior, and user-token fallback.
- Ensure one Cara loop/controller is the recommended polling owner; other agents consume its durable snapshot/journal rather than independently polling.

Test shared user quota exhaustion, app installation identity, GraphQL and REST budgets, cache generation invalidation, webhook wake coalescing, adaptive backoff, exact reread before mutation, and no secret leakage. A GitHub App is desirable for a separate least-privilege installation bucket and webhooks, but must not substitute for reducing API volume.

title: Make sync rebuild a real rebased chain after parent head changes
description:
Operator-directed live Cacophony gap after bd-49a809 closed. Harry expects one bounded `cara sync --all` to repair/rebase the whole active chain in parallel, rather than requiring the merger agent to inspect and update every PR manually.

Live reproduction with packaged Cara 0.0.2: Cacophony caravan `[1972,1962,1959,1958,1946]` was clean until merger repaired PR #1972 from `3f245f7066becbb6fec1d98fe9528c6c8a88fef6` to `e635eeb33ae78d9829b0f5c2a485b32681c860b6`. PR #1962 still represented the prior parent generation. `cara status` reported `incompatible` for `[1972,1962]`; `cara sync --all` returned `link_conflict` with conflicting paths `README.md` and `SPEC.md`, no provider receipts, and suggested manual checkout/repair. It did not rebuild descendants.

The deployed Cacophony `.caravan/config.yaml` has `force_merge: true` but no `rebase_on_join`; bd-49a809 defined that mode with safe default false. This creates an operator-visible rollout/behavior gap: sync silently falls back to manual link-conflict repair instead of making the requested whole-chain mode and remediation explicit.

Acceptance:
- When `rebase_on_join: true`, `sync --all` must build a complete root-to-tail rebase plan against exact current parent OIDs, preflight every edge/conflict and all force-with-lease ownership/permission guards before the first write, then rebuild eligible independent steps with bounded safe parallelism while preserving dependency order.
- Each rewritten PR emits old/new head, parent, lease, base, exact provider receipts, and invalidates prior CI; descendants are rediscovered after each generation and receive fresh exact-head CI.
- A conflict stops before mutating that edge or its descendants and returns exact files plus the retained successfully rebuilt prefix.
- When the mode is absent/false, `status`, `check`, and `sync` must explicitly report `rebase_on_join=disabled` and the exact project-config action rather than implying the agent should hand-rebase every edge.
- Add a Cacophony-shaped five-member fixture covering parent-head repair, whole-chain rebuild, no partial writes on preflight conflict, stale remote head, moved main, and rerun idempotency.
- Document the safe canary/rollback for enabling this mode in an existing project. Do not weaken fork, ownership, dirty-worktree, conflict, or force-with-lease guards.

This is distinct from bd-49a809's implementation slice: it tracks sync orchestration, bounded parallelism, explicit disabled-mode diagnostics, and live rollout behavior proven missing in Cacophony.

Additional operator acceptance 2026-07-18: handle merged-head promotion/retarget, not only in-place parent-head repair. Exact live target is merged #1972 -> active successor #1962 -> child #1959. Whole-chain planning must use a verified retained refs/pull/<merged>/head range boundary if the merged predecessor branch was deleted, rebuild #1962 onto exact main, rebuild #1959 onto planned #1962, then midpoint rediscovery and existing ensure_base(main) retarget must consume fresh facts. Verify this exact chain live after implementation/deploy; keep repair-workspace work in bd-cf44d1 separate.

Implementation generation a28453d on main@eb77ec7: split physical rebase into PreparedRebase/RebasePlan/apply with retained worktree objects (no recomputation); distinct remote/simulated parent OIDs; verified merged-predecessor refs/pull/<n>/head range source; complete selected-chain planning and global default/PR/branch/dry-run lease barrier before writes; all-member auto-merge disable after barrier; dependency-ordered apply with max-2 parallel independent chains; exact partial prefix receipts on apply race; mandatory midpoint rediscovery/head verification before existing sync CI/base/auto-merge policy; typed plans/receipts/checkpoints/CLI; MutationKind::RebaseBranch; 1972→1962→1959→1958→1946-shaped fixture, deleted merged predecessor promotion, conflict zero-write, apply-time lease race, idempotent wrapper tests; canary/rollback docs. Strict all-target clippy, 222 all-target tests, and Darwin flake check green before final apply-target guard; focused physical 5/5 green after guard.

Post-land live read-only verification using ff66a89 binary against canonical Cacophony checkout: status exits 0 and explicitly reports rebase_on_join disabled with exact config action. Active caravan is [1962,1959,1958,1946]. #1962 is promoted/retargeted to main@cff967990a08e7fad3f78979616917018bd7c449 with head 05fe82fe80c692613463a888bd4df5bc34d4ddee; #1959 base is that exact #1962 branch/OID and head d95f2de64871549adcc72c3f8266cc11b478f3e4. All four live compatibility edges are clean. Remaining status issue is expected auto_merge_invariant on #1962 (auto-merge disabled during manual recovery), and both #1962/#1959 have empty fresh CI pending rollout. No live mutation was attempted because deployed config still omits opt-in; enabling current post-land main now requires explicit canary config authorization.

title: Classify nonlinear physical-rebase history as an external decision
description:
Post-eb6c581 live acceptance on Cacophony #1958 proves the stale-default lease fix works narrowly: status saw historical base e1f87cd and current default 172de05, and sync progressed beyond the former repeated `rebase_stale_lease`. It then failed before mutation with deterministic `rebase_nonlinear_range` because exact head 6c89535 contains six merge commits in the candidate-only range. Scheduler incorrectly classified this immutable exact-generation failure as retryable `retry_tick`, even though rediscovery/retry cannot change it.

Fix scheduler/error policy so `rebase_nonlinear_range` and other deterministic unsupported-history/range-shape failures are `external_decision` (or operator_action where appropriate), emit exactly one canonical sync-failed decision event, and carry bounded exact merge OIDs, affected PR/caravan, candidate/base/default generations, zero-mutation receipt, and actionable continuations. Do not wake on true provider races or waiting CI, and do not imply retry can succeed without a head/config/strategy change.

Acceptance:
- Exact unchanged nonlinear head returns external_decision, retryable=false, with repair/reshape/evict or audited merge-preserving-strategy choices.
- A provider head/default race remains retry_tick.
- Repeated tick on unchanged head dedupes the external decision without mutation.
- Live fixture mirrors #1958: completed_steps/provider/rebase receipts empty and no provider state changes.
- Focused scheduler/hook tests and docs/help update.

Live outcome after filing: cluster control had already authorized one exact-head canonical Cara force for #1958 before the later no-force message arrived. A force-only config explicitly disabled rebase_on_join and auto-admission, retained exact head/base/default revalidation, posted the durable force audit, and admin-squash merged only #1958 at provider merge commit 2e20ed68244490194d79270d3fda2ce30c0a811d. No cumulative rewrite was attempted and no other PR mutated. This removes #1958 as the live blocker but does not remove the scheduler defect: an unchanged rebase_nonlinear_range still must not be labelled retryable/retry_tick in future occurrences.

title: Treat candidates contained in an already-merged PR as superseded
description: Confirmed NOT fixed on main at 7e56547. Generation integrity is computed only from open PRs: github.rs open_generation_facts / pull_requests_with_generation build facts from the open-PR query, so generation::analyze never sees a merged predecessor. A candidate whose exact commits are strictly contained in an already-merged PR therefore stays a live ordered admission attempt instead of being structurally ineligible with blocks_order=false, exactly as open supersession already behaves. Required: extend containment evidence to merged same-stream PRs using exact merge commit/tree/patch evidence, classify the contained candidate superseded_generation with a precise reason and safe next action, exclude it from ordering rather than wedging the queue, and never auto-close it. title: Unwind stack descendants when a member is evicted
description:
PARTIAL: the evidence half is landed on main; the automatic descendant rewrite is NOT, and one concrete blocker is now known.

LANDED (103c7c4): eviction reports descendants_inheriting_evicted_patch in the typed receipt and human output, naming exactly which members were physically rebased onto the evicted PR and therefore still carry its commits, plus the unwind instruction. Previously the receipt implied a clean removal that had not happened, which is how discarded ancestor content silently reached main.

ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED, with findings worth keeping. I wired a RewriteContext (repository_path, timeout, rebase_on_join) through reshape::execute and added unwind_descendants(), which walks descendants in order using PlannedRangeBase::RemoteBranch{evicted head} as the exact range boundary and PlannedBase::Simulated for each rewritten predecessor, verifying every prepared rewrite before applying any so a stack is never half-unwound. That compiled, passed existing reshape tests, and was strict-Clippy clean.

It was reverted because the new fixture did not prove the intended behaviour: rebasing a descendant with range base = evicted head onto the exact target produced commit_count=1 (correct: only the descendant own commit was replayed) but the resulting tree STILL contained the evicted member file, and the new head parent was neither the target OID nor the evicted head OID. Until that is explained, the rewrite must not ship: it force-pushes other owners branches, so an unproven range boundary is exactly the failure mode that reintroduces discarded content.

NEXT SESSION START HERE: reproduce with fixture() in src/physical_rebase.rs, branch `evicted` off main adding one file, branch `descendant` off it adding another, then prepare_candidate(descendant, RemoteBranch{evicted head}, Remote(main@new_main), default). Inspect why new_head^ is not the target. Suspect the range/target resolution in prepare_candidate treats PlannedRangeBase::RemoteBranch differently from the sync chain path, which passes range_base_for_rewritten_parent instead. Compare against the sync chain rebuild, which is the proven production path for exactly this shape.

Meanwhile bd-e9187e cascade eviction gives operators a safe way to release descendants rather than inherit a stale patch.

title: Provide a managed clean repair workspace for Cara sync decision recovery
description:
## Live Cacophony canary failure

On 2026-07-18, `cara status` correctly detected caravan `1962 -> 1959 -> 1958 -> 1946`, with PR 1962 still targeting merged predecessor 1972. `cara sync --all` could not advance it from either available Cacophony controller workspace:

1. The managed controller checkout was dirty with broad unrelated tracked/untracked state, so Cara returned `dirty_worktree`.
2. A first-party `caco project checkout` could not pass provider initialization (`gh repo view` reported that no configured remote pointed to a known GitHub host).
3. The controller therefore created a raw detached `.cara-clean` git worktree, manually fetched the exact PR head, manually updated the local branch ref after `local_branch_diverged`, and manually merged `origin/main` before resolving the typed `head_conflict` in README.md and SPEC.md.

This is the unsafe escape hatch the Cacophony merger contract forbids. Cara found the right decision but did not provide a first-party owned workspace/continue path in which the agent could repair it.

## Required outcome

- Add a Cara-owned isolated repair workspace for mutating `sync`, or integrate with a declared managed-checkout provider so ordinary dirty controller state is irrelevant.
- Fetch/check out the exact provider PR head using an expected-head receipt without requiring callers to run raw `git update-ref`.
- After the operator/agent resolves a typed conflict, provide an explicit verify-and-continue command that checks expected remote head, patch scope, conflict markers, and branch ancestry before non-force publication and resumes `sync --all`.
- Preserve the worktree and emit bounded recovery instructions on interruption; never leave an untracked nested worktree in the controller checkout.
- Add fixtures covering dirty caller checkout, daemon/internal remotes, locally divergent PR refs, and resume after a two-file head conflict.
- Keep semantic conflict resolution agent-owned; this bead is about safe workspace and resumability, not auto-guessing content.

Audit receipt from caco-ctrl replay: the controller did invoke Cara first (`cara status --json`, then `cara sync --all --json`) and respected typed stops for missing initialization, dirty worktree, local branch divergence, and `head_conflict`. The failure is end-to-end recovery: `caco project checkout` could not initialize because its internal remote was not GitHub-recognized, and Cara exposed no owned repair workspace/continue operation. caco-ctrl then crossed the safety boundary into `git worktree add --detach .cara-clean`, manual exact fetch/update-ref, raw merge/conflict edits/commit, branch push, and repeated Cara sync. Thus discovery/decision use was correct; repair execution was not Cara-owned and violated the intended no-raw-surgery contract. Current fix must make the post-decision path fully first-party, and controller guidance should stop rather than hand-roll when that path is unavailable.

Implementation checkpoint on branch commits 7d73574 + a0f38a7 + c2b6b9e (rebased onto eb77ec7): new CLI/JSON/MCP `repair start/status/continue/abort` surface. Start resolves explicit GitHub provider SSH URL by repository slug and creates an independent exact-head clone under caller Git common Caravan state, so dirty caller, daemon-internal origin, and local PR ref divergence are untouched. Atomic manifest records repository/PR/head/old-base/target/provider/config fingerprint/workspace/conflict paths/baseline index/state/timestamps/prepared or published head. Continue checks config/session/workspace/provider identity, exact merge target, no unresolved/unstaged/untracked/marker state, typed conflict-only index scope, exact parents, unchanged head+target refs; then commits and ordinary non-force pushes the explicit provider URL, verifies ref, and resumes sync-all while holding the caller repository operation lock. Committed/pushed interruption resumes idempotently; explicit confirmed abort deletes only local session state. Focused evidence green: 6 repair tests (dirty+internal origin, scope rejection, committed-before-manifest recovery, moved-head no overwrite, exact parents/non-force publication, confirmed abort no provider mutation), CLI parser, 3 CLI/MCP parity tests, rustfmt on new module, git diff check, strict library Clippy. Full-tree rustfmt is pre-existing red on eb77ec7 outside touched repair code; no unrelated formatting churn included. Awaiting bd-cacf7c orchestration land before final rebase/reintegration; no physical_rebase or checkout_for_decision overlap.

title: Reconcile squash-equivalent pre-squash commits when attaching candidates to a caravan tail
description:
## Live Cacophony reproduction

PR2227 is the tail of caravan `[2215,2223,2225,2227]` at head `94373464efe68fcca5b4010c83b100c33e7469ff`. Main-based PR2245/PR2247 cannot attach because merge-tree reports conflicts in `crates/caco-cli/src/lib.rs` and `crates/caco-daemon/src/canonical_queue.rs`.

The conflict is inherited stack history, not bd-4640a7 source. Tail carries pre-squash commit `79abc31d4e` from PR2208; main carries its squash `1a09ceecef`. At the squash point both relevant blobs are byte-identical, but commit identities differ, so replaying the stacked pre-squash history conflicts against content already on main. Every squash-landed member can recreate this at the next tail.

## Required

- During promotion/rebase/attachment, detect pre-squash commits whose resulting content/tree is already represented on current main.
- Reconcile/drop only with exact cumulative tree/blob proof; commit-message/patch heuristics alone are insufficient.
- Preserve genuinely-new child content and fail closed on semantic difference.
- Emit receipt listing old commit, squash/main proof, affected paths, before/after cumulative tree and dropped/reconciled action.
- Tests for exact blob equality, disjoint later main movement, partial overlap, same patch/different tree, multiple squashes, conflict after equality point, and PR2215→2227 topology.
- Do not rewrite a live provider branch without reviewed owner/hold authority.

Near-term PR2227 disposition is operator-controlled under membership hold; this bead is the durable recurrence fix.

## Correction: PR2227 is not the causal live case

Owner re-measurement proved the initial PR2227 attribution was wrong. Blob equality existed only at ancestor `79abc31d4e` for caco-cli, and canonical_queue equality was vacuous because PR2208 did not touch that file. At current head `94373464ef`, merge base, main tip and PR head are three distinct blobs for both `crates/caco-cli/src/lib.rs` and `crates/caco-daemon/src/canonical_queue.rs`. PR2227's present incompatibility is an ordinary three-way semantic conflict, not safely droppable squash-equivalent history. Never use take-either or automatic commit dropping for this PR.

The general pre-squash duplicate hazard remains valid and needs controlled tests, but PR2227 must not be cited as proof of causality. Keep general structural acceptance separate from specific file-level conflict evidence.

title: Release workflow schedules an aarch64-darwin job no runner can ever accept
description:
Every release since v0.0.11 has required a manual `just release-backfill-target <tag> aarch64-darwin`, nine consecutive times. The cause is not flaky infrastructure.

`.github/workflows/release.yml` pins the darwin leg to `runs-on: [self-hosted, nix, aarch64-darwin]`. Queried live, the repository has seven registered runners and every one of them is Linux X64:

    caravan-ms-dev, ms-dev-2..6, pocket4
    labels: self-hosted,nix,Linux,X64,x86_64-linux,nixos,<host>

No runner advertises `aarch64-darwin`. The job is therefore unschedulable by construction: it queues until the run is cancelled or times out, and the release run never reaches a terminal state. `fail-fast: false` hides it as a hang rather than a failure.

Second, smaller issue: the `aarch64-linux` leg pins `runs-on: [self-hosted, nix, ms-dev-2]`, a single host. When ms-dev-2 is busy (it was, at the time of filing) that leg queues behind unrelated work. It is slow rather than broken, and the pin is deliberate because only ms-dev-2 advertises aarch64 in Nix extra-platforms, so it should stay pinned unless another host gains that capability.

Remedy: stop scheduling a leg that cannot be scheduled. Either register a darwin runner, or drop the matrix entry and make the documented `just release-backfill-target` path the contract, so a release run concludes honestly instead of hanging on a job no machine can accept. A workflow that cannot succeed should not be presented as pending.

title: Support a safely paused Caravan head with auto-merge disabled
description:
## Live need

Cacophony placed a canonical incident hold on Caravan head PR #2008 after a PR-history convergence incident. Immediate containment correctly disabled squash auto-merge while preserving every branch, label, and child base. Cara then reports:

`AutoMergeInvariant: caravan head #2008 must have squash auto-merge enabled`

That invariant is correct for an actively progressing caravan, but Cara has no explicit frozen/maintenance state. The only currently safe response is to leave the caravan globally invalid, which prevents the merger from using Cara for unrelated caravans while the held head awaits CI/operator recovery.

## Acceptance

- Add an explicit idempotent `cara pause` / `cara resume` contract (or equivalent typed frozen state) for one caravan.
- Pausing records bounded non-secret metadata: caravan head, expected head SHA/base, actor/reason, timestamp/expiry, and optional external hold/choice reference.
- Pause disables head auto-merge using exact preconditions but preserves labels, branch topology, children, and all PR heads.
- `status` reports a paused caravan as intentionally frozen, not graph-invalid; `sync --all` skips it without mutating and continues independent caravans.
- `sync` for the paused caravan returns a stable no-op receipt naming the pause and safe next action.
- Resume revalidates exact head/base/labels/check state before re-enabling squash auto-merge; stale facts fail closed.
- Pause cannot hide cyclic/branching topology, closed PRs, changed heads, or unsafe labels. Only the auto-merge invariant is suspended intentionally.
- Add tests for incident hold, CI wait, expiry without silent resume, concurrent status/sync, stale head on resume, independent caravan progression, and idempotent pause/resume retries.
- Document operator recovery and ensure no background loop can auto-resume without an explicit audited action.

- **Self-update metadata** — a deployed `0.0.9` returns
  `{"tag":"v0.0.9","version":"0.0.9","newer_than_current":false}` with all six
  assets listed; `self-update status` reports `next_staged:false`.
- **Offline `provider_mutated=false`** — against Cacophony's exact
  `.caravan/config.yaml` with no network and no token:
  `{"compatible":true,"config_version":1,"min_cara_version":"0.0.0","provider_mutated":false,"reader_version":"0.0.9"}`.

### Live acceptance (read-only, real canonical repository, main `dd88541e17`)

`cara 0.0.9 status`: `healthy=true`, `caravans=[]`, `problems=[]`,
`unqueued=[2117, 2184, 2186, 2188, 2194, 2195, 2196, 2197]`,
`admission.next_candidate=2117`.

`cara check --pr 2195` at the same moment:

- `0.0.8` (deployed): `eligible=false`, `next_action=reject`,
  `candidate is not canonical first admission attempt; fail closed on PR #2117`.
- `0.0.9`: `eligible=true`, `next_action=new`,
  `admission_note=explicit admission intent for PR #2195; automatic priority/FIFO order would have selected PR #2117 first`.

Guards stay fail-closed under `0.0.9` — explicit intent buys evaluation, never
admission: `--pr 2117` → `repair` (dirty merge); `--pr 2196` → `reject`
(`2196...2197=Some(Diverged)`); `--pr 2186` → `reject` (superseded by canonical
open PR #2188); `--pr 2195 --tail-pr 2117` → error `caravan_tail_not_found`.
`admission.next_candidate` is `2117` under both versions, so automatic
new-caravan FIFO selection is untouched.

The remaining step — an actual mutating join — is the queue owner's action after
deployment, not a hand-run provider mutation from this bead.

### Pin audit

No Cacophony production surface pins a Cara version, and that is enforced:
`.caravan/config.yaml` carries the neutral `min_cara_version: "0.0.0"` sentinel,
`scripts/cara-runtime.sh` is system-only with a diagnostic-only version probe,
`cara-sync.yml` runs through that wrapper, and `canonical_queue.rs` treats the
version as informational. `scripts/cara-runtime-version-guard.sh` fails if any
of that regresses. The `caravan` flake input (`dad4327`, pre-`1722445`) is
developer/validation only and deliberately absent from the production runtime
path.

Consequently **no force-reintegration was authorized or performed**: no
immutable generation was found pinning incompatible older Cara semantics. No
requeue, no reorder.

The deployed binary is a Nix user-environment entry built from Caravan's
`packages.<system>.caravan`, so rolling forward means advancing the fleet's
Caravan lock to `db1ca86` and switching the canonical node — not hand-placing a
binary. `cara self-update` correctly refuses to overwrite it.

### Landed in Caravan

- `scripts/release-pin-rows.sh` + `just release-pin-rows <tag>` — derives exact
  downstream pin rows from published assets, re-verifying each published
  `.sha256` and failing closed on a missing platform or tampered checksum.
- `tests/release_contract.sh` — offline fixtures for all three targets, the
  partial-release refusal, and the tampered-checksum refusal.
- `tests/fixtures/config-rolling-sentinel.yaml` — the real downstream
  `min_cara_version: "0.0.0"` shape, now an offline release gate.
- `justfile` — backfill refuses to replace an already-published asset whose
  digest differs, instead of unconditionally `--clobber`ing bytes a downstream
  pin may already reference.
- `docs/release/v0.0.9-rollout.md` — the full receipt, including rollback.

### Rollback

Exact known-good previous pin is `cara 0.0.8`, tag `v0.0.8`, commit
`01513b5e1883ea2057f7b1cac67c005589e68a7d`; its reviewed per-platform digests
are already in `.cacophony/cara-runtime-pins.tsv` and are reproduced in the
rollout doc. Rollback is a system-package downgrade plus the same read-only
proof; no Cacophony source revert is needed beyond removing the appended `0.0.9`
rows. The cost of rolling back is precisely the live behaviour above: explicit
`--pr` admission intent returns to failing closed behind the FIFO front
candidate.

### Not done — blocking closure

Canonical Cacophony still runs system Cara `0.0.8`. The deploy plus its
read-only `caco_materialization` proof (`source=system`, `version=cara 0.0.9`,
`version_probe_rc=0`, `binary`, `min_cara_version=0.0.0`,
`provider_mutated=false`, `config_fingerprint`) and the pin-row append are
tracked by Cacophony `bd-a10775` (P0, open, unclaimed — `caco bd dispatch`
failed at agent spawn, so it needs a controller or operator). Both projects were
broadcast. Do not close this bead until that proof is terminal.

title: Restore exact force intent when physical rewrite publication fails
description:
## Live failure

During Cacophony caravan #2079→#2080, sync removed `caravan-force` from #2080 through `force_invalidate_rewrite` for old head `77199f2` and planned head `79232af`, then physical rewrite publication failed. The provider remained on the old exact head generation, but its external force intent was absent, so a resumable retry could not reach force policy without a new operator label.

## Required behavior

Force invalidation and physical publication must have a deterministic resumable contract. If Cara removes intent before a branch write, and that write proves it did not publish the planned generation, restore the exact old-generation label under a fresh precondition plus durable audit, or reorder/stage authority so no failed publication can strand unchanged-generation intent. Never carry force intent onto a rewritten generation, restore after indeterminate publication, or hide partial provider receipts.

## Acceptance

Hermetic fixtures cover failed-before-push, confirmed no-publication, indeterminate push outcome, successful rewrite, and retry. Exact old-generation intent is preserved/restored only when non-publication is proven; rewritten or indeterminate generations fail closed with bounded actionable evidence.

Discovered while implementing bd-1f3ff4 from live operator evidence relayed by ms-mac-caravan-crvn-dev-msm-2.

Implementation complete at exact generation 29cf0f35233cd410aa65a39eae34af8a18ecac00 over web-controls main 9ac9140. Sync and membership now refetch the failed plan PR after force invalidation/apply error. Only exact observed old_head proves nonpublication and triggers fresh-precondition caravan-force add plus deterministic force_restore_nonpublication audit; observed planned head remains invalidated; any third head or refetch failure is indeterminate and never restores. Restoration add+comment capacity is reserved before physical mutation. Errors retain original apply failure, restoration state, completed steps/provider receipts; partial restoration failure is typed/resumable. Hermetic fixtures cover pre-push/proven nonpublication, published, indeterminate, idempotent retry/dedupe, audit failure partial receipt, and both sync/membership paths. Full 379 all-target tests and strict Clippy green.

title: Add cascading and whole-caravan eviction
description:
Depends on caravan/bd-0dab27 (gate reshape on non-regression rather than perfect fleet health), which is the actual blocker; this bead is the ergonomics layer on top.

Live context 2026-07-27: with a broken Cacophony chain the operator had no first-party way to dismantle it and resorted to manually removing caravan labels and resetting every base to main. That is exactly the raw provider mutation Caravan exists to avoid, and it leaves no receipts, no audit comments, and no eviction records.

Required:
- `cara evict --cascade --pr N`: evict N and every member after it.
- `cara evict --all` (or an explicit dissolve verb) for a whole caravan.

Design point that makes it safe: process TAIL FIRST. Removing the current tail never requires closing a gap, because it has no child, so each removal is individually trivial and the operation is a bounded sequence of tail removals rather than a graph rewrite. With bd-0dab27 in place each step is also provably non-regressive.

Per member preserve every existing guard: exact PR state and head re-read immediately before mutation, add caravan-evicted, remove caravan and caravan-force, disable auto-merge, durable control-label audit comment, and zero-write abort on drift. Retarget each released member to the default branch as it leaves, so no PR is left pointing at an evicted predecessor and every one is independently reviewable and re-admittable.

Emit one receipt per evicted member plus a summary naming the caravan, the ordered members evicted, and the final fleet state. Partial failure must leave a resumable, honestly reported state, never a half-dissolved chain with no record.

title: Bound Cara status discovery on large repositories instead of hanging silently
description:
## Reproduction

Cacophony's native merger uses Cara against `harryaskham/cacophony` (30 open PRs, one three-member caravan, many historical check rows). Installed binary:

- `cara 0.0.1`
- SHA-256 `b4227c043c031f2db9629e050e1b5ff17487bed94099aad8831e572ae2c991fa`
- cwd: Cacophony canonical repository root on Helsinki

`cara status` had previously completed and reported one caravan (`#2008 -> #1985 -> #1983`). It now fails to emit any output or return under two independent bounded calls:

1. `cara status` exceeded 60 seconds.
2. `timeout 30 cara status` was killed at 30 seconds with zero output.

Cacophony itself remained healthy and direct GitHub PR inventory completed. This blocks reliable `cara sync` progression and suppresses the merger's required per-tick visibility.

## Acceptance

- Bound every GitHub discovery subprocess/API request and the complete status operation with explicit documented deadlines.
- On timeout, return a stable structured error naming the exact discovery phase, elapsed/deadline, retryability, and safe next action; never hang silently.
- Avoid unbounded status-check history or N×PR provider requests where one bounded GraphQL/REST query or concurrency-limited batch suffices.
- Emit no partial mutation from `status`; preserve read-only semantics.
- Add a fixture with at least 30 open PRs, multiple checks per PR, one active caravan, and historical merged members.
- Add a slow/hung provider fixture proving deadline enforcement, child-process cleanup, zero leaked locks, and deterministic error output.
- Record discovery timing by phase so future regressions are diagnosable without shell timeouts.
- Verify a healthy large-repository status completes within a documented operator-safe budget.

Filed from Cacophony controller health checks during the first live Cara caravan cutover. Related earlier parser/crash trackers were distinct; search found no existing timeout/performance bead.

## Live Cacophony large-repository acceptance

Core generation landed at `50a8fb7440aa8d2c687041ffcce2e2d2d800550e`; shared-budget child-cap follow-up landed at `14939b7cd404eb3bc1d973c1e7d1303e406e293d`.

Discovery now uses five constant provider commands: one all-open snapshot with current check rollups supplies current PR, active members, and admission candidates; merged history omits `statusCheckRollup`. Compatibility prepares every unique active/default ref through three batched network calls and one batch object verification, then performs only one local merge-tree per report. `status_with_deadline(context, Instant)` lets sync compose one absolute budget, while each child remains capped at normal `command_timeout_secs`.

Fresh release binary, sanitized environment, live read-only Cacophony root (30 PR snapshots, one caravan/seven members): worker cold profile rc=0 wall=24695ms, stdout=108416B, stderr=0; StatusOutput timing deadline=29999ms total=24401ms, discovery=5584ms, compatibility=17436ms, label inventory=1380ms. Controller warm independent profile rc=0 wall=13377ms, stdout=108406B, stderr=0; timing total=13361ms, discovery=4494ms, compatibility=8164ms, labels=702ms. Git worktree stayed clean and HEAD unchanged; no provider mutation occurred.

Timeout evidence names the exact phase and includes total elapsed/deadline, retryability, resumability/safe action, command, and bounded output. Large 30-PR/multi-check/history, constant command count, batched compatibility, absolute deadline/reaping, and 150s-whole/30s-child-cap tests are green; full 148 tests and strict all-target/all-feature clippy passed. Exact proof bundle `bd-e98eff-cacophony-status-proof.tar.gz` SHA-256 `aeb849dffb544a1b83e4c0539673ebb3fae4b926f2ec4da77ca979e65cf18226` is attached.

title: Guarantee forward progress when caravan physical-sync reserve exceeds tick budget
description:
Cara's correct all-or-nothing apply-budget refusal becomes a monotonic deadlock once a live caravan grows larger than `sync.max_duration_secs` can ever process.

Live Cacophony evidence:

```
physical_sync_budget_insufficient
4560000ms required, 3430138ms remaining (38 command slots)
```

Config: `sync.max_duration_secs: 3600`, `command_timeout_secs: 120`, `max_mutations_per_tick: 64`, `max_candidates_per_tick: 8`. Caravan2208 grew from 4 to 7 members while blocked. At seven members, Cara requires 76 minutes against a 60-minute deadline. Because every pass refuses before mutation, no member drains; because nothing drains, accepting more members only increases the required reserve. Scheduled and manual drivers hit the same bound.

The safety refusal is correct—never start an apply that might overrun mid-chain—but the system must preserve bounded forward progress.

Required, in order:

1. Prefer a checkpointed/resumable bounded-prefix apply: plan/verify the complete graph, reserve enough for an exact prefix plus durable checkpoint, apply strictly root-to-descendant, persist completed-prefix receipts before return, and resume idempotently next tick without replaying completed provider mutations.
2. If complete-graph all-or-nothing is architecturally required, compute maximum admissible chain size from the configured deadline before admission and refuse further joins with typed `caravan_budget_capacity_exhausted` evidence while allowing the existing processable prefix to drain.
3. Required/remaining budget must model actual operations, concurrency and already-completed checkpoints rather than a permanently increasing whole-chain worst case.
4. Preserve force-with-lease, exact provider revalidation, no manual reorder/eviction/split, and fail closed on drift/unknown receipts.
5. Status must expose required budget, processable prefix, blocked candidate, configured deadline and safe next action before the cliff, not only after a sync refusal.
6. Add tests for 1..N members around the threshold, interrupted prefix/resume, provider drift, CI/head transitions, independent caravans, candidate admission at capacity and no duplicate mutations.
7. Validate against the seven-member Cacophony caravan2208 without manually reordering its members.

A temporary deadline increase is an operator-owned stopgap only; it moves the cliff and is not completion. Current manual sync loop is paused to avoid burning rate limit on guaranteed no-write passes.

## Ratchet changes geometry when new arrivals form separate caravans

Observed after the budget refusal: `caravans` went from 1 to 2 with no sync driver running. The second caravan is a single member, PR `#2228`, an ordinary new publication that formed its own caravan rather than joining the deadlocked chain.

That matters for how this is fixed. The original recording of this deadlock assumed a single chain growing without bound until `required_ms` exceeds the deadline. If new arrivals instead form separate caravans, the first chain stops growing, which is better, but drain is still zero and the NUMBER of stuck units now increases rather than the size of one unit. Same deadlock, different geometry.

Consequence for acceptance criteria: a fix that only caps or resumes a single chain would not address the multi-caravan accumulation case. Whatever forward-progress mechanism is chosen should make progress across the set of caravans, not merely within one, and should be measured by total units drained rather than by whether any single chain can be applied.

Credit: observed and reasoned by the helsinki profile worker while under an explicit read-only watch, and verified independently by cluster control, which confirmed caravan 2228 has exactly one member and is an ordinary admission rather than a second sync actor.

## Exact mechanism: required_ms is command_slots x command_timeout_secs, a pure worst-case projection

Three measured datapoints from live refusals, contributed by the helsinki profile worker under a read-only watch, establish the formula precisely:

- 7 members, 38 slots: `4560000ms required` vs `3430138ms remaining`, short by 1129862
- 6 members, 32 slots: `3840000ms required` vs `3455426ms remaining`, short by 384574
- 6 members, 33 slots: `3960000ms required` vs `3425694ms remaining`, short by 534306

In every case `required_ms` equals `slots x 120000` exactly, where 120000 is `command_timeout_secs: 120`. So the reserved apply budget assumes EVERY command consumes its full timeout, and is not informed by observed latency at all. That is the root of the deadlock: real commands complete far faster, but the reserve is computed as though none do.

Two consequences that sharpen the fix options recorded above:

- raising `sync.max_duration_secs` is even more clearly a stopgap than stated. At 120s per slot you need `max_duration >= slots x 120s + planning`, so roughly every five additional slots costs another ten minutes of deadline, permanently.
- lowering `command_timeout_secs` has more leverage than the remedy text suggests, because it divides `required_ms` directly. At 100s, the current 33 slots would need 3300000ms and would fit inside the 3425694ms remaining with no other change. That is a genuine same-night unblock, but it trades against real provider and Git latency, so it needs an owner's judgement rather than a guess.
- the durable ask already recorded, reserving budget per unit of work actually attempted, is exactly right, because the entire gap here is worst-case versus actual.

Also confirmed: a drain does NOT reliably relieve the deadlock. Losing the root cut required_ms by roughly 600000 but left it short, and the requirement then rose again from 3840000 to 3960000 as one slot was added. The ratchet keeps climbing across a successful merge.

Planning consumption is real and must be included in any sizing: the 3600000ms deadline had already dropped to ~3425694ms remaining before apply was reserved.

## Fourth datapoint: formula holds, and parallel caravans do NOT compound the deficit

Datapoint 4 from the helsinki read-only watch: `3960000ms required vs 3429503ms remaining, 33 command slots`. 33 x 120000 = 3960000 exactly, a fourth consecutive exact hit, so `required_ms = command_slots x command_timeout_secs` has still not been falsified.

Full trend:

| slots | required | remaining | short by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 38 | 4560000 | 3430138 | 1129862 |
| 32 | 3840000 | 3455426 | 384574 |
| 33 | 3960000 | 3425694 | 534306 |
| 33 | 3960000 | 3429503 | 530497 |

Remaining is stable across passes at roughly 3425000 to 3455000, so planning consistently consumes about 145000 to 175000ms before apply is reserved. The deficit is therefore driven almost entirely by slot count and not by variable planning cost, which is good news for a fix: slots is the only lever that moves.

Important correction to the multi-caravan concern recorded earlier in this bead: on this pass `caravans` went 1 to 2 again while the SELECTED caravan stayed at 33 slots. The new caravan did not add slots to the selected one. Cluster control verified the second caravan is `2232`, a single member, PR `#2232` "fix(android): bound chat memory and OOM classification", an ordinary new publication.

So parallel caravans are NOT compounding the selected-chain deficit, which is consistent with the per-chain-prefix model in `ad14f74` treating independent chains separately. Accumulation shows up as more units rather than a larger selected unit. That materially narrows the fix: forward progress across the set still matters for total drain, but the deadlock itself is a single-chain slot-count problem, not a cross-chain summation problem.

## Second ratchet driver ISOLATED by controlled comparison: base drift, not chain growth

A controlled quiet-interval test isolates a second and previously unrecorded driver of the deadlock. Slot count changes ONLY when `main` moves, and holds exactly steady when `main` is quiet.

Paired series of (main head, slots):

- `b464e1ae5cb`, 38
- (root #2208 merged), 32
- `b464e1ae5cb`, 33
- `b464e1ae5cb`, 33 — main quiet, slots steady
- `9d6278a10f0`, 36 — main MOVED (release v1.2.1575), slots jumped 33 to 36
- `9d6278a10f0`, 36 — main quiet, slots steady

The decisive pass: two samples roughly 35 minutes apart on an unchanged base produced byte-identical projections, 4320000 required with remaining differing by only 438ms. That rules out a time-based or spontaneous ratchet.

Mechanism confirmed: projected apply cost rises with BASE DRIFT. Mechanism disproven: members re-parenting and consuming slots. Cluster control verified per-member state independently and found the chain stacked on each other's branches with only the root targeting `main`, and the root had NOT re-parented, still at head `2e02a53116` last updated 02:25:35Z with `ahead 2, behind 2` against `main` after the 03:30 release cut. So nothing consumed slots by doing work; the planner is pricing rebase work it has not performed and cannot start.

Why this matters for the fix, and it is worse than pure chain growth:

- unrelated `main` traffic increases projected cost while the chain simultaneously grows staler, because nothing applies the rebases. One event does both.
- a quiet `main` is stable but still deadlocked; a busy `main` actively worsens it.
- there is a perverse loop: a queue that cannot drain forces manual lands, manual lands move `main`, and every such move makes the queue more expensive to drain.

Consequence for acceptance criteria: capping chain size is necessary but NOT sufficient. A fix must also ensure projected cost does not grow unboundedly with base drift on a chain that is not being applied, for example by pricing only the prefix it intends to apply this pass, or by applying rebases incrementally so drift is retired rather than accumulated.

Formula confirmation continues: 36 x 120000 = 4320000, a sixth consecutive exact hit, so `ad14f74` has not yet reached the runtime in use (`cara 0.0.10`, consistent with `bd-bbc981` pending).

Credit: isolation designed and executed by the helsinki profile worker under a read-only watch, with per-member base state verified independently by cluster control.

## RETRACTION: the base-drift isolation above is FALSIFIED — do not act on it

The "second ratchet driver isolated" section above is WRONG and must not be used for fix design or deployment verification. Retracted by its own author on the next pass, and verified by cluster control.

Falsifying observation: `main` head was UNCHANGED at `9d6278a10f0` across three consecutive passes, yet slots jumped 36 to 42 on the third, `5040000ms required vs 3376327ms remaining`. Slots moved while `main` was quiet, which is exactly the outcome that was predicted to break the finding. `caravans` also went 2 to 3 active across that interval.

Why the earlier test was underpowered: the two quiet passes with steady slots showed only that slots do not drift spontaneously with TIME on an unchanged base AND unchanged membership. Membership happened to be static across both, so the test never controlled for it. The single 33 to 36 jump coincided with the v1.2.1575 release cut and was attributed to base drift, but membership change is an equally plausible and unexcluded explanation for that same jump.

Corrected position, deliberately weaker than before:

- `required_ms = command_slots x command_timeout_secs` remains solid, now seven consecutive exact hits including 42 x 120000 = 5040000.
- Slot count is NOT stable, and at least two candidate drivers remain plausible: chain or membership growth, now directly evidenced by a quiet-main pass with slots +6 and caravans +1; and base drift, still consistent with the per-member read but NOT established, since its only supporting datapoint is confounded with membership change.
- The deadlock persists across every observed configuration regardless of which driver dominates.

Consequence for the fix: do NOT scope acceptance to "cost must not grow with base drift" as though that were established. The durable requirements already recorded above stand on their own, since they address worst-case reserve versus actual work whatever moves the slot count. Isolating the driver requires holding membership constant, which no observer here can control.

Improvement adopted for future evidence: capture caravan COUNT and selected-chain membership alongside `(main head, slots)` on every pass, so a future jump can be attributed rather than inferred.

Recorded because the falsified version was previously written up here as a controlled comparison and routed onward; anyone who read it should re-read this section.

## Negative result: slot count varies with every sampled field held constant

A same-instant capture recorded slots moving 41 to 42, `required_ms` 4920000 to 5040000, while every other tracked field was unchanged:

- `main` unchanged at `9d6278a10f0`
- caravans unchanged at 3
- cara `merge_candidates` unchanged at 8, identical PR set `[2233,2232,2227,2225,2223,2215,2213,2210]`
- cara compatibility entries unchanged at 14
- daemon `ordered_candidates` unchanged at 5, with its `observed` timestamp genuinely advancing from 05:08:11 to 05:43:05

Combined with the earlier 42 to 41 decrease, every mechanism proposed during this investigation is now excluded for at least one observed transition:

| proposed driver | excluded by |
|---|---|
| base drift | both the 42→41 and 41→42 transitions, main quiet for both |
| membership growth | the 42→41 transition, membership independently confirmed at six |
| caravan count | the 41→42 transition, steady at 3 |
| candidate set/ordering | the 41→42 transition, identical 8-PR set |
| daemon ordered_candidates | the 41→42 transition, steady at 5 across a real refresh |

The honest conclusion is that slot count varies for reasons not visible in any field sampled here. No sixth mechanism is proposed. Note that CI check state is one dimension neither observer sampled, and PR check transitions did occur during this window; that is offered only as an unsampled dimension, NOT as a proposed cause.

Directly actionable consequence for anyone sizing a stopgap: slots have been observed at 33, 36, 41 and 42, with `main` quiet for most of that range. Any `sync.max_duration_secs` or `command_timeout_secs` value sized against a single observed slot count will be wrong within about an hour. A stopgap must carry headroom above the observed range rather than tracking the current reading, and even then it only moves the cliff.

This also reinforces requirement 3 above: a reserve computed from a quantity that moves unpredictably, while assuming every command consumes its full timeout, cannot be made safe by tuning. It has to be replaced by a reserve tied to work actually attempted.

Formula status: twelfth consecutive exact hit, 42 x 120000 = 5040000, so `ad14f74` had still not reached the observed runtime at this point.

## Head-of-line handoff gap REPRODUCED: autonomous root merge twice, autonomous handoff zero times

The deadlock's user-visible signature has now been observed twice in one night with identical shape, which upgrades it from an incident to a reproduced defect.

Occurrence 1: root `#2208` merged natively once green; caravan re-formed as `2210`; the base retarget to `main` and the squash re-arm were then performed BY HAND by the member's owner after `cara sync` refused pre-mutation on the budget reserve.

Occurrence 2: root `#2210` merged natively at 06:03:38 with all checks green and no intervention; `main` advanced to `176fd149d37ecbcf7b7b90652dde277a80abb7ec`; the caravan re-formed as `2213` with five members `[2213, 2215, 2223, 2225, 2227]`. Canonical immediately went degraded with exactly two problems:

```
dangling_base: PR #2213 still targets merged predecessor #2210; sync must advance it to `main`
auto_merge_invariant: caravan head #2213 must have squash auto-merge enabled
```

Verified independently: `#2213` is OPEN and CLEAN with zero failing and zero pending checks, its base is still the agent branch of its predecessor rather than `main`, and it has no auto-merge armed.

What this establishes:

- Automatic ROOT MERGE works and is proven twice. Given an armed root and green required checks, the provider lands it with no operator or sync involvement.
- Automatic CHAIN HANDOFF has never once occurred. Both times, the two repairs that promote the next member to root, base retarget and root arming, were left undone because physical sync refuses before its mutation phase.
- The two failures are therefore not independent. The budget refusal is precisely what prevents the handoff, so every root merge produces a degraded queue that then requires manual repair to continue.

Consequence for acceptance: a canary or proof that only observes "the root merged" is measuring the half that already works. The falsifiable criterion is that after a root merges, the successor is advanced to `main` and armed WITHOUT manual intervention. That has zero successful observations to date.

Deliberately NOT repaired by hand on this occurrence, so the reproduction is preserved as evidence rather than overwritten.

## The deadline is never fully available: a chain sized exactly to max_duration_secs still cannot start

A later observation reduces this from a large structural gap to a marginal one, and in doing so exposes a clean off-by-planning defect in the admission arithmetic.

Measured: 30 slots, `required_ms = 3600000`, `remaining = 3416655`, short by only 183345. Every earlier pass was short by between 384574 and 1557755.

Two arithmetic consequences, both derived purely from observed numbers rather than any proposed mechanism:

1. At 30 slots the projection is EXACTLY 3600000ms, which is exactly the configured `sync.max_duration_secs: 3600`. So a chain sized precisely to the entire deadline still cannot begin, because planning has already consumed roughly 183000ms before the apply reserve is computed. The reserve is checked against REMAINING budget while the admissible chain size is implicitly reasoned about against TOTAL budget. The two are never equal, so the effective capacity is strictly less than the configured deadline and always will be. Any capacity calculation, cap, or stopgap that uses `max_duration_secs` directly is off by the planning cost.
2. At 28 slots the projection would be 3360000ms, which fits inside the observed 3416655ms remaining. So the chain is roughly two slots from being able to mutate unaided, and may simply begin working after another member or two drains, with no config change at all.

Point 1 should be treated as a durable requirement rather than an observation. Whatever replaces the current reserve must either compare like with like, by computing admissible size against budget actually remaining at reserve time, or must reserve planning explicitly so the comparison is honest. Otherwise the boundary condition is permanently unreachable and the system is guaranteed to refuse a chain it was configured to accept.

Point 2 is also a caution for interpreting any future success. If the queue starts moving after further drain, that is NOT evidence that a deployed fix worked. It would be the chain falling below the marginal threshold on its own. Distinguishing the two requires the behavioural check recorded elsewhere in this bead: a `required_ms` that is no longer an exact multiple of `command_timeout_secs`.

Successor criterion at this point, independently verified by cluster control across all five remaining members:

| PR | mergeStateStatus | armed | base |
|---|---|---|---|
| #2213 | CLEAN | false | `agent/ms-dev-3/...8x5t4` (predecessor #2210 MERGED) |
| #2215 | CLEAN | false | `agent/ms-dev-3/...h8e3r` |
| #2223 | CLEAN | false | `agent/ms-dev-6/...d23tq` |
| #2225 | CLEAN | false | `agent/ms-dev-6/...v2dom` |
| #2227 | UNSTABLE | false | `agent/ms-dev-5/...3ru8p` |

Four of five are CLEAN, unarmed, and dangling on a predecessor branch. Nothing advanced any base or armed anything autonomously in roughly the first hour after the root merged. Formula status at this point: fifteenth consecutive exact hit, 30 x 120000 = 3600000.

## RESOLVED IN BEHAVIOUR: the predicted discriminator fired positive on 0.0.11

The falsifiable test specified earlier in this bead has now run and returned the passing result.

Test as specified in advance: on `0.0.10` the reserve was `required_ms = command_slots x command_timeout_secs` exactly, sixteen consecutive exact hits. The agreed discriminator was that a `required_ms` which is NOT a flat multiple of `command_timeout_secs` proves the bounded-prefix work is live, while an exact multiple would mean the binary changed but the reserve logic did not.

Measured by cluster control via read-only `cara status --json` in the canonical daemon checkout, at main `7c0bb4158e13ce20673b3a62699fdfef827406dc`:

```
sync_budget.command_timeout_ms = 600000
sync_budget.deadline_ms        = 3600000
caravan 2215: required_ms = 315000, retained_ms = 240000, processable_prefix = [2215, 2223, 2225, 2227]
caravan 2233: required_ms = 135000, retained_ms = 105000, processable_prefix = [2233]
```

Neither 315000 nor 135000 is a multiple of 600000. Under the old model a four-member chain at a 600000ms command timeout would have reserved several million milliseconds against a 3600000ms deadline and refused before mutation, as it did all night at 120000ms per slot. Instead it reserves 315000ms, under nine percent of the deadline, and publishes an explicit processable prefix covering all four members.

This satisfies the substance of requirements 1, 3 and 5 recorded above: the reserve now models work actually attempted rather than a whole-chain worst case, a processable prefix is exposed in status rather than only after a refusal, and the deadlock condition no longer arises for these chains.

Three caveats deliberately attached:

- The runtime measured is the MUTABLE cargo-installed `0.0.11` at `/home/harry/.cargo/bin/cara`, not the reviewed store closure. This is evidence that the CODE behaves correctly. It is NOT evidence that the reviewed artifact is deployed; that claim belongs to the Cacophony-side deployment bead and remains unproven.
- Config changed underneath the measurement series. `command_timeout_secs` is now 600 on main and canonical while the sixteen-hit baseline was taken at 120, and `sync.max_duration_secs` was briefly 65525 before being corrected to 3600 at commit `7c0bb4158e13`. The discriminator survives this because it is stated as "not a flat multiple of `command_timeout_secs`, whatever that value is", rather than as a literal 120000.
- Admission remains closed: `max_admissible_members = 0` with at-capacity wording, so existing caravans can drain but new members cannot join. Whether that is intended gating or a second independent bound is not established here.

Credit: the discriminator was formulated by the helsinki profile worker from the original `required_ms = slots x command_timeout_secs` derivation, generalised by it to be independent of the literal timeout value, and specified before the fix was observable, which is what makes this a test rather than a post-hoc reading.

## Reopened: admission capacity still uses legacy full-timeout slots

Canonical Cacophony config now has `sync.max_duration_secs=3600`, `command_timeout_secs=600`; Cara0.0.11 proportional reserve defaults to 15 seconds per command. Read-only canonical status proves physical prefixes work: caravan2215 has 21 required slots but `required_ms=315000`, and 16 retained slots give `retained_ms=240000`, both exactly 15s/slot with the full four-member prefix processable.

However `max_admissible_members()` still calls `deadline_command_slots()`, which divides the deadline by the full child timeout: `3600/600=6`. The minimum ordinary chain-capacity shape exceeds six slots, so capacity is projected as zero and every nonempty caravan is `at_capacity`. `blocked_candidate=2234` and `caravan_budget_capacity_exhausted` close joins even though the same status proves the existing chain fits comfortably under the proportional reserve.

This is a mixed-model regression: apply/drain budgeting uses the landed proportional reserve while admission capacity retains the retired worst-case timeout arithmetic. With no caravans, one independent root may still start, but it cannot accept a second member; normal batching collapses to serial one-member caravans.

Required:

- derive `max_admissible_members` from the same proportional reserve/model used by `admit_physical_prefix`, or deterministically simulate the hardest one-pending-member shape through that model;
- retain worst-case timeout only as evidence, never as the admission bound;
- preserve fail-closed zero capacity only when the proportional model truly cannot process one member;
- tests for deadline3600/timeout600/reserve15 expecting positive multi-member capacity and consistency between projected capacity, processable prefix and typed refusal;
- status must not say a full processable prefix is simultaneously over a zero-member bound;
- preserve existing new-independent-caravan and real no-progress safeguards.

Runtime provenance caveat: measurement used mutable cargo Cara0.0.11, not reviewed store deployment, but source inspection independently confirms the mixed formulas in `src/sync/budget.rs`.

title: Stop electing a self-classified unrepairable candidate to the admission front
description:
Investigation 2026-07-27 before implementing: most of this is already covered, and the residual needs an explicit cost decision rather than a mechanical fix.

Already covered:
1. sync greedy auto-admission ALREADY persists caravan-join-skipped when a candidate is mechanically incompatible (persist_auto_skip, sync.rs), carrying an AutoJoinSkipReceipt with candidate head/base, tested tails, compatibility reasons, config fingerprint and heuristic version.
2. read.rs resolve_admission ALREADY moves a caravan-join-skipped candidate into `skipped` and out of the ordered attempt list, so a skipped unrepairable candidate does not hold the front and is re-elected automatically when a fresh generation clears the label.
3. bd-c1799b/bd-7099e8 landed explicit-intent precedence, so an explicit --pr request now proceeds past unrelated unjoined rows regardless. The live PR2117 wedge, where clean candidates behind an unrepairable front were rejected, is therefore already unblocked for explicit admission.

Residual gap: when auto-admission is disabled or the sync tick cannot run, nothing ever persists the skip, so automatic ordering still elects an unrepairable candidate. Closing that properly requires compatibility evidence for UNQUEUED candidates at status time. Today graph::analyze only computes compatibility for caravan heads against the default branch and for member pairs; candidates are checked on demand by check_analysis. Computing merge checks for every unqueued candidate on every status is a real cost increase on a surface that already dominates provider latency, and it should not be added silently.

Options for the operator: (a) accept the current behaviour, since explicit intent already bypasses and sync persists skips whenever it runs; (b) compute candidate-versus-default compatibility for a bounded number of leading candidates only, and exclude proven-conflicting ones with blocks_order=false; (c) compute it for all candidates and accept the cost. Recommend (b) if this recurs, bounded by the existing candidate budget.

Downgraded from P0 to P2 because the live queue-wedge symptom is already fixed by explicit-intent precedence; what remains is an efficiency and honesty improvement in automatic ordering.
